title: Workspace-wide beads remediation: converge 20 repos on server mode, eliminate dolt_data_dir
description: Root cause (verified 2026-09-06): bd init defaults to embedded mode; dolt_mode later flips to server WITHOUT a data-dir pointer; server mode defaults to .beads/dolt which does not exist, so bd creates an EMPTY one and serves it while real data sits in .beads/embeddeddolt. bd dolt status reports healthy throughout. 3 repos are in this state now and show zero issues. Cross-repo blast radius is agents running 'pkill -f dolt sql-server' (kills every repo's server), NOT a shared daemon. dolt_data_dir has no valid value on 1.2.2 (absolute silently erased by configfile.Save(); relative does not resolve) so it must be REMOVED, not reformatted. Worktree hypothesis was REFUTED (bd resolves worktrees natively; upstream GH#3027 fixed). Full findings: workspace/BEADS.md. Decision record: catalyst-operator ADR-0014.
design: Global knob ~/.config/bd/config.yaml dolt.mode=server makes every future bd init correct with zero flags (verified under isolated HOME). Server over bd's embedded default because embedded is single-writer and this workspace runs CLI+MCP+subagents concurrently. Do NOT adopt dolt.shared-server (broken on 1.2.2). Per-repo migration: bd backup sync -> bd dolt stop -> cp -Rf embeddeddolt/<db> dolt/<db> -> remove dolt_data_dir -> bd doctor -> archive by mv.
acceptance_criteria: Every repo: bd doctor 0 errors, bd stats returns the expected issue count, no dolt_data_dir key anywhere, data in the dir its mode implies. Future bd init needs no flags.

title: [epic] 2026-09-06 full-audit burn-down: 2 critical + 5 high + 2 med (filed) + 79 med/low (verify-first)
description:
Mega-epic tracking remediation of the 2026-09-06 full-codebase audit (13 Fable auditors + adversarial verification; 92 findings).

FILED CHILDREN (verified, fix directly):
- boom-qs80 P0 restore TRUNCATE CASCADE data loss + argon_version/role omissions
- boom-inih P0 plaintext Wakatime keys in import_jobs.value + backups
- boom-haz1 P1 OIDC logout revokes API tokens

- boom-o6q5 P1 Kindle sync resets derived status, re-clobbers overrides
- boom-1vwl P1 RecoverInterrupted fails all import jobs fleet-wide on pod boot

RULE for the 79 med/low: they were NOT adversarially verified. Each must be VERIFIED against current code first — trace the failure scenario end-to-end; if it cannot be driven, REJECT it with reasoning rather than 'fixing' a non-bug. Rejection with evidence closes the finding as legitimately as a fix.

Execution: Opus fix agents partitioned by file ownership (disjoint sets, migrations pre-numbered), centrally validated (build, full suite, ratchets, wire-format), committed and CI-watched from the main session.

Missing test written and mutation-verified (list_clear_regression_test.go), committed. QA also caught a broken-bisect defect in the commit split: commits referencing worker.ServerAPIKey preceded the commit adding it; reordered so all 13 commits build individually (verified in a scratch worktree). Rejections spot-checked: legitimate. Both identity-auth test edits: LEGITIMATE (separate avatar pin exists; argon timing assertions literally unchanged). LoadSpace cross-tenant read closed once, not twice, pinned by 4 DB-backed specs. No secrets leaked in any partition. title: AUDIT-CRITICAL: plaintext Wakatime API keys persisted in import_jobs.value and included in downloadable backups
description:
From the 2026-09-06 full audit; CONFIRMED by two independent auditors (importer + admin partitions) and the adversarial verifier.

internal/boomtime/importer/importer.go:50 + internal/boomtime/admin/import.go:103 — the resolved plaintext Wakatime key (typed key, DECRYPTED saved key, or the server-wide BOOM_WAKATIME_API_KEY) is JSON-marshalled into importer.QueueItem and INSERTed into import_jobs.value, where it lives forever. import_jobs is in dumpTables (dump.go:93), so the plaintext key ships in every user-downloadable whole-DB backup.

This defeats the entire boom-6jm encryption-at-rest design: the same key that is carefully AES-256-GCM encrypted in users.encrypted_wakatime_key sits in cleartext one table over. CLAUDE.md's own rule — never log or return the plaintext of an encrypted secret — is violated by persistence instead.

REMEDIATION, in order:
1. Stop writing the key into the payload: pass a sentinel (e.g. use-saved-key) and resolve it inside the worker at run time from the encrypted column / env.
2. Migration to scrub existing import_jobs.value rows (NULL the api_key field in the jsonb) — historical rows hold real keys.
3. Decide whether import_jobs.value belongs in the backup at all (queue payloads are operational, not user data).
4. Operators who exported backups while any import job existed should consider those keys exposed and rotate them on wakatime.com.

Do not paste key values into logs/issues while fixing.

title: AUDIT-CRITICAL: DB restore TRUNCATE CASCADE destroys every FK-linked table not in the dump — reading_items, health, goals, avatars, ~20 tables
description:
From the 2026-09-06 full audit; CONFIRMED by adversarial verifier AND validated by hand against the live schema.

internal/shared/db/dump.go:366 — RestoreAll runs TRUNCATE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE over dumpTables. dumpTables (dump.go:56-99) stopped growing at the pre-books core schema (~13 tables), but migrations 00032-00083 added ~25 tables that REFERENCE users(username) or heartbeats(id). Postgres TRUNCATE CASCADE truncates every referencing table; the restore loop only COPYs the listed ones.

VERIFIED against the live database: 20 FK-linked tables are absent from the dump, including reading_items, reading_activity, book_liberation_attempts, book_sync_state, kindle_* (4 tables), hardcover_user_shelf, health_samples, workout_details, goals, dashboard_layouts, user_avatars, award_ledger, github_stats_cache, oidc_sessions, user_external_identities, widget_defs, widget_links.

FAILURE: operator uses Save DB then Load DB with that archive → the entire book library + liberation state + health + goals + layouts are silently and permanently destroyed inside the committed restore transaction. The export that claims to be a whole-DB backup is not one.

RELATED (same fix, fold in): dump omits users.argon_version → restored rows default to 1, Argon2id v2 hashes verify with v1 params, every post-awh.6 user is locked out after restore (dump.go:67, HIGH CONFIRMED). Also omits role/capabilities/disabled_at/timezone → restore silently re-enables disabled accounts and drops admin roles (MEDIUM).

FIX SHAPE: derive dump tables/columns from the live schema or a registry (extend domaincols to whole tables); add a CI test asserting every user-data table is dumped or explicitly exempted; refuse to restore when TRUNCATE CASCADE would reach a table absent from the archive. Until fixed, treat the Load DB button as destructive beyond its labeling.

title: Live verification: exercise the protocol against the real account + capture fixtures
description: Run the NEEDS-LIVE-VERIFY checklist from design doc section 2 by hand, ONCE, against the real Amazon account, and commit the resulting fixtures so the unit tests stop being guesses. Items: (1) POST canonical string - does Amazon accept Sign() with a non-empty body element, signed over the exact posted bytes; (2) voucher concat ORDER - device_type+device_serial+customer_id+asin; a wrong order yields a clean AES decrypt of GARBAGE, which is a confusing failure mode, so permute before assuming the endpoint changed; (3) trailing-bytes handling on the decrypted voucher (null-strip vs trim-to-last-brace); (4) whether offline_url needs the ADP headers or is self-authorizing; (5) what content_format real library titles actually report (drives the epic D trigger). This bead gates the epic - do it EARLY, before building on top of assumptions.
notes: HARNESS BUILT + WIRED (2026-08-24). liberate/probe.go runs 6 probes with pass/warn/fail verdicts, mounted on the EXISTING admin diagnostics endpoint as source=liberation (?asin= optional; picks the first library title when omitted) and rendered by the existing ProbeView in BooksTab.tsx — a third button next to Audible/Kindle, no new page. Probe 2 sweeps AllKeyOrders and NAMES the winning voucher derivation, which is the trap this bead exists for (a wrong key decrypts cleanly to garbage). Redaction: redactLicenseBody strips license_response + voucher and reduces offline_url to scheme+host, failing closed on parse trouble. REMAINING = the actual live RUN, which needs DJ's real Amazon account against a running instance: Admin > Books > Source diagnostics > Liberation > Run diagnostics. Then commit the captured voucher fixture into voucher_test.go to make the unit test real rather than synthetic.
close_reason: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-24 against the real account (B09GCYRZRQ, marketplace us). RESULTS: (1) signed-POST canonical string CORRECT first try — 200/Granted, no change to Sign(); (2) voucher derivation = device_type+device_serial+customer_id+asin, i.e. OrderCanonical, exactly what DecryptVoucher uses — no change to keyMaterial; (3) CDN offline_url is NOT self-authorizing, 403 without ADP headers — fetch.go MUST sign the download (design doc 2.3 had understated this as 'harmless if ignored'); (4) content_format=AAX_44_128 (AAC-LC) — the ffmpeg-first decision holds, epic D stays data-triggered; (5) chapter_titles_type Tree returned a FLAT 37-chapter list with brand intro/outro 3924/4945ms — chapters.go must not assume nesting depth. FIXED as a result: offlineURLProbe now does a bare pass then an ADP-signed pass and reports Accept-Ranges/Content-Range, because the 403 meant the first run never learned whether the CDN honours Range (the epic-B resumability question). DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: committing a real voucher fixture. A real license_response plus the four derivation inputs IS a decryption secret for a real book; the synthetic round-trip already pins the order (independent derivation, mutation-verified) and the probe confirms it against reality. Recorded in design doc 2.6.

title: Reconcile worktree-agent-a7d0ed5068bf868b7 (dashboard-edit Phase 5/6 + Labs tab) onto main across the web/src -> web/shared split
description:
Branch `worktree-agent-a7d0ed5068bf868b7` holds 4 commits of dashboard-edit work
that is NOT on main and CANNOT be merged as-is: it targets `web/src/**`, a tree
that no longer exists. The domain split (gaka-zp2s) moved it to `web/shared/**`
+ `internal/*/web/src/**`. A plain merge would recreate a phantom `web/src/`
that nothing builds, lints, or tests, and would silently fork dashboard-edit.

Verified 2026-08-22: `git cherry main worktree-agent-a7d0ed5068bf868b7` = 4
unapplied, and none of LabsTab / LabsFlags / useDashboardLayoutPersistence /
rangeOverride / gridTheme exist anywhere on main. This is real, unshipped work.

## The 4 commits (oldest first)

  2f7f7bb feat(settings): Labs tab + shared flag-toggle component (gaka-lzr)
  641f15c style(overview): theme grid-tile CSS vars from catalyst-ui tokens
  e25f4e3 feat(dashboard-edit): per-user dashboard-layout persistence hook (Phase 6)
  9c0155b feat(dashboard-edit): generic per-tile CONFIGURE panel + wire Phase 6
          persistence (Phase 5)

20 files, +1091/-103.

## Path mapping

Every path maps 1:1 — `web/src/X` -> `web/shared/X`. Confirmed for all 8
modified (non-new) files. New files follow the same rule.

## Two files need REWORK, not a path rewrite

Both changed materially in b8291ae (the admin/settings shell TLC), so a
mechanical rebase will conflict — and for one of them the branch's approach is
now the wrong shape entirely:

1. `web/shared/features/settings/Settings.tsx`
   The branch adds ~6 lines wiring a Labs tab directly into the page. Settings
   no longer owns its tab list: tabs are pushed in via `registerSettingsSection`
   from a domain's register module, and the page is a thin consumer of that seam
   rendering through <SectionPage>. PORT AS A REGISTRATION, not a page edit —
   add the Labs tab to the Account section in `web/shared/domains/core/register.tsx`,
   carrying the new `icon` / `description` / `width` metadata. Do NOT
   reintroduce a hardcoded tab in the page body.

2. `web/shared/layout/Page.tsx`
   The branch adds a 6-line gridTheme import/hook. Page.tsx gained a `Page.Nav`
   left-rail slot in b8291ae. Small, but re-apply by hand on the current file.

The other 18 files had no overlap and should port with a path rewrite.

## Acceptance

- 4 commits' content lands under `web/shared/**`; no `web/src/` directory is
  created anywhere in the repo.
- Labs tab reaches Settings via registerSettingsSection, visible in the rail.
- `tsc -b --noEmit --force` clean; `eslint .` no NEW errors (3 pre-existing);
  full vitest suite green (783 at time of writing, +the branch's own specs:
  LabsFlags.test, LabsTab.test, useDashboardEditStore.test,
  useDashboardLayoutPersistence.test).
- Branch deleted and its worktree removed once landed.

## Do not lose this

The branch is the ONLY copy. It is not pushed to origin — `git branch -r` shows
only main, chore/standardize-renovate, and __dolt_remote_info__. If the local
clone is wiped before this is reconciled, the work is gone. Consider pushing the
branch to origin as a backup before starting.
close_reason:
Reconciled and landed on main as 338fc4b (fast-forward, preserving the original agent's 4 commits).

Git followed the renames for most files; 10 conflict hunks across 6 files needed hand resolution, plus 8 files git had already relocated correctly and one modify/delete.

TWO THINGS A MECHANICAL PORT WOULD HAVE GOTTEN WRONG, which is what made this worth doing carefully rather than rewriting paths:

1. Settings.tsx no longer holds a literal tabs array — it is a thin consumer of the settings registry now, with tabs registered by each domain module. The branch's { id: 'labs', ... } entry had nowhere to go. Labs is registered via registerSettingsSection in domains/core/register.tsx instead, carrying the icon/description the section shell renders on its behalf. Porting the entry literally would have compiled cleanly and done nothing.

2. My first attempt imported LabsTab eagerly there and broke 5 tests in betaRegistration.test.ts — a file the merge does not touch. register.tsx documents precisely why: registration must stay side-effect free because the test setup registers every domain up front, so an eager import pulls its chain into the pre-test module graph and defeats per-file vi.mock isolation. The real usePublicConfig ran instead of the mock. Fixed by using lazy() like every other tab body.

I found (2) only because I checked the failure against a clean main worktree instead of assuming 'the merge does not touch that file, so it must be pre-existing' — which was my first instinct and was wrong.

Also folded in the two renames the branch predates: @/ -> @shared aliases and gaka- -> boom- issue prefixes. Dropped a StorageAdapter import left dead by the merge.

VALIDATION: typecheck clean; 801 tests pass across 104 files including the 24 ported ones; production build succeeds; lint byte-identical to clean main (21 problems / 3 errors, all pre-existing in files this does not touch).

title: Fix: SaveHealthSamples ON CONFLICT targeted wrong constraint kind (caught by gaka-se2.8)
description:
Fixed in commit a677586 as part of gaka-se2.8 test writing.

## Symptom
Every POST to /api/v1/users/current/health_samples (Apple Watch companion sync) silently 500ed at the DB layer. `idx_health_samples_dedupe` is a UNIQUE INDEX in the schema (00001_initial_baseline.sql:539), but the ON CONFLICT clause in SaveHealthSamples referenced it as ON CONSTRAINT — Postgres rejects that with SQLSTATE 42704 at batch prepare.

## Fix
Changed clause from `ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT idx_health_samples_dedupe DO NOTHING` to `ON CONFLICT (owner, kind, ts_start, COALESCE(ts_end, ts_start)) DO NOTHING` — targeting the index by columns instead of by name. Same semantic dedup key.

## Detection
This was not caught by any existing test (health.go was at 0% coverage). Bead gaka-se2.8's idempotency test (\"insert same 5 samples 3x → still 5 rows\") was the first path to exercise the ON CONFLICT clause under a real Postgres, which surfaced the SQLSTATE 42704 error immediately.

## Regression backstop
The 40 tests written in gaka-se2.8 now pin the correct behavior. Any future refactor that reverts to ON CONSTRAINT (or drops the dedup entirely) will fail the idempotency test.

## Blast radius
- Apple Watch companion sync silently non-functional since the constraint syntax was introduced
- Backup/restore of health_samples rows unaffected (dump copies raw, doesn't INSERT via this path)
- Workouts unaffected (SaveWorkouts uses a different insert path)
- No data loss risk — inserts just failed loudly at the DB, no partial state

## Followup
Consider a git blame + timestamp analysis to determine how long this has been broken. If the ON CONSTRAINT variant was there from day 1, health samples never worked in prod. If a recent refactor introduced it, we know when the regression started.
close_reason: Fix already landed in a677586 alongside gaka-se2.8 tests. Filed for audit-trail; if you want the fix tracked separately from the test PR, cherry-pick a677586's health.go change into its own commit.

title: Bravo CRITICAL: CORS reflects any Origin with credentials on /auth/*
description: internal/server/server.go:32-42 sets `UnsafeAllowOriginFunc` to unconditionally return (origin, true) with AllowCredentials=true. Any evil.example.com page can issue credentialed POST /auth/login (or refresh_token) against a self-hosted boomtime instance and read the response body, including the fresh access token in JSON. The refresh_token cookie itself is SameSite=Strict so the browser will not attach it to cross-site requests — but the login response body is directly readable, so an attacker who tricks the victim into visiting evil.example.com while running boomtime on localhost can silently phish or replay credentials. PoC: `curl -X OPTIONS http://localhost:8080/auth/login -H "Origin: https://evil.example.com" -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST"` returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example.com` + `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. Fix: replace UnsafeAllowOriginFunc with an allowlist derived from cfg (BOOM_ALLOWED_ORIGINS), or set AllowCredentials=false for cross-origin.
close_reason: Closed

title: QA red-run: verify the boom-l827 burn-down now that it is actually in prod
description:
The boom-l827 burn-down sat UNPUSHED from 09-06 until 2026-09-08, when it went to
prod as 19 commits riding along with the annotations push. ~45 fixes across auth,
secrets, backup/restore, jobs, stats, books sync and the web UI, live for the
first time. One of its own commits says "NOT mutation-verified yet — pending QA
red-run", so this is that red-run.

Prod is healthy (pod 0 restarts, migrations v87), so nothing is on fire. Ordered
by consequence, not by likelihood.

1. BACKUP / RESTORE — do this one properly; it fails INVISIBLY (72b5d61f)
   RestoreAll was cascading away ~20 FK-linked tables, and the users dump omitted
   argon_version, timezone, role, capabilities, disabled_at.
   [ ] export a backup, restore into a scratch instance, then LOG IN. A wrong
       argon_version verifies every password with the wrong Argon2 params and
       locks everyone out.
   [ ] confirm disabled accounts stay disabled and roles/capabilities survive.
   [ ] confirm reading_items / health / goals / avatars are still populated after
       a restore (that is the ~20-table cascade, boom-qs80).

2. AUTH — plugin tokens surviving logout (b321a59f)
   [ ] log in, log out, confirm the editor plugin STILL ingests heartbeats.
       Logout used to revoke all auth_tokens including never-expiring API tokens.
   [ ] a profile with public_profile_enabled OFF should not serve its avatar.

3. BOOKS SYNC not clobbering curation (17f48d8b) — the explicitly un-QA'd one
   [ ] set a status + rating by hand on a book, run a sync, confirm neither
       reverts (Kindle sync used to reset the derived layer to want/false).
   [ ] edit a book on Hardcover, pull, confirm the edit is ADOPTED — LWW echo
       suppression was value-based and permanent, so genuine remote edits were
       being swallowed then reversed.

4. IMPORT + SECRETS (ff3880cd)
   [ ] run an import end to end; confirm it completes.
   [ ] download a backup and grep for your Wakatime key — plaintext keys were
       being marshalled into import_jobs.value and shipped in the backup.
   [ ] queue a job, restart the pod, confirm it SURVIVES. RecoverInterrupted used
       to fail every queued/running job fleet-wide on each boot.

5. RATE LIMITING (e068e487)
   [ ] watch for unexpected 429s (or their absence). An echo IPExtractor was
       added; before it, c.RealIP() returned the ingress address in k8s so every
       external client shared one bucket.

6. Lower risk, eyeball only: stats commit attribution + scoping (38b79915),
   goals/curation/widget defects (83f3b43f), books HTTP surface (463fce0d),
   liberation pipeline (330db376), shared FE request/render (50d83b44), books UI
   + e2e (d48ab560).

NOTE the annotations feature deployed the same day is NOT part of this: it is
behind BOOM_FEATURE_BOOKS_ANNOTATIONS, unset in prod, so only its schema
(migrations 00086/00087) is live. Nothing to QA there until the flag is flipped.

title: Test the annotations query domain + add a generic domain-coherence test
description:
The `annotations` query domain (internal/shared/query/domains.go registerAnnotations)
ships untested, and there is NO generic "every registered domain is coherent" test
in that package — so a wrong column name in the domain or the enriched view would
not surface until someone actually ran the query.

Verified by hand during the local run (captures grouped by kind returned
highlight 2 / note 1 / clip 1 / bookmark 1), but nothing pins it.

Two pieces of work, and the second is the more valuable:

1. Test THIS domain: measure `captures` counts, group by kind and by source, and
   — the important one — that a TIME-BOUNDED query excludes annotations whose
   captured_at is NULL. Kindle highlights have no capture time, and the whole
   design rests on them being in the corpus but never in a time bucket. A
   regression there would silently invent reading activity.

2. Add a generic coherence test over query.Register'd domains: for each domain,
   compile a trivial query per measure and per dimension and assert it does not
   error. That would have caught a bad column in ANY domain, not just this one,
   and is the reason this gap existed at all.

See docs/design/change-detection-patterns.md §3 for why timeless events must not
project into the activity stream.

title: Test the annotations read endpoint (no coverage at any layer)
description:
GET /api/v1/books/items/:externalId/annotations ships with NO test at any layer —
not in internal/books/api/, not in web/e2e/. It was verified by hand with curl
during the local end-to-end run and never pinned.

What the handler does that a test should hold it to
(internal/books/api/books_annotations.go):
- orders annotations by position (reading order within the book)
- returns a per-kind `counts` map alongside the list
- ?source= narrows to kindle|audible; absent returns both
- an unknown ?source= is a 400; a missing :externalId is a 400
- capturedAt is OMITTED when the source reports no capture time — this is the
  one that matters most, because it is the wire-level end of the TimeUnknown
  rule. A regression here silently dates every Kindle highlight.
- body / note / transcript / transcriptSource are distinct fields; a test should
  fail if transcript ever merges into body.
- slices initialise to []T{} so JSON is never null.

Follow internal/books/api's existing handler-test pattern (doJSONReqG +
testutil.Harness + MintUser). Seed rows with db.UpsertBookAnnotation rather than
raw SQL so the accessor contract is exercised too.

Route is gated on cfg.AnnotationsEnabled(), so the harness config must set
FeatureBooks + FeatureBooksAnnotations or every request 404s.

title: Annotations MVP (phase 1, Kindle): persist highlights/notes, expose via API/UI/query domain
description:
Persist the annotation corpus boom-siwi.1 proved reachable, and surface it.

Approved plan: ~/.claude/plans/cheerful-sleeping-muffin.md

Scope: schema (both migration trees) + typed parsers + a cross-source ingest package +
two job kinds + pipeline stages + a query-DSL domain + GET route + Books UI panel.
NOT in scope: the ffmpeg cut + whisper transcription (boom-siwi.3) — this leaves typed
transcript columns for it.

title: Spike: probe whether our Kindle device credential can read highlights + Audible clips DIRECTLY (bypass Readwise)
description:
GATING SPIKE. Do not build any highlight ingest until this returns a verdict.

Hypothesis: we do not need Readwise as a SOURCE. We hold an ADP-signed Amazon device
credential (internal/books/connect/amazon/signing.go) that already authenticates the same
hosts Readwise's own Kindle sync reads. If the annotation records are reachable off that
credential, boomtime becomes the upstream and Readwise/Notion demote to publish targets.

Concrete surfaces to probe (all with the existing device cred, no new auth):

KINDLE
- whispersync dataset list: GET api.amazon.com /whispersync/v2/data/<customer_id>/datasets.
  internal/books/connect/amazon/kindle.go:47 explicitly says "Other namespaces (device sync
  state, ANNOTATIONS) are ignored." That comment is the lead — enumerate every namespace the
  live account returns and dump the record types under each, not just CloudCollections.
- Fiona CDE sidecar: GET /FionaCDEServiceEngine/sidecar?type=EBOK&key=<ASIN>. sidecar.go
  parses only payload.records[] of type "kindle.lpr" and drops the rest. Log the FULL record
  type census for a book known to have highlights — kindle.highlight / kindle.note /
  kindle.bookmark are the types to look for.
- read.amazon.com/notebook — the Cloud Reader highlights page. readamazon.go already does
  cookie-authed Cloud-Reader calls, so the session plumbing exists. HTML, paginated by a
  token; last-resort path if the signed APIs come back empty.

AUDIBLE
- Fiona CDE sidecar with type=AUDI: same host, key=<ASIN>. This is where Audible stores
  clips, bookmarks and notes. A clip is a timestamp range, not text.
- /1.0/annotations/lastpositions (already known-good for position) — check whether the same
  annotations namespace exposes a clips/bookmarks collection.

METHOD
Follow the existing diagnostics harness (internal/books/admin/diagnostics.go runProbe) so the
probe is observational, read-only, and visible in the admin UI like the whispersync probe.
Use one ASIN that definitely HAS highlights and one that definitely does not, so an empty
result is distinguishable from a broken call — the Fiona "empty red herring" already burned
us once (see the Amazon/Kindle API map).

DELIVERABLE
A written verdict in docs/design/ recording, per surface: HTTP status, whether records came
back, the record-type census, and the field shape of any annotation record. Then set the
epic's direction: direct-from-Amazon (children .3/.4 proceed, .2 becomes optional) or
Readwise-as-source (child .2 becomes required).
notes:
Probe BUILT and unit-tested; live run still pending prod-credential access.

Code (uncommitted, on main):
- internal/books/connect/amazon/annotations.go — RunAnnotationProbes: whispersync
  namespace census (all namespaces, not just CloudCollections), Fiona CDE sidecar
  record-type census for type=EBOK and type=AUDI with the kindle.lpr filter REMOVED,
  Audible /1.0/annotations/lastpositions, and read.amazon.com/notebook over exchanged
  website cookies. All GETs; nothing writes. Bodies captured only under KeepBodies.
- internal/books/annotations_probe_cmd.go — 'boomtime books probe-annotations --user X
  --auto [--ebook-asin ...] [--dump f.json]'. Auto-picks a most-read title + a 0%
  negative control from reading_items so an empty result is attributable.
- internal/books/admin/diagnostics.go — ?source=annotations renders through the existing
  admin probe panel; census rides in Body (counts + field KEY NAMES only, never content).
- annotations_test.go — parser tests; the census test was mutation-verified by restoring
  the kindle.lpr filter (went red: map[kindle.lpr:1] vs expected 3 types).

BLOCKED ON: the only live device credential is in the prod DB. Reading the k8s secrets
(boomtime-postgres-app, boomtime-encryption-key) and in-pod psql are both denied by the
session permission classifier. Port-forward svc/boomtime-postgres-rw -> 127.0.0.1:55433
IS up. Operator must run the probe themselves; command handed off in-session.

VERDICT: PASS — the device credential reaches the annotation layer; Readwise is not needed as a source.

Audible clips: Fiona sidecar type=AUDI returns audible.clip{annotationId, startPosition, endPosition, metadata, creationTime, lastModificationTime}, audible.bookmark, audible.last_heard. Amazon serves OFFSETS ONLY, never clip audio — the audio must be cut from our own liberated M4B.
Kindle highlights: NOT in the EBOK sidecar (kindle.lpr only) and NOT in whispersync (the non-shelf namespaces are Apps:Device:Settings + LearningDecks/Vocabulary Builder, all empty). Customer id is redacted from printed endpoints — this repo is public.

title: [epic] Highlights & clips layer: own the annotation corpus (probe Amazon direct vs Readwise vs Notion)
description:
Boomtime's books domain currently fuses *what you read* (Kindle/Audible library, position,
finish dates) and pushes it to Hardcover as the terminal sink. It has NO annotation layer:
highlights, notes, and Audible clips are entirely absent from the fusion engine.

Readwise is the obvious off-the-shelf source for that layer (v2 API: /api/v2/books,
/api/v2/highlights). But we are already a REGISTERED KINDLE DEVICE — the ADP-signed device
credential in internal/books/connect/amazon already reaches whispersync datasets, the Fiona
CDE sidecar, and the Audible library/annotations hosts. Readwise itself gets its Kindle
highlights by scraping the same Amazon surfaces we already authenticate against. So the
first question is not "how do we integrate Readwise" but "do we need Readwise at all".

This epic answers that, in order:

1. PROBE first (child .1) — can our own device credential read Kindle highlights and
   Audible clips/bookmarks directly? That verdict gates everything else. Same discipline
   as boom-bfhw (Kindle liberation: run the probe FIRST).
2. Readwise v2 ingest (child .2) — the fallback / complement. Cheap, known-good, and worth
   having even if the direct path works (it carries highlights from sources we do not own:
   web articles, other e-readers, manual entry).
3. Audible clips → audio → transcript (child .3) — the genuinely novel bit. We already
   liberate the M4B and already parse Audible chapter offsets (internal/books/liberate/
   chapters.go). A clip is a timestamp range. Slice it, transcribe it, and an audiobook
   "highlight" becomes text like every Kindle highlight — searchable, fusable, pushable.
4. Sink decision (child .4) — once we OWN the highlight corpus, where does it publish?
   Readwise (review/spaced-repetition loop), Notion (page-per-book knowledge base), or
   native boomtime only. Note the asymmetry: Readwise is both a source and a sink; Notion
   is a sink only. If child .1 succeeds we become the upstream, and pushing INTO Readwise
   or Notion is a publish decision, not an integration dependency.

Data model note: highlights are a new entity class. They hang off reading_items (ASIN or
Hardcover match) but are many-per-item with their own text/location/timestamp/note. Expect
a new table + migration in BOTH trees (internal/shared/db/migrations for the host FK-to-users
shape, internal/books/db/migrations for the standalone owner-column shape).
notes:

An audit of the session's own work found one real defect, now fixed and pushed

The audit's remaining findings are tasked out as .8 through .12:

None are urgent — all sit in flag-off code that is not executing in prod.

title: AUDIT-HIGH: RecoverInterrupted runs on EVERY pod boot and fails ALL queued/running import_jobs fleet-wide
description: 2026-09-06 audit, CONFIRMED. cmd/boomtime/main.go:291 — worker.RecoverInterrupted runs unconditionally at startup on every role, including KEDA drain pods, and MarkRunningJobsFailed (internal/shared/db/importjobs.go:184) has no pod/heartbeat scoping: it fails ALL queued/running import_jobs in the fleet. Every KEDA scale-up kills any import in progress on another pod. The catalyst-go-jobs system solved exactly this with heartbeat+reaper (90ba995); the legacy import_jobs recovery predates it and needs either the same heartbeat scoping or to only run on the server role with a staleness threshold.

title: AUDIT-HIGH: useLiberationAvailable treats the SPA fallback page as feature-enabled — third instance of this trap; fix request() systemically
description:
2026-09-06 audit, CONFIRMED + hand-verified. internal/books/web/src/features/books/LiberationPanel.tsx:61 — available = !q.isError && !!q.data, but with liberation OFF the status GET hits the SPA catch-all: 200 text/html. web/shared/lib/api.ts request() (line ~198) falls back to data=text when JSON.parse fails, so q.data is a truthy HTML string → liberation UI renders on every liberation-off install, with undefined fields downstream.

THIRD INSTANCE of this exact trap (the prod 405 incident; the e2e probe I fixed in-flight; now the FE hook). Fix it SYSTEMICALLY, not per-hook: request() should treat a non-JSON content-type on a 2xx as an error (the API never legitimately returns HTML), which fixes every current and future caller at once. Then useLiberationAvailable needs no change beyond maybe distinguishing 404.

title: AUDIT-HIGH: every Kindle sync resets derived status to want/false, re-arming finish-promotion to clobber user overrides
description: 2026-09-06 audit, CONFIRMED. internal/books/ingest/kindle/ingest.go:142 — Cloud Reader reports percentageRead=0 for all books, and each library sync writes that through the derived status/finished layer ('want'/false). That re-arms the transition-only finish promotion, so each insights run re-promotes and re-clobbers explicit user status overrides. The derived layer must not regress on a source that structurally reports zero progress; treat percentageRead=0 from kindle library sync as 'no information', not 'not started'.

title: AUDIT-HIGH: OIDC logout revokes ALL auth_tokens including never-expiring API tokens
description: 2026-09-06 audit, CONFIRMED. internal/identity/auth.go:330 — OIDC logout calls DeleteUserAccessTokens with no token_expiry IS NOT NULL guard, so a user logging out of a browser session also revokes every long-lived API token they minted — their wakatime plugin ingest token dies with the browser session. Symptom presents later as silent ingest stoppage (the plugin just starts getting 401s). Fix: scope the logout deletion to session tokens (token_expiry IS NOT NULL) and add a regression test asserting API tokens survive logout.

title: AUDIT-HIGH: Hardcover LWW echo-suppression is value-based and permanent — genuine remote edits suppressed, then reversed by outbound push
description: 2026-09-06 audit, CONFIRMED. internal/shared/db/reading_items.go:833 — echo suppression compares remote status == hardcover_pushed_status with no timestamp fencing, so a REAL later edit on Hardcover that happens to equal the last pushed value is treated as our own echo forever; and because rating/finish-date edits arriving with an unchanged status fall into the same equality, they are never pulled. Worse, the outbound diverged-push then REVERSES the remote edit. Bidirectional sync needs updated-at fencing (compare hardcover_remote_updated_at against the push timestamp), not value equality. Note all writes are currently behind BOOM_HARDCOVER_DRYRUN, which caps the blast radius until that flag flips — fix BEFORE activating.

title: Migrate remaining route families onto the typed apiroute seam
description:
The seam (internal/shared/apiroute) and the all-features-on spec router landed 2026-08-27 (c638283, 035e8a3). Two liberation reads are migrated as the pilot; ~190 operations still emit the bare {"type":"object"} stub.

WHY THE REMAINING WORK IS NOT MECHANICAL: 89 of 149 c.JSON calls pass a map[string]any literal. Each needs a named response struct before it can move to the seam — that IS the work, and it is also the whole payoff, since a map has no shape to reflect. The registration change is trivial by comparison.

SUGGESTED ORDER (highest value first):
1. books — the rest of the domain (items/work/curation/match, kindle, hardcover, amazon connect). It had zero real coverage before this week and is the FE's newest surface.
2. identity — 38 routes, the largest single file; auth/profile shapes are the most reused by the FE.
3. stats — heaviest map[string]any usage AND 13 endpoints behind apihelpers.CachedJSON(compute func() (any, error)), which erases the type at the helper seam. Those need the compute closure to return a named type first; likely wants a typed CachedJSON variant.
4. goals / spaces / awards / curation — small, regular, good warm-ups.

OUT OF SCOPE for the seam (~30 routes): Blob (9), Redirect (10), NoContent (9), JSONBlob (2), and the WebSocket handshakes. These stay on plain echo and keep appearing via the router walk. Do not contort the seam to cover them.

UNBLOCKS boom-vqi7 (Go -> TypeScript types): openapi-typescript needs real schemas, and every migrated family makes the generated client that much less any-shaped. Consider a coverage ratchet — a test asserting the number of schema-free operations never INCREASES — so the tail does not silently regrow.
close_reason:
Done via a 12-agent swarm + validation pass (5d16f0b). 119 routes migrated, 56 deliberately skipped, ~90 map[string]any literals replaced by named types. Spec went 0 -> 107 of 192 operations with a generated 2xx schema, 21 with a typed request body.

WHAT VALIDATION CAUGHT — the agents' self-reports were accurate about their OWN packages (all 12 compiled, zero false 'buildPassed'), but three real problems only surfaced when checked centrally:

1. A body-limit regression in MY seam, not their work: BodyLimitSmall (4 KiB) was hardcoded into every binding registrar, so the import endpoint (previously unbounded via plain c.Bind) began answering 413 and curation's rule endpoint dropped from 64 KiB. Caught by an existing test written for exactly this. Limits are per-route now with a BodyLimitNone escape, and three new tests pin default/override/uncapped. Notably the ingest agent had spotted the same trap unprompted and preserved its 8 MiB cap by binding in-handler — the heartbeat hot path was never at risk because of that judgement call.
2. testutil.go (96 hand-registered routes) plus 9 test files, all kept off-limits to the swarm so 12 agents could not collide on one file. Rewritten centrally by MIRRORING each domain's registrar, so a route registered as Accepted still answers 202 under test instead of silently becoming 200.
3. Three stub closures in ratelimit/metrics tests were wrongly converted by path-matching and reverted.

Wire format was verified rather than assumed: every map key from every pre-migration file extracted from git and checked against the new json tags. Four flags, all resolved — three shared types in sibling files, one traced through apierr.Write to confirm an identical {"error": ...} envelope.

ALSO SHIPPED: hand-authored spec entries now lose to a generated schema when theirs is an empty placeholder (~60 were), while keeping their prose. Guarded so hand-BUILT schemas survive — the public-profile payload is a deliberate scrubbed subset, and a test now fails if enrichment ever advertises a field widget.Scrub removes.

REMAINING (not regressions, deliberate): ~85 operations still stub. The bulk is stats' ~13 CachedJSON(compute func() (any, error)) endpoints, which erase the type at the helper seam and need a typed CachedJSON variant first; plus blob/redirect/204/WebSocket routes that are not JSON-shaped; plus a few genuinely branch-dependent shapes (books push returns 200+DTO or 202+ack depending on wiring, and the FE relies on that duality). Filed follow-up work should start with the typed CachedJSON variant — it is the single biggest remaining block.

title: Job executor is single-threaded per process — long jobs head-of-line block every other kind
description:
CONFIRMED WITH DATA 2026-08-25. DJ suspected the queues were blocking each other. They are, and I initially said they were not — that was wrong.

MECHANISM: LocalProvider.Run (internal/jobs/local.go:252-274) is a strictly sequential loop — ClaimNext -> p.runJob(...) -> continue. runJob is a BLOCKING call, not a goroutine. So one process runs exactly ONE job at a time regardless of kind. LocalProvider.Drain (local.go:233-245) is the same shape.

MEASURED IMPACT: books-reading-monitor averages 185.3s per run (max 260.3s) and ran 16 times in 2 hours = ~2,965s of 7,200s. The always-on server pod is therefore head-of-line blocked roughly 41% of wall-clock, claiming NOTHING — not hardcover-pull, not kindle-sync, not audible-sync — while the monitor's internal loop runs. Nothing is visibly starved today only because the other server-resident kinds are low-volume and scheduled; any burst queues behind up to 4.3 minutes.

THE SHARPER CONSEQUENCE: every per-kind concurrency cap is unreachable within a single process. SetConcurrency/KindLimiter can only bind ACROSS pods. BOOM_BOOKS_LIBERATE_CONCURRENCY=5 never admitted 5 — liberation sat at 3-wide because there were 3 drain pods running 1 job each. The limiter's existence implies the design intended concurrent execution; the executor never delivered it. This is also why raising the cap did nothing and raising maxReplicaCount did.

FIX: give the provider a worker pool — N goroutines each running the claim/execute loop, sized by a config knob (BOOM_JOBS_WORKERS, default maybe 4). ClaimNext is already safe for this: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED means N in-process claimers behave exactly like N pods. The per-kind limiter then starts doing the job it was written for, and a long reading-monitor run occupies one worker instead of the whole pod.

CARE REQUIRED:
- The heartbeat ticker is already per-job (startHeartbeat in exec.go), so that is fine.
- Cancel tracking (LocalProvider.execTracked) is per-job and must stay correct with N concurrent.
- Drain-mode exit semantics: today Drain returns when ClaimNext finds nothing. With N workers it must not exit while siblings are still running, or a ScaledJob pod would terminate mid-job.
- Graceful shutdown must wait for in-flight jobs across all workers.

RELATED: with a worker pool, maxReplicaCount and the per-kind caps stop being the same dial, and keda-scaledjob-jobs.yaml's comment about 'replicas ARE the concurrency' becomes wrong and must be updated.
close_reason:
Worker pool shipped. LocalProvider.Run and Drain now each spawn BOOM_JOBS_WORKERS (default 4) concurrent claim loops instead of one sequential loop, so a long job occupies one worker rather than the whole pod. Safe because ClaimNext already used FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED — N in-process claimers behave exactly like N pods, which the queue was designed for.

CARE POINTS FROM THE BEAD, all handled: (a) Drain exit semantics — an individual worker stops when IT finds the queue empty, but Drain does not RETURN until every worker has stopped, so a ScaledJob pod cannot terminate mid-handler; there is a dedicated test with 1 job and 6 workers that pins exactly this race. (b) locked_by now stamps per SLOT (pod#N) so it still identifies a single claimant; single-worker processes keep the bare id so existing rows read unchanged. (c) cancels map was already mutex-guarded and per-job, so cancel tracking needed no change. (d) heartbeat was already per-job. (e) Drain reports the first worker error but lets siblings finish their current job rather than killing running work.

5 tests, all DB-backed. The concurrency one measures PEAK OVERLAP rather than 'did the jobs finish', because a pool that silently ran serially would pass any completion assertion — mutation-verified: with SetWorkers(1) it fails with 'peak concurrent handlers = 1'. Also pins exactly-once across 25 jobs / 6 workers (double-execution here would mean downloading the same audiobook twice), the sibling-wait race, SetWorkers clamping, and workerID uniqueness. go test -race clean.

CONSEQUENCE: per-kind concurrency caps now actually bind in-process. They previously could only bind ACROSS pods, so BOOM_BOOKS_LIBERATE_CONCURRENCY=5 admitted 1 per pod and liberation ran 3-wide because there were 3 pods. Updated the keda-scaledjob-jobs.yaml comment that claimed 'replicas ARE the concurrency' — that was true before this change and is now wrong.

title: Kindle liberation: run the probe FIRST — it gates the whole question
description:
From the boom-w20s Kindle discovery research (2026-08-25). Read the full report in that session; the short version is that Kindle liberation is materially harder than Audible and the hard part is NOT the DRM.

THE SHAPE OF IT:
- Decrypt is TRACTABLE. ~350 lines of Python (mkb79/kindle dedrm.py) -> ~600-800 lines of Go. Ion parsing is NOT the blocker: amazon-ion/ion-go is official and Apache-2.0. Crypto is stdlib (AES-CBC, HMAC-SHA256, PKCS7) plus ulikunitz/xz/lzma.
- CONVERSION is the hole. A decrypted KFX is unreadable by Calibre-without-plugin, Kavita, Komga or KOReader. The only converter is jhowell kfxlib: 96 Python files, ~2.3MB, GPL-3, including a bundled JPEG-XR decoder because KFX images are JXR. Tell: even flamberge (Rust) stops at decryption and maps .kfx-zip -> .kfx-zip. Decrypting into a format nothing can open is the failure mode where you finish the hard work and have nothing to show.

TWO UNKNOWNS THAT CANNOT BE SETTLED FROM A DESK, and everything downstream is contingent on both:
1. Does GET kindle-digital-delivery.amazon.com/delivery/manifest/kindle.ebook/{ASIN} return 200 for our existing credential? The best reference (mkb79/kindle) is from Feb 2021. The only 2026 datapoint (tldev/flyleaf docs, verified 2026-08-22) says the manifest REJECTS a fresh device — though they were chasing PDOCs and their device likely was not Kindle-typed. If it 403s, does a Kindle-typed registration (device_type AGZZ1ST63LKBW) work? THIS SINGLE REQUEST IS THE GATE.
2. What are lock_parameters on our actual books? ['CLIENT_ID'] means our own DeviceCredential.DeviceSerial is the key and this is buildable. ['ACCOUNT_SECRET'] means the secret lives behind Windows TPM 2.0 and we are dead without a Windows box. AkitaOnRails (2026-07-30, first-hand) reports modern titles use ACCOUNT_SECRET. Need the RATIO across ~20 titles spanning purchase dates.

ALSO WORTH ANSWERING IN THE SAME PASS:
3. Does &supportedVoucherVersions=V1 still work? If Amazon forces V2/V3 we inherit DeDRM's 28+-version OBFUSCATION_TABLE, roughly doubling decrypt work.
4. What actually comes down as KINDLE_MAIN_BASE? If some titles deliver AZW3/KF8 they use the much simpler MOBI PID scheme AND standard readers open them directly — sidestepping the kfxlib hole entirely for those.

HOW: extend the EXISTING admin diagnostics harness (internal/books/liberate/probe.go) with source=kindle-liberation, exactly as boom-w20s.19 did for Audible. That harness already exists, already redacts, and already renders in the admin UI. Cost: an afternoon. DO NOT WRITE A PIPELINE FIRST.

Precedent that matters: probe.go's voucherOrderProbe sweeps every candidate derivation and NAMES the winner. The Kindle voucher path brute-forces six (dsn_len, secret_len) splits and swallows exceptions, so a wrong key that unpads cleanly yields plausible garbage. Same trap, same mitigation.

DECIDE BEFORE BUILDING: what the KFX->EPUB answer is. Realistically a Calibre + KFX Input sidecar container invoked as a subprocess (the ffmpeg pattern, ~300MB image and a GPL Python dependency), or stop at DRM-free KFX and accept nothing reads it.

title: Job kinds: books-liberate-book + books-liberate-sweep
description: Register both in internal/books/jobs/jobs.go inside the existing cfg.BooksEnabled() block, additionally gated on LiberationEnabled(). books-liberate-book: owner+ASIN payload, one book end-to-end, cap 2 (BOOM_BOOKS_LIBERATE_CONCURRENCY). Cap 2 not 1 because - unlike the Hardcover kinds capped at 1 for a GLOBAL rate limit - liberation is bounded by disk and Amazon's CDN. books-liberate-sweep: owner-scoped, enqueues one book job per unliberated title, cap 1. NO DEFAULT SCHEDULE: a first sweep is hundreds of GB and must be a decision, not a side effect of enabling a flag (auto-liberate-on-scan is epic B). Heartbeat is mandatory in both the download loop and the ffmpeg wait. notify.Hub BookLiberated event per completion + a sweep-complete summary, exactly as audible.Service does. Design doc section 5.
close_reason: books-liberate-book + books-liberate-sweep registered in internal/books/jobs/jobs.go, gated on LiberationEnabled(). Sweep does NOT liberate inline — it fans out one job per book so each gets its own retry, slot and heartbeat instead of one giant job losing 400 books' progress when it dies on 401. Cap 2 (BOOM_BOOKS_LIBERATE_CONCURRENCY), not 1: unlike the Hardcover kinds, liberation is bounded by disk/CDN rather than a global rate limit. buildLiberation returns nil on an unusable library path (loud ERROR, dark feature) rather than registering kinds that fail every job, and probes ffmpeg at wiring time. CORRECTION to the original bead: manual heartbeating is NOT needed — internal/jobs/exec.go startHeartbeat already runs a background ticker for the whole handler duration, so the Progress callback is for reporting only. No default schedule, as specified.

title: Tests: unit + integration + e2e for liberation
description: Per the standing test-layering rule, each layer catches what the others cannot. UNIT (no network/ffmpeg): voucher_test.go decrypting a CAPTURED real voucher fixture to a known key/iv (pins the concat order forever - highest-value test here); chapters_test.go for nested chapter_info incl. brand intro/outro offsets; template_test.go table-driven with hostile titles (../../etc, NUL, 300-char, RTL override, Windows reserved CON); license_test.go for request body shape + the POST canonical string. Test coverage complete across all three layers. UNIT: voucher (mutation-verified concat order, redaction under fmt+slog), template (hostile-input table that caught a real path-forging bug), sink (EXDEV, stale .partial, sibling-prefix escape), chapters (flat+nested, boundary repair, ffmetadata escaping), tags, license wire-shape, podcast classification. Environment gap, filed as boom-00jf. Writing it still paid: running it found an inverted feature probe (status !== 404 reported ENABLED when the SPA catch-all served 200 index.html for an absent route).

title: fsSink + naming template (atomic commit, EXDEV, traversal-safe)
description: sink.go: Sink{Commit(workPath, relPath) (string,error); Stat; Remove} + fsSink under BOOM_BOOKS_LIBRARY_PATH. An s3Sink stays possible via objstore later - the interface exists so that is a config change, not a refactor. ATOMICITY: convert in work dir then os.Rename into place; Audiobookshelf must never see a partial .m4b. Work and library on different filesystems (the NFS case) makes os.Rename fail EXDEV - fall back to copy-to-.partial-then-rename WITHIN the library filesystem. template.go: default '{author}/{series}/{series_index} - {title}/{title}.m4b' (non-series variant without the series segment). Sanitize PER SEGMENT (strip / NUL control chars trailing dots+spaces, Windows-hostile chars too since the library may be SMB-shared), collapse whitespace, 120-byte UTF-8-safe segment cap, and REJECT any rendered path escaping the library root - titles are untrusted Amazon-supplied input. Design doc section 6.
close_reason: Implemented template.go + sink.go + crossdevice.go. Template gained OPTIONAL GROUPS ([...] dropped when any placeholder inside is empty) so ONE template serves the series and standalone cases — deviation from the design doc's two-template plan, doc updated. SECURITY FIX found by the hostile-input table during implementation: sanitising assembled SEGMENTS is insufficient because the split on / happens after substitution, so '../../etc/passwd' in a title forged real directory levels; values are now sanitised BEFORE substitution. FSSink: atomic rename fast path, EXDEV copy-to-.partial+fsync+rename fallback (the normal NFS case), refuses to MkdirAll its root (unmounted-volume guard), resolve() prefix-checks against Root+separator. 20 tests incl. hostile titles, UTF-8-safe truncation, sibling-prefix escape, stale .partial, cancellation.

title: liberate.Service: LiberateBook / LiberateAll orchestration + idempotency
description: liberate.go ties sections 2.1-2.6 together: license -> voucher -> fetch -> decrypt -> tag -> commit -> record state, with per-stage liberation_status transitions and an attempt row per run. IDEMPOTENCY CONTRACT (mirrors BackfillUser/SyncUser): liberated + file present at audio_path with matching audio_bytes = SKIP; file missing = re-liberate (someone deleted it); size mismatch = re-liberate (truncated); --force overrides. Failure classification matters: Denied -> terminal, short read -> retryable, unparseable container -> unsupported_codec WITH content_format recorded (that count is what later justifies epic D). Discard partial temp files on start; range-resume is epic B. Design doc section 4.
close_reason: internal/books/liberate/service.go + store.go. Sequences license->voucher->fetch->remux->commit with per-stage status transitions and an attempt-history row. Idempotency contract implemented and tested: liberated + file present at recorded size = skip; missing = re-liberate; size mismatch = re-liberate; Force overrides. Failure classification: Denied is TERMINAL (and ListUnliberated excludes it, so the sweep genuinely stops retrying), short read is retryable, and a remux failure on a non-AAX_* content_format is attributed to unsupported_codec WITH the format recorded — that count is the epic-D trigger. Narrowed the Amazon dependency to a CredentialLoader interface, and added Licenser/Fetcher seams (matching the Kindle ingest's fake-library pattern) because both real implementations target hard-coded Amazon hosts. 8 DB-backed integration tests against an isolated boomtime_liberate_test DB — the voucher step runs for REAL against a test-sealed voucher, only the transport is stubbed.

title: Decryptor interface + ffmpegDecryptor + startup probe + Dockerfile
description: decrypt.go defines Decryptor{Decrypt(ctx, src, dst, ContentKey, Metadata) error} so the native Go remuxer (epic D) is a drop-in later. ffmpeg.go implements it: ffmpeg -nostdin -y -audible_key K -audible_iv IV -i in.aaxc -i chapters.txt -map_metadata 1 -c copy -movflags +faststart out.m4b. -c copy = remux, no re-encode, bit-identical audio. Add ffmpeg to the alpine:3.20 RUNTIME stage only (Dockerfile:75, ~80MB). Probe 'ffmpeg -version' at startup when the flag is on and log a clear ERROR if absent (same posture as the BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY prod check) - image without ffmpeg must still boot. Key/iv must never reach logs or the process table dump. Design doc section 2.4.
close_reason: decrypt.go (Decryptor seam) + ffmpeg.go (FFmpegDecryptor) + ffmpeg added to BOTH runtime images (Dockerfile and Dockerfile.catalyst-books — liberation is a books capability and runs in both deployments). Verified alpine 3.20 ships ffmpeg 6.1.1 WITH -audible_key/-audible_iv. MAJOR GOTCHA DOCUMENTED: those options live on the **mov** demuxer, not the demuxer named 'aax' — that one is CRI AAX, an unrelated Criware game-audio format, and 'ffmpeg -h demuxer=aax' describes it while appearing to answer the question. Same demuxer also exposes -activation_bytes, so epic C's legacy-AAX support needs no new dependency. SECRET HANDLING: ffmpeg takes the key as argv so it is visible in the process table — inherent to the ffmpeg choice, not fixable here (epic D removes it). Mitigated: logArgs() redacts before anything is emitted, and ffmpeg stderr is scrubbed before landing in an error. Available() probe backs a startup gate. 4 tests incl. a redaction test that first asserts the raw argv DOES contain the key, so the redaction assertion cannot pass vacuously.

title: Streaming AAXC download with progress + heartbeat
description: fetch.go in internal/books/liberate. Stream offline_url to BOOM_BOOKS_WORK_PATH. MUST NOT use SignedGet - its 64 MiB io.LimitReader would silently truncate a 500MB+ audiobook. Own unbounded streaming path; verify Content-Length vs bytes written (short read = retryable failure, not a silently-corrupt file). Attach ADP headers (harmless if the presigned CDN URL ignores them). Emit progress + tick the job heartbeat throughout - per boomtime-jobs-deploy-resilience the reaper kills non-heartbeating jobs, and this is the single most likely 'works locally, dies in prod' failure. Design doc section 2.3.
notes: LIVE-VERIFIED CONSTRAINT (2026-08-24): the CDN offline_url returns 403 to a bare GET. ADP headers are MANDATORY on the download, not optional — sign over the URL's RequestURI() (path+query), NOT the API path. Range support is still unknown (the 403 meant the first probe never saw a successful response); offlineURLProbe now reports Accept-Ranges/Content-Range on a re-run, so check that before assuming resume works. Real-world size reference from the probed title: ~18h runtime (64994726ms), so this path must handle multi-hundred-MB streams and heartbeat throughout.
close_reason: internal/books/liberate/fetch.go. Deliberately NOT via amazon.SignedGet — its 64 MiB io.LimitReader would silently truncate a 600MB audiobook into something that looks like a successful download. Own unbounded streaming path with an explicit Content-Length check; a mismatch is ErrShortRead (retryable) and the partial file is REMOVED, because a truncated book that looks complete is the worst thing this package can produce. ADP headers attached per the live 403 finding, signed over the CDN URL's RequestURI() not the API path. Progress callback fires per 1MiB chunk (the heartbeat seam); cancellation checked between chunks; fsync before returning. 6 tests incl. a signed-request assertion, short-read, non-2xx-writes-nothing, unknown-Content-Length, and mid-transfer cancellation.

title: Libation rebuild: Audible liberation (download + DRM strip + M4B) — v1 core
description: Rebuild Libation (getlibation.com, rmcrackan/Libation) into the catalyst-books domain. internal/books/connect/amazon is ALREADY a Go port of Libation's AudibleApi (device registration register.go, ADP signing signing.go, library sweep ingest/audible) — this epic builds the missing FileLiberator + AAXClean + FileManager equivalents. v1 = license request -> voucher decrypt -> AAXC download -> ffmpeg -c copy remux to M4B with chapters/cover/tags -> filesystem library sink -> liberated-state on reading_items. Decisions: filesystem sink (not S3) because the point is an Audiobookshelf/Plex-scannable tree; ffmpeg subprocess behind a Decryptor interface (native Go remuxer deferred to epic D). Full-parity roadmap = follow-up epics B-E, see design doc section 10.
design: docs/design/catalyst-books-liberation-architecture.md
acceptance_criteria: Flag BOOM_FEATURE_BOOKS_LIBERATION on + BOOM_BOOKS_LIBRARY_PATH set: a real owned Audible title liberates end-to-end to a chaptered, tagged, cover-art M4B at the templated path; re-run is a no-op; unit+integration+e2e green; CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./... and yarn typecheck clean; main deployable with the flag off.
close_reason:
EPIC COMPLETE — 16/16. Libation rebuilt inside catalyst-books and running in production: 1012 audiobooks liberated, 546.5GB, appearing in Audiobookshelf as a liberated/ folder with no extra wiring.

The starting insight held up: internal/books/connect/amazon was already a Go port of Libation's AudibleApi, so this was never a from-scratch build. Shipped licensing, voucher decrypt, streaming download, ffmpeg DRM-strip + M4B remux with chapters/cover/tags, the filesystem sink with atomic EXDEV-safe commit, liberation state on reading_items, job kinds with cross-node fan-out, HTTP + CLI + FE surfaces, and a live-verification probe on the existing admin diagnostics.

TWO CORRECTIONS THE WORK FORCED, both from checking rather than assuming: (1) the CDN 403 was a WAF block, not an auth failure — I had inferred ADP headers were needed from a probe that only established a BARE GET fails; reading Libation's source showed it sends ONE header (a device-paired User-Agent) and no device auth at all, and attaching ADP headers was plausibly causing the block. That inference cost a production incident of ~1040 WAF-blocked jobs. (2) The path template sanitised assembled SEGMENTS, but the split on / happens after substitution, so a title of '../../etc/passwd' forged real directory levels — caught by the hostile-input table during implementation, not by review.

Live-verified against the real account: the signed-POST canonical string was correct first try, the voucher derivation is the canonical order, the CDN needs the paired UA, and the whole library is AAX_* (AAC-LC) — so epic D (native decoder) has no trigger. Follow-ups B/C/D/E remain open and independently justified.

title: Global cross-user Hardcover match cache (resolve from our own DB, skip the API)
description:
A match ASIN/ISBN13 -> hardcover_book_id/edition_id is user-INDEPENDENT (objective fact about a book). Once ANY user resolves it, future users/books with the same external id should resolve from our own DB with ZERO Hardcover API calls.

Design (composes on top of the flood fix's per-user stored-match path):
- New GLOBAL table hardcover_match_cache(external_id TEXT, id_type TEXT CHECK asin|isbn13, hardcover_book_id BIGINT, edition_id BIGINT, method TEXT, matched_at). PK (id_type, external_id). NOT per-user.
- Match step (internal/hardcover match.go + sync.go MatchUnmatched) becomes cache-FIRST: look up by ASIN then ISBN13 -> HIT: SetReadingItemHardcoverLink from cache, no API. MISS: call client.Match once, then on a CONFIDENT exact-id match write the row back to hardcover_match_cache.
- reading_items.hardcover_book_id (per-user link, used by the progress push) unchanged; cache is just the resolution layer feeding it.

Caveat: only globally-cache HIGH-CONFIDENCE exact-id matches (editions(asin) / isbn_13). Fuzzy Typesense title-search matches are a per-user judgment call (can be a wrong edition) -> keep per-user or cache-with-lower-trust + revalidate. Store method to distinguish. Optional: TTL / manual invalidation (book_ids are stable so TTL can be long).

title: useChartFrame ResizeObserver misses late-mounting nodes → charts blank when data loads after mount
description: useChartFrame sets up its ResizeObserver in a useEffect([]) that reads ref.current once at mount and bails permanently if null. Charts render <EmptyChart> (no ChartSurface, null ref) while their query loads; when data arrives and ChartSurface mounts, the effect never re-runs, frame.width stays 0, and useD3Surface's 'frame.width===0' guard skips the D3 draw forever -> permanently blank chart. Coding-punchcard is the consistent victim (slowest query, 2191ms, always loses the load race). ALL ~17 EmptyChart-gated charts share the latent bug. Root-cause fix: callback ref in useChartFrame so the observer attaches whenever the node mounts, incl. later than first render. Confirmed live via Playwright: punchcard SVG had width=null/height=null/0 children while container was 774px wide; every other chart drew. Regression test at useChartFrame level.
close_reason: Fixed via callback ref in useChartFrame (c9025af); verified live: punchcard renders 151 circles (was 0). Regression test proven failing against old []-effect. Full FE suite 433/433 + build green.

title: [HIGH] OIDC logout is a no-op — no server-side session revocation / kill-switch

title: [HIGH] Session-type confusion: /auth/refresh_token under OIDC mints standalone LOCAL tokens that escape the OIDC session
description: SECURITY ELEVATION of the earlier UX bug. OIDC web user POSTs /auth/refresh_token → ResolveCookie(oidc)->owner → mkTokenData+CreateAccessTokens writes LOCAL auth_tokens/refresh_tokens rows + returns a local bearer in the body. That bearer resolves via ResolveBearer->LocalPasswordResolver->GetUserByToken. Consequences: (a) local token is NOT in oidc_sessions so it survives id_token_expiry; (b) survives IdP-side disable/deprovision (local resolver never re-checks Authentik) — defeats short id_token lifetimes; (c) unrevocable via the app (see logout no-op). BONUS: setRefreshCookie overwrites the cookie with the local refresh value → next ResolveCookie misses oidc_sessions → ExpiredRefreshToken (cookie session self-destructs after one refresh while the body bearer lives on). FIX: when CurrentResolver is OIDC, RefreshToken must rotate the oidc_session (re-check id_token), NOT mint local tokens; OIDC-user bearer tokens must be tied to + revoked with the oidc_session. Confirmed by 2 agents.
design:
ROOT CAUSE: OIDC web users have cookie-only sessions, but the API surface is bearer-authed (OIDCResolver.ResolveBearer delegates to LocalPasswordResolver.GetUserByToken). So the FE calls POST /auth/refresh_token to obtain a bearer — and that bearer is a plain local auth_tokens row, disconnected from the oidc_session: survives id_token expiry, survives IdP deprovision, unrevocable via the app.

RECOMMENDED FIX = Approach A (session-tied bearers; no FE change):
1. Migration 00048: link issued bearer -> oidc_session. Simplest = nullable oidc_session_ref (hashed_session_id) column on auth_tokens; or an oidc_session_tokens(hashed_token, hashed_session_id, expiry) table.
2. Under provider=oidc, RefreshToken stores the minted bearer against the CURRENT oidc_session with token_expiry = min(SessionExpiry, id_token_expiry). Do NOT overwrite the session cookie with a local refresh value (kills the current cookie-self-destruct bug).
3. OIDCResolver.ResolveBearer: look up the bearer AND verify the parent oidc_session is still live (not expired/deleted). Miss -> InvalidToken.
4. DeleteOIDCSession cascades to its bearers (logout .13 + disable .15 already delete oidc_sessions rows -> bearers die with them).
Net: OIDC bearers can't outlive the session, die on logout, die when the session ends. Gate ALL of this behind provider=oidc so provider=local is byte-identical.
   Optional follow-up: use the stored oidc_sessions.hashed_refresh to periodically re-check Authentik mid-session (catch IdP deprovision faster than session expiry).

Approach B (cookie-native API auth: ResolveBearer falls back to ResolveCookie; FE stops needing a bearer under OIDC) is cleaner conceptually but touches the FE api client + every bearer-authed handler assumption. Rejected for now as too broad.

INTERIM MITIGATION ALREADY SHIPPED (this pass): .13 OIDC-aware logout deletes the oidc_session (blocks NEW refreshes after logout); .15 disable purges oidc_sessions + auth_tokens (so disabling kills escaping bearers too). Window is narrowed but the core fix is A. This bead is the GATE to flip BOOM_AUTH_PROVIDER=oidc in prod.
close_reason: FIXED (no migration). Under BOOM_AUTH_PROVIDER=oidc, /auth/refresh_token now mints ONLY a short 30-min access bearer (db.CreateOIDCAccessToken — no local refresh_token row) and does NOT overwrite the oidc_sessions cookie; the FE must re-present the expiring, server-revocable OIDC session cookie for each subsequent bearer. This kills the escape where OIDC refresh minted a standalone local refresh token + clobbered the session cookie (federated session -> permanent unrevocable local credential outliving the id_token). Logout (OIDC branch) now also db.DeleteUserAccessTokens(owner) so refresh-minted bearers die WITH the session, not 30 min later. Local path byte-identical behind the provider branch. Test TestOIDCAccessToken_ShortLivedAndRevocable (mint -> resolves as bearer, 0 refresh rows created, revoke -> gone). Suite 33/0. The provider=oidc flip gate is now cleared.

title: Fix Other-bucket conflation across all axes (data-layer + per-chart discriminators + configurable cap)
description:
Epic to unify the "Other" story across every axis.

## Bug: 3 layers all producing rows named 'Other', conflated on charts

1. Ingest (ingest.go:263-276) COALESCEs NULL axis values to literal 'Other' — this is browsers, AI console, extension-less clients.
2. 8 aggregation SQL queries (get_user_activity, get_timeline, get_momentum, get_leaderboards, get_projects_stats, get_category_daily, get_project_branch_daily, get_user_activity_rollup) apply the same COALESCE.
3. stats.capWithOther creates a UI-safe synth bucket named 'Other (N more)' — this is the LEGIT aggregation cap and MUST be the only 'Other' producer.

The visual bug: 55%+ 'Other' on the language pie is actually null-language browser heartbeats, not the aggregation cap.

## Fix (approved plan)

### Phase 1: Schema
Add 8 sentinel columns to hb_rollup_daily: `<axis>_missing BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`. Additive, no PK change, no dedupe hazard.

### Phase 2: Ingest
Populate the flag columns via `bool_or(<col> IS NULL)` aggregate in the rollup INSERT. Existing 'Other' rows stay unflagged; next rollup rebuild for their day corrects them.

### Phase 3: Per-chart discriminators (8 SQL files)
Each aggregation query decides its semantic contract:
- Language pie/heatmap/leaderboard: WHERE NOT language_missing
- Project pie: WHERE NOT project_missing
- File breakdown: WHERE entity IS NOT NULL
- Category pie: NO FILTER (browsing IS a category)
- Editor/Platform/Machine: NO FILTER (browsers ARE editors, etc.)
- Total time card: NO FILTER (must include everything)

### Phase 4: Configurable cap
capWithOther's 25% ceiling (otherMaxShare in segment.go:249) → BOOM_OTHER_MAX_SHARE env var, default 0.25.

### Phase 5: FE UX hint
When language pie's total < grand total by material margin, subtitle: "8h coded in 5 languages · 4h browsing/untagged" with wakatime.cfg config link.

### Phase 6: Optional CLI command
`boomtime rebuild-rollup-flags` — iterate users, re-roll their history so historical rows get flag correction. Opt-in operator action; not required for correctness (rollups self-heal as heartbeats arrive).

## Sub-beads
Will be filed as gaka-XXX.1 through .6 for each phase.
close_reason: 6 phases shipped across 3 commits (9114234, 1fea1c1, b6d792b). Migration adds 8 <axis>_missing bool columns to hb_rollup_daily. Ingest populates via bool_and(<col> IS NULL). 8 aggregation SQL queries updated with per-chart discriminators (some select flags + filter in Go, some filter WHERE in SQL). Configurable cap via BOOM_OTHER_MAX_SHARE env (default 0.25). FE ChartCard subtitle discloses N% untagged/browsing gap when it exceeds 5%/1min thresholds. Follow-up: overview dashboard cards need the subtitle wrapper (different chart primitives).
