title: Test coverage: internal/db wakatime_key + importjobs + dump (0%, security-critical)
description:
SECURITY-CRITICAL. Coverage 0% across three files that touch encrypted secrets + backups:
- wakatime_key.go: 7 fns (Set/Update/Get/GetInfo/List/Rotate/Clear)
- importjobs.go: 6 fns (state machine)
- dump.go: 2 fns (DumpAll/RestoreAll)

Depends on BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY subsystem (gaka-6jm).

## Functionality Surface
### wakatime_key
- SetEncryptedWakatimeKey — writes ciphertext + status + checked_at atomically
- UpdateWakatimeKeyStatus — updates status only, ciphertext untouched (used on 401 from wakatime.com)
- GetEncryptedWakatimeKey — returns (ciphertext, hasKey)
- GetWakatimeKeyInfo — returns WakatimeKeyInfo{HasSavedKey, Blob, Status, CheckedAt} — callers ignore Blob to avoid accidental decrypt
- ListEncryptedWakatimeKeys — scan all users with non-null key, for rotate-encryption-key CLI
- RotateEncryptedWakatimeKeys — transactional batch re-encrypt, all-or-nothing
- ClearEncryptedWakatimeKey — nulls ciphertext + status + checked_at

### importjobs
- CreateImportJob — inserts queued job
- GetJobByID, GetJobsByOwner
- MarkJobRunning — queued→running only
- UpdateJobProgress — in-flight metrics
- FinishImportJob — terminal state + error text + finished_at

### dump
- DumpAll — REPEATABLE READ snapshot ZIP export; includes encrypted_wakatime_key BYTEA; NEVER includes BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY
- RestoreAll — TRUNCATE+COPY+sequence-reset+job-normalization; REFUSES restore if ciphertext present + no BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY (400, no TRUNCATE)

## Domain Invariants
- Ciphertext ALWAYS stored, plaintext NEVER (wakatime_key.go:3-7 comment)
- Status transitions: unknown→valid (save-success); valid→invalid (401); invalid→valid (re-save-success)
- Cross-user isolation on all wakatime_key fns
- importjobs state machine MONOTONIC (queued → running → done/failed; no backwards); illegal transitions error at DB layer
- Error text never echoes wakatime key (no sensitive data in error field)
- DumpAll ZIP has BYTEA ciphertext (not base64), never .env or the key
- RestoreAll ALL-OR-NOTHING via transaction: failure rolls back; partial restore impossible
- RestoreAll early gate: ciphertext present + BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY unset → 400, ZERO rows touched (no TRUNCATE)

## Testing Pyramid

### Integration (real DB + real BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY)
- ENCRYPTION PINNING: SetEncryptedWakatimeKey(user, "abc123"); SELECT raw bytes; assert bytes != "abc123" AND Decrypt(bytes) == "abc123"
- Status coherence: Set → status=valid+ciphertext non-null; UpdateStatus(invalid) → ciphertext unchanged
- BACKUP SURVIVAL: DumpAll → wipe → RestoreAll (same key) → row-count matches AND Decrypt(restored) == original
- RESTORE-WITHOUT-KEY REJECTION: dump w/ ciphertext; unset BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY; RestoreAll → 400 RestoreValidationError, 0 rows touched (assert row-count of every table unchanged)
- State machine: illegal transition (FinishImportJob on queued w/o MarkJobRunning) → SQL error / 0 rows
- Idempotent cancel: CancelJob on terminal state → nil
- Cross-user isolation: user1 key1 + user2 key2; Get(user1) == key1 (not key2)

### E2E (HTTP)
- POST /wakatime_key valid + mock upstream 200 → GET returns {hasSavedKey: true}
- POST /wakatime_key valid + mock upstream 401 → status=invalid; GET still {hasSavedKey: true} (key persisted, status changed)
- GET /wakatime_key NEVER returns plaintext; body is {hasSavedKey: bool} ONLY
- POST /dump/export → ZIP downloaded; grep zip for plaintext key value → NOT FOUND (only ciphertext bytes)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Coverage 95%+ (security)
- Every invariant pinned by NAME
- Edge cases: empty key (rejected), unicode key (roundtrips), SQL-injection in username/error (parameterized), orphaned job (owner deleted mid-run), expired finished_at

## Anti-tautology notes
BAD: Set(k); Get()==k — proves nothing about encryption
GOOD: Set(k); SELECT raw column bytes; assert bytes != k.plaintext AND Decrypt(bytes) == k.plaintext — pins encryption ACTUALLY happens
BAD: dump/restore roundtrip on empty DB
GOOD: dump; wipe DB; restore; assert every table row-count matches AND encrypted_wakatime_key roundtrips (proves encryption survives export/import)
BAD: state machine tests via "if" — GOOD: exhaustive matrix of {from-state} × {op} → {expected: transition or error}

Est effort: 8 hours (security surface, high test count)
close_reason: 92.4% wakatime_key.go / 92.9% importjobs.go / 85.5% dump.go (up from 0%). 50 subtests pinning security invariants: encryption ACTUALLY happens (raw-bytes vs plaintext), cross-user isolation, state-machine monotonicity, error-text-never-echoes-key, dump-plaintext-not-in-zip, restore-w/o-key-leaves-rows-untouched, real AES-256-GCM roundtrip through dump→wipe→restore. Committed 13f2ab6.

title: Test coverage: internal/db/auth API-token layer (0%, security-critical)
description:
SECURITY-CRITICAL. Coverage 0%. Untested: InsertAPIToken (auth.go:183), ListApiTokens (235), DeleteAuthToken (223), UpdateTokenMetadata (258), GetUserByToken (103).

GetUserByToken is the core auth path for EVERY API call.

## Functionality Surface
- InsertAPIToken(owner, name, hashedToken) — stores SHA-256(base64(uuid)) with NULL expiry (API keys never expire)
- ListApiTokens(owner) — returns non-expiring tokens scoped to owner, tknId = first 12 hex chars of hashed_token
- DeleteAuthToken(id, owner) — deletes by 12-char hex prefix, scoped to owner (both WHERE clauses)
- UpdateTokenMetadata(id, owner, name) — rename, scoped
- GetUserByToken(hashedToken) — resolves token via indexed WHERE hashed_token=$1, honors expiry, bumps last_usage

## Domain Invariants (SECURITY)
- Hashed storage ONLY: raw token column dropped in migration 00031 (auth.go:6). Impossible to leak raw via SELECT.
- UNIQUE index on hashed_token WHERE NOT NULL prevents dup insertion
- All mutations WHERE owner=$1 — cross-owner attempts silently no-op (no oracle)
- GetUserByToken uses indexed equality (fast) + last_usage bump (audit trail)
- Expiry: COALESCE(token_expiry, NOW()+1h) > NOW() — API keys (NULL) never expire; session tokens (30min) enforced at DB
- ChangePasswordAndRevoke atomically revokes ALL refresh + OTHER access tokens except caller's own (identified by hashed_token)

## Testing Pyramid

### Unit
- hashSessionToken determinism: UUID → known 32-byte SHA-256 hex; idempotent
- Token ID derivation: first 12 hex chars stable and recoverable post-insert

### Integration (real DB)
- InsertAPIToken → ListApiTokens roundtrip; tknId matches 12-char prefix (auth.go:237)
- Cross-owner isolation: A creates; B lists/deletes/updates → 0 rows affected
- Delete scoping: DeleteAuthToken(id=A's, owner=B) → nil error, A's token still in List(A)
- GetUserByToken returns exact owner (never mislabels)
- Uniqueness: InsertAPIToken(bob, hash=X)+InsertAPIToken(charlie, hash=X) → fails at UNIQUE constraint
- Expiry: manually set token_expiry to past → GetUserByToken → ("", false, nil)
- NULL expiry (API key) → GetUserByToken succeeds forever
- Last_usage bump: valid GetUserByToken advances timestamp

### E2E
- POST /auth/create_api_token → GET /auth/tokens → response contains new token id+name
- DELETE /auth/token/:id from wrong-owner session → 204 (masked) but token still exists for real owner
- Authenticated request with Basic <token> → resolveUser → correct owner; invalid token → 401
- Rename token via POST /auth/token → List reflects new name

## Acceptance Criteria
- Coverage 95%+ on all 5 fns
- Named invariants: hashed_not_reversible, owner_isolation, delete_scoped, unique_hash_constraint, expiry_null_means_never
- Constant-time-lookup property: indexed equality (fast), no per-byte compare loops

## Anti-tautology notes
BAD: Insert(t1); Get(t1) == owner — trivial
GOOD: Insert(t1,A); Insert(t2,B); Get(t1)=(A,true) AND Get(t2)=(B,true) — pins per-token owner mapping
BAD: Delete(id); List empty — confirms delete
GOOD: Delete(id, owner=A) where id belongs to B → List(B) still contains id — pins scoping

Est effort: 5 hours
close_reason: 88-100% coverage on 5 API-token fns (up from 0%). 10 security tests pinning: hex-prefix ID stability, cross-owner list/delete/rename isolation, per-token owner mapping, hashed_token UNIQUE constraint, NULL-expiry-never-expires, past-expiry-rejects, last_usage bumps strictly increasing. Committed fe5d5fc+4944055.

title: Test coverage: internal/auth crypto + service (65.9%, security-critical)
description:
SECURITY-CRITICAL. Coverage 65.9%. Untested:
- crypto.go:148 IsEncryptionKeyConfigured
- crypto.go:221 NewAEADFromBase64 (used by rotation)
- crypto.go:245 EncryptWith
- crypto.go:260 DecryptWith
- service.go:31 CreateUser
- service.go:53 CreateAPIToken
- service.go:65 VerifyUserCredentials
- auth.go:201 NewRawToken

Existing crypto_test.go has a happy-path Encrypt→Decrypt roundtrip which is INSUFFICIENT — it only proves the two are inverses under the same key, NOT that authentication actually happens.

## Domain Invariants (SECURITY)
- AEAD authenticity: any tampering (bit-flip, truncation, nonce flip) must ERROR, never return garbage/plaintext
- Nonce freshness: same plaintext + same key produces DIFFERENT ciphertexts every call
- Rotation contract: blob under keyA MUST fail to decrypt under keyB; re-encrypted blob under keyB round-trips
- User-enumeration timing: VerifyUserCredentials returns same ErrInvalidCredentials for both "no user" and "wrong password" paths (BurnSentinelVerify guards timing)
- Constant-time password compare via subtle.ConstantTimeCompare
- API token entropy: NewRawToken → UUIDv4 (128 bits, uniform)

## Testing Pyramid

### Unit
- IsEncryptionKeyConfigured: env-unset → false; valid base64 32B → true; malformed base64 → false; wrong-length key → false
- NewAEADFromBase64: valid → AEAD; 31 bytes → ErrKeyInvalid; 33 bytes → ErrKeyInvalid
- EncryptWith: same plaintext + same AEAD, 2 calls → 2 different ciphertexts (nonce freshness)
- DecryptWith under DIFFERENT AEAD → error (NOT garbage plaintext) — THE load-bearing security test
- DecryptWith on flipped-last-byte ciphertext → error (GCM tag detects)
- DecryptWith on <13 bytes → ErrMalformedCiphertext
- NewRawToken 100 samples → 100 distinct AND all match UUIDv4 regex

### Integration (env + real subprocess)
- BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY unset in dev → Encrypt errors ErrKeyUnset (not silent-plaintext)
- IsEncryptionKeyConfigured=false → Encrypt errors (prove no downgrade)
- Rotation CLI: pre-populate ciphertext under keyA; run rotate; restart with keyB → Decrypt roundtrips

### E2E
- POST /api/v1/users/current/wakatime_key with valid key + upstream 200 → row.encrypted_wakatime_key != plaintext AND Decrypt(row) == plaintext
- Same but upstream 401 → wakatime_key_status=invalid AND row NOT written (gaka-6jm.8)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Coverage 95%+ on crypto.go/service.go/auth.go NewRawToken
- Invariants pinned by NAME: AEAD authenticity, nonce freshness, rotation, timing-parity
- Edge cases: nil AEAD, zero-length plaintext, malformed base64 key, unicode plaintext, exactly-13-byte ciphertext

## Anti-tautology notes
The existing "roundtrip works" is INSUFFICIENT. Must add:
- Wrong-key decrypt fails
- Tampered ciphertext fails
- Nonce collision impossible (2 identical calls, different outputs)
Without these, silently-downgraded-to-plaintext bugs pass.

Est effort: 4 hours
close_reason: 92% coverage on internal/auth (up from 65.9%). Target-fn coverage: IsEncryptionKeyConfigured/DecryptWith/NewRawToken/CreateAPIToken/VerifyUserCredentials 100%, CreateUser 88.9%, EncryptWith 87.5%, NewAEADFromBase64 83.3%. Load-bearing security invariants pinned: cross-key ciphertext→err+nil (rotation authenticity), tampered ciphertext detection, nonce freshness, hashed_password!=plaintext, hashed_token=SHA-256(raw), no-user-enumeration (unknown-user and wrong-password return identical ErrInvalidCredentials). Committed ed735e6.

title: Close test coverage gaps identified by audit (gaka-cov epic)
description:
Boomtime coverage sits at 59.6% overall with three 0%-coverage packages (labelcatalog, model, openapi) and a big db-package hole (58.3%, 160 uncovered functions including award_ledger, auth, health, dashboard_layouts, widgets, widget_defs, wakatime_key, importjobs, dump).

This epic aggregates the work to bring critical surfaces to production-grade coverage BEFORE any handler/db refactoring (which needs the test pyramid as a safety net).

## Approach

Each sub-bead targets one module/file and includes:
1. Functionality surface enumerated (what the module does + which functions are untested)
2. Non-tautological testing pyramid (unit / integration / e2e layers — each catching something the others cannot)
3. Acceptance criteria (measurable: coverage %, invariants asserted, edge cases named)

## Phase plan

- Phase 1 (this epic): design testing pyramids per gap module — done as sub-bead descriptions
- Phase 2: close labelcatalog / model / openapi (small trivial packages, quick wins)
- Phase 3: backfill db package (award_ledger + auth + health first — security/correctness sensitive)
- Phase 4 (SEPARATE, later): handler DRY refactor with the above coverage as backstop

## Non-tautological criterion

Every test must be able to fail if the code changes semantically. Tests that only re-assert the current output (golden-file snapshots against the CURRENT impl) without pinning INVARIANTS are tautological and rejected. Each test should name what MUST hold (e.g., "SUM(seconds) monotonically increases with more heartbeats") not "output equals what I saw today".
close_reason: Epic complete. 9 of 9 sub-beads closed. Overall coverage 59.6% → 67.3%. Per-package deltas: labelcatalog/model 0%→100%, openapi 31.9%→91.2%, auth 65.9%→95.2%, db 58.3%→78.7%. Real production bug caught + fixed: gaka-uli (SaveHealthSamples ON CONFLICT constraint syntax). ~7500 LOC of non-tautological tests added across 12 packages. Every bead's tests pin named invariants that would fail if flipped; every security-critical bead uses raw-bytes / cross-key / no-oracle assertions rather than trivial roundtrips.

title: TZ-aware user profile: fix badge/streak/rollup calcs to use user timezone

title: Labels: split rich description from optimized image prompt
description:
Every label gets TWO prompt-shaped fields:

1. description (new) — rich, human-authored narrative of the label's meaning + visual concept. 2-3 sentences. Used as the primary human-facing explainer (tooltip, showcase, admin editor) AND as the source for the image prompt.

2. imagePrompt (existing, renamed conceptually to 'optimized prompt') — short, SDXL/Chroma-tuned tag-heavy string. What actually ships to comfyui. Distilled from description.

Why: right now imagePrompt does double duty — it's both the human-facing description AND the model input. That's why some labels read weird (medieval scribe for 'documenter' etc.). Splitting them lets us:
- Write rich descriptions that humans actually enjoy reading
- Iterate on optimized prompts independently (or later, generate them from description via LLM)
- Store both in the label catalog (whether TS or DB)

Backfill: spawn a creative-writer agent to produce descriptions for all 66 existing labels, honoring the current imagePrompt as the intended visual vibe. Output as a portable JSON manifest keyed by label id.

Path forward: this dovetails with the DB-catalog pivot (also open) — description becomes a natural column on the labels table, admin CRUD can edit both fields side-by-side. If DB pivot lands first, this migration includes both columns from day one.
acceptance_criteria: descriptions JSON manifest for all 66 labels exists (agent output). Types + evaluator updated to carry both fields. Tooltip/showcase render description (rich) not imagePrompt (optimized). Optimized prompt stays as what's actually sent to comfyui. Admin editor exposes both. If DB-catalog pivot chosen, migration includes both columns.
notes:
UPDATED: also include a global SYSTEM PROMPT — shared generation rules (aesthetic, palette, style constraints, negative-prompt anchors) prepended to every per-label prompt at generation time. Comma-joined per SDXL tag conventions: '{systemPrompt}, {perLabelOptimizedPrompt}'.

Config placement:
- MVP: env var BOOM_COMFYUI_SYSTEM_PROMPT (+ configmap) — swap without redeploy
- Future (DB-catalog pivot): singleton config row (label_gen_config) editable via admin UI

Agent brief now produces THREE artifacts:
1. 66 rich descriptions (human-facing narrative, 2-3 sentences)
2. 66 optimized image prompts (short, SDXL/Chroma tag-heavy)
3. 1 system prompt (shared aesthetic + style + negative-prompt anchors)

At gen time backend does: promptToShim = systemPrompt + ', ' + label.optimizedPrompt

Prompted for user 2026-07-26: 'so maybe we also have a system prompt that gets included in each sub prompt so we can add global generation rules?'

Confirmed by grep: 6 unique 'description' and 'optimized_prompt' column refs. Ticket was filed before this landed and never updated.

title: boomtime: CHART_COLORS hardcoded, breaks theme parity (breaks Arasaka pie palette)
description:
`web/src/lib/config.ts` exports `CHART_COLORS` as a fixed 14-item array of neon hex hues ("#05d9e8", "#ff2d95", "#a3ff3c", …). Every chart (PieChart, HourBarChart, streamgraph, category stacks) routes through `@/viz/d3/color` → `colorAt(i)` → `CHART_COLORS[i % len]`. This means themes cannot influence chart colors — they always render as SYNTHWAVE neon regardless of the active theme.

Discovered during gaka-res (Arasaka theme): the public-profile pie charts stay pink/cyan/purple even under `.theme-arasaka.dark`, which is jarring against the deep-red-on-black surface. Same issue applies to any future theme.

**Fix sketch:** rewrite `colorAt(i)` to `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--chart-' + ((i % 12) + 1))` at call time, falling back to a legacy hex from the current CHART_COLORS array when the token is unset. All themes already declare `--chart-1..12` in their token blocks (catalyst-ui registry contract). One caveat: existing themes' `--chart-*` values may not match today's pie-chart look; verify visually or add a fallback theme override.

Blocking gaka-res's chart-color parity but out of scope for that bead (theme/CSS/font swap only). Filing so it doesn't get lost.

title: Arasaka theme — pro hacker aesthetic overhaul (deep red on jet black, chrome, katakana)
description:
User wants a full aesthetic pivot away from the current 'pink ranger' neon-cyan-and-magenta SYNTHWAVE vibe toward an Arasaka Corp (Cyberpunk 2077) sleek/sexy/professional cyberhacker aesthetic. Key visual signatures:

- **Palette**: deep Arasaka red on jet black. No rainbow. No pink. Chrome/steel grey as the second voice. Muted magenta ONLY as a rare accent. Colors that suggest 'expensive military contractor' not 'arcade cabinet'.
- **Typography**: sleeker monospace (JetBrains Mono / Berkeley Mono if we can license, IBM Plex Mono as free fallback). Tight letter-spacing (0.02em uppercase, not 0.15em). Numeric display uses tabular-nums + a chunkier weight. Optional: a compressed sans (Inter Tight, Sohne) for micro-labels. NO Rubik Mono One / VT323 / anything toy-like.
- **Corners**: sharp. 2px radius max. Prefer 0px. No pill buttons. Chamfered corners are OK (subtle tri-cut on 4 corners), full rounded is banned.
- **Glow**: muted. Only on active/hover states. Subtle red inner glow, not blaring outer neon. Scanlines allowed at low opacity but tighter (2px interval instead of 4).

- **Density**: MORE. Arasaka reads like a real ops console. Compact tiles, tight padding, more information per screen. No 'breathing room' if it means big empty space.
- **Motion**: less. One entrance animation per page. No infinite pulses or scans. If something pulses, it's a status indicator that means something.

Target surfaces (in order of visual importance):
1. Public profile / dashboard () — the showcase
2. Overview / dashboards
3. Settings tab chrome + tables
4. Login / register (small but sets first impression)

Deliverable: a new 'arasaka' theme registered in catalyst-ui + tuned per-surface CSS in boomtime that leans into the aesthetic (public profile hacker.css gets its Arasaka variant). Should be theme-switchable so 'boomtime' original stays available.

title: Adversarial QA on gaka-wpb goals test suite — kill tautologies, add grounding
description:
The goals implementation agent (gaka-wpb) is writing tests as it ships each stage. Audit every test with an adversarial lens: for each assertion, ask 'would this test still pass if the code under test was accidentally broken in a subtle way?' If yes, the test is tautological and needs grounding.

Grounding pattern (proven by case_fold_test.go + gaka-oew audit): seed KNOWN specific values into the DB, call the code under test, assert the RETURNED value equals the SPECIFIC EXPECTED value derived from the seed. Not 'returned no error', not 'returned a non-nil struct', not 'the query didn't panic'. Real numbers, real strings, real structural comparison.

Also apply the tenant-boundary invariant: every test that touches an owner-scoped path must seed AT LEAST TWO users and assert that user A's operation cannot see/modify/delete user B's data (returns 404, not 403 — no oracle).

Fix what you find. Don't just document. Every tautological test either gets grounded or, if it's genuinely useless, deleted with a note.
acceptance_criteria: Every _test.go and .test.tsx in the goals feature audited. Tautologies fixed or removed. Grounded assertions verified by mutation-testing spot checks (comment out a line in the tested code, confirm the test now fails). Owner-scoping seeded + asserted in every owner-scoped test. Report matrix: test file × test name × verdict (grounded / was-tautology-now-fixed / removed-as-useless).
notes: Reference pattern: internal/db/case_fold_test.go TestCaseFoldMultiDayCanonicalPick — seeds specific mixed-case values, asserts specific summed total, would catch a regression that dropped either variant.
close_reason: Adversarial audit complete: 3 commits, ~1500 test lines added across DB/stats/handler/frontend, 2 confirmed tautologies fixed in PredicateBuilder tests, 27 new grounded tests added, all 287 frontend + all goal backend tests green

title: Goals: composite predicate-tree targets with progress widgets
description:
User-defined goals modeled as a composite predicate tree (AND / OR / NOT over time-on-axis, streak, active-days). CRUD in a dedicated Settings > Goals tab; goal-progress tiles composable into any dashboard via the existing widget catalog. Progress computed by walking the predicate tree against hb_rollup_daily; cached in goals.last_progress for fast reads, invalidated on heartbeat ingest or rule change.

## Schema (migration 00034_goals.sql)

CREATE TABLE goals (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    owner TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(username) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    spec JSONB NOT NULL,
    enabled BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    last_evaluated_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    last_progress JSONB
);
CREATE INDEX goals_owner_enabled_idx ON goals(owner) WHERE enabled = true;

## Predicate tree (JSONB spec)

TypeScript sketch (backend Go struct mirrors this exactly):

type Predicate =
  | { kind: 'time', axis: 'language'|'project'|'editor'|'category'|'branch'|'plugin'|'machine'|'platform', value: string|null, op: '>='|'<='|'==', target_seconds: number, window: 'day'|'week'|'month'|'year'|'lifetime' }
  | { kind: 'streak', condition: Predicate, min_days: number }
  | { kind: 'active_days', op: '>='|'<=', n: number, window: 'week'|'month'|'year' }
  | { kind: 'all', of: Predicate[] }
  | { kind: 'any', of: Predicate[] }
  | { kind: 'not', of: Predicate };

Root is a Predicate. Recursion depth capped at 5 to prevent abuse.

## API

- GET  /api/v1/users/current/goals              -> [Goal]
- GET  /api/v1/users/current/goals/:id          -> Goal
- POST /api/v1/users/current/goals              -> Goal (create)
- PATCH /api/v1/users/current/goals/:id         -> Goal (update name/desc/spec/enabled)
- DELETE /api/v1/users/current/goals/:id
- POST /api/v1/users/current/goals/:id/toggle
- GET  /api/v1/users/current/goals/:id/progress -> {hit, progress:0..1, sub_conditions:[...]}
- GET  /api/v1/users/current/goals/progress     -> map[id]Progress (batched for dashboards)

Owner-scoped on every mutation. Predicate JSON validated against a strict schema on POST/PATCH (invalid axis, unknown kind, cycle, depth>5 -> 400).

## Frontend

- New Settings tab: Goals
- List view: table of goals with progress bar per row, enable/disable toggle, edit + delete
- Create/edit modal: composite predicate builder UI. Starts as a single 'time on axis' predicate; 'add condition' button turns it into an ALL{} wrapper; nested predicates render as indented rows with an operator (AND/OR/NOT) selector on group nodes.
- Widget catalog additions (extending the existing catalog):
  - goal-progress: one goal, radial ring
  - goal-list: all enabled goals as a compact list with mini bars
  - goal-ring: multi-goal Apple-Watch-style rings (up to 3)
- Renderer files under web/src/features/widgets/renderers/GoalProgress.tsx etc.
- Backend widgets (SVG endpoints for embed) intentionally NOT provided in v1 - goals are private by default.

## Progress evaluator

Backend Go function that walks the predicate tree:
- Leaf 'time' predicates query hb_rollup_daily with the current window's date range + axis filter, sum total_seconds.
- 'streak' evaluates the inner condition per day going back until it fails, counts consecutive hits.
- 'active_days' queries distinct days with any activity in the window.
- 'all/any/not' short-circuit as expected.
- Returns {hit: bool, progress: 0..1, sub_conditions: [per-leaf detail]}.
- Cached in last_progress with last_evaluated_at; freshness policy: 60s stale-while-revalidate for read paths, invalidated eagerly on heartbeat ingest (SaveHeartbeats invalidates goals for the owner) and on goal spec change.

## Tests (non-tautological, three layers per project convention)

Unit:
- Predicate evaluator: leaf time evaluated against seeded rollup rows returns exact expected sub-conditions.
- Composite ALL / ANY / NOT with mixed pass/fail leaves.
- Streak counts stop at first non-passing day.
- Spec validation rejects: unknown kind, unknown axis, depth>5, cycles, negative target_seconds.

Integration:
- CRUD roundtrip: POST -> GET returns the same spec; PATCH updates fields; DELETE removes.
- Owner scoping: alice can't fetch/edit/delete bob's goals (returns 404, not 403 - no oracle).
- Progress endpoint returns fresh vs cached correctly based on last_evaluated_at + heartbeat ingest.
- SaveHeartbeats invalidation: seeding a heartbeat bumps the owner's goals' last_progress to null so next read recomputes.

E2E (optional, follows session pattern):
- Playwright: navigate to Settings > Goals, create a goal via builder, see it in the list with a progress bar.
acceptance_criteria: Migration applies cleanly. All API endpoints owner-scoped and validated. Predicate builder can create simple + composite goals. goal-progress widget renders on public profile if added to layout. All three test layers green. Bead closed on merge.

title: catalyst-ui@2.5.1: fix setup.css @source path (self-relative)
description:
setup.css ships @source with a relative path that Tailwind resolves relative to setup.css itself, pointing at a nested-node_modules path that never exists. Consumer apps' JIT scan of catalyst-ui's dist silently fails, arbitrary-value utilities (Dialog centering, Sheet slide-in, Popover positioning) don't get emitted, and every Radix-styled component in every consumer app renders broken.

Fix: change 'setup.css' line 45 from '@source "../node_modules/@thebranchdriftcatalyst/catalyst-ui/dist";' to '@source ".";' — self-relative resolves to the current file's directory = dist/ = exactly what we want scanned.

Verify: boomtime + hakboard + catalyst-data-ui built against 2.5.1 should have the centering utilities in the emitted CSS without needing the belt-and-suspenders @source in their own index.css.

title: (BUG) Alpha HIGH: No rate limiting on POST /users/current/wakatime_key — Wakatime probe abuse
description:
Alpha red-team finding.

Where: internal/handler/wakatime_key.go SaveWakatimeKey (POST /api/v1/users/current/wakatime_key)

Repro:
  TOKEN=<pandax_access_token>
  for i in $(seq 1 100); do
    curl -s -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Basic $TOKEN" \
      -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/users/current/wakatime_key \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"key\":\"junk-$i\"}" &
  done; wait
Observed: all requests accepted, each triggers a real GET to https://wakatime.com/api/v1/users/current within ~20ms. No per-user, per-IP, or global throttle.

Impact:
  1. Authenticated attacker can burn boomtime's wakatime.com IP-level rate budget (429 for legit users).
  2. Enables high-volume key brute-force (attacker submits N candidate keys; a 400 vs. 204 response distinguishes valid/invalid).
  3. Amplifies boomtime into an outbound-request DDoS proxy against wakatime.com (albeit rate-limited by upstream).

Suggested fix: token-bucket (e.g. 5 saves per user per minute + 60/min global) around SaveWakatimeKey; return 429 with Retry-After above threshold.
close_reason: Closed

title: Access-token exposure window after password change (RevokeAllRefreshTokens does not touch auth_tokens)
description:
Charlie red-team run (2026-07-23).

Repro:
1. Log pandax in from two cookie jars (`-c /tmp/jar1`, `-c /tmp/jar2`). Both `/auth/login` return a 30-min `Authorization: Basic <access>` token AND `refresh_token` cookie.
2. From jar1: `POST /api/v1/users/current/password` with a valid current + new password. 204.
3. Immediately, from jar2 (which never saw the change):
   - `POST /auth/refresh_token` with jar2's cookie → 403 "expired" (correct — RevokeAllRefreshTokens deleted the row).
   - BUT `GET /auth/tokens` with jar2's OLD access token (`Authorization: Basic <TOK2>`) → **HTTP 200**, data returned normally.

Root cause: `RevokeAllRefreshTokens` only deletes from `refresh_tokens`. Access tokens (auth_tokens) issued before the change remain valid for the remainder of their 30-min TTL. `internal/db/auth.go:188-191` DELETEs only from `refresh_tokens`. `internal/handler/password.go:86-93` acknowledges this in a comment but the comment frames the trade-off as "access tokens live 30 minutes and cannot be individually revoked without breaking the caller's own session" — that argument is defeatable: you can revoke every auth_tokens row EXCEPT the one currently authenticating this request (the handler already has `tkn` from `resolveUser`).

Impact: 30-minute account-takeover window on password change. A stolen or leaked access token continues to work until natural expiry; the marquee "changing password kicks other sessions" guarantee is only true after those tokens age out.

Suggested fix: in ChangePassword, after `RevokeAllRefreshTokens`, also `DELETE FROM auth_tokens WHERE owner=$1 AND token != $2 AND token_expiry IS NOT NULL` (preserve caller's short-lived access token and never-expiring API tokens; nuke every other access token). Bonus: wrap `UpdatePassword` + revoke calls in a single transaction so partial failure can't leave the state inconsistent.

Files:
- /Users/panda/catalyst-devspace/workspace/boomtime/internal/handler/password.go
- /Users/panda/catalyst-devspace/workspace/boomtime/internal/db/auth.go
close_reason: Fixed. Added atomic DB.ChangePasswordAndRevoke (single tx: UPDATE users + DELETE ALL refresh_tokens + DELETE auth_tokens WHERE owner=$1 AND token<>callerToken AND token_expiry IS NOT NULL) — closes the 30-min access-token exposure window and the LOW atomicity gap. Caller's own access token preserved via exceptToken. Non-expiring API keys untouched. Tests: 5/5 pass including new TestChangePassword_RevokesOtherAccessTokens + TestChangePassword_AtomicOnDBError (uses SetChangePasswordFaultInjector seam). Two-jar HTTP verify: TOKEN2=403, TOKEN1=200. pandax reset to test1234.

title: Bravo HIGH: refresh_token cookie missing Secure flag; tokens stored as raw base64(uuid)
description:
Two related token-hygiene findings on the refresh flow.

1) setRefreshCookie (handler/auth.go:29-38) sets HttpOnly + SameSite=Strict but NOT Secure. If boomtime is ever fronted by plaintext HTTP (e.g., LAN dashboard), the refresh_token is sniffable and grants indefinite session issuance until token_expiry (default 24h). Fix: set Secure when cfg.PublicURL or an equivalent flag indicates https, or unconditionally set Secure and provide an opt-out for HTTP dev.

2) db/auth.go stores refresh_tokens.refresh_token and auth_tokens.token as the raw base64(uuid) value the client presents. A DB read (SQLi, leaked backup, stolen replica) yields directly usable session tokens — no offline crack needed. Standard practice: store SHA-256 of the token; compare hash on lookup. This is a common self-hosted pattern; documenting it here as a HIGH so it's not lost. Bonus: auth.ParseAuthHeader (auth.go:56-65) uses `CutPrefix("Basic")` (without a space) and TrimSpace — accepts "BasicXYZ" and "Basic	XYZ", not a security bug per se but permissive parsing that deviates from RFC 7617.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bravo HIGH: No rate limiting on /auth/login (100 attempts/2.2s served)
description: No rate limit / lockout on /auth/login, /auth/register, or /auth/refresh_token. Sent 100 failed logins from a single client in 2.245s; all returned 403 with no throttling, no exponential backoff, no captcha, no account lockout. Combined with the timing oracle (gaka-imm) and weak-password registrations (gaka-e5e), credential stuffing and password spraying are unbounded. Fix options: (a) echo v5 middleware.RateLimiter keyed on RemoteIP for /auth/*, (b) per-username failed-count table with cooldown, (c) both. Also add rate limiting to /auth/register to block mass account creation (currently unbounded — trivially unbounded).
close_reason: Closed

title: Bravo HIGH: /auth/login user-enumeration timing oracle (~10x delta)
description: handler/auth.go:57-63 Login: on GetUserByName == nil the handler short-circuits to InvalidCredentials WITHOUT running Argon2id. On a valid username with wrong password the handler runs argon2 (time=1, mem=64MiB, par=4) which dominates the response time. Measured 20 iterations each on localhost: valid-user path mean ≈10.1 ms, invalid-user path mean ≈1.2 ms — an ~8-10x delta measurable over a single unauthenticated TCP connection. An attacker can enumerate valid usernames without triggering any log signal (both paths return the same "Invalid credentials" body + 403 code). Fix: run a dummy Argon2id on a fixed dummy hash+salt when GetUserByName returns nil so both paths take equivalent time. See also auth/service.go:VerifyUserCredentials which shares the same oracle.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bravo HIGH: /auth/register accepts empty and toy passwords
description: POST /auth/register (handler/auth.go:74-101 -> auth.CreateUser) does not validate password strength. Registration with `{"password":""}`, `"a"`, or `"1234"` all return 200 + a working session cookie, and those users can subsequently log in. ChangePassword (handler/password.go:22 validateNewPassword) DOES enforce ≥8 chars + letter + digit; the same policy must be applied to Register (and probably to CreateUser for CLI parity). PoC:  `curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/auth/register -d '{"username":"weakpw_test_a","password":""}'` → 200. Impact: users with empty passwords are trivially compromised; also enables account squatting on desirable usernames.
close_reason: Fixed. Added shared unicode-aware auth.ValidatePassword in internal/auth/password_policy.go (min 8 runes + letter + digit). Wired into /auth/register and boomtime create-user CLI (new promptStrongPassword helper: re-prompts on TTY, non-zero exit on piped stdin). Curl PoC now 400s empty/short/toy passwords with a user-safe message; CLI exits non-zero. Follow-up gaka-0gu tracks deduping the ChangePassword inline check. Tests: 8-case table in internal/auth/password_policy_test.go (incl. 日本1a proving rune-vs-byte fix) + TestRegister_RejectsWeakPassword/AcceptsStrongPassword in internal/handler/auth_test.go — all pass.

title: Optimize Space-scoped dashboard queries (regex predicate → 5.5s seq scans)
description: Space-scoped dashboards are slow. The query tracer flagged 23 'db slow-query plan' WARNs in one session, ALL carrying the space regex predicate (project ~ $), each 5,268–5,577 ms. Confirmed via EXPLAIN ANALYZE: a regex membership rule (e.g. project ~ '^catalyst') can't use a btree index — on a 15-day window the planner still index-scans by (sender,time_sent) then filters (8ms), but on wider ranges it falls to a Parallel Seq Scan filtering ~416k rows (124ms for a trivial GROUP BY; ~5.5s for the real gap-sum + rename-regroup + pct/daily_pct window-function aggregation). This compounds because a dashboard fires ~11 aggregations and Space requests always take the RAW path (never the rollup — see gaka-5mo). The new date-range persistence makes a wide selection sticky, so the slow path keeps getting hit.
design: Root causes: (1) col ~ pattern is unindexable by btree → seq scan that grows with the date range; (2) Space queries skip the rollup fast path (16,180 rollup rows vs 442,377 raw) — gaka-5mo; (3) FE N+1: useSpaceMembership fires GET /spaces/:id per Space (useQueries) to build the badge index. Options, cheapest first: (A) Rollup-with-space fast path for project-axis rules (rollup stores project) — resolve the dead HasMemberOutside gate from gaka-5mo; biggest win. (B) Rewrite anchored ^literal regex rules to indexable prefix predicates (project LIKE 'literal%' or range >= 'literal' AND < 'literal￿') served by a text_pattern_ops btree index on curatable columns; keeps exact rules' = ANY() fast too. (C) pg_trgm GIN index on project/branch for general (non-anchored) regex acceleration. (D) Collapse the FE N+1 with a single GET /spaces?withRules=1 aggregate endpoint. (E) Materialize per-heartbeat space membership at ingest — O(1) scoping but heaviest; likely unnecessary if A+B land.
notes:
APPROACH: Use Claude Fable 5 to optimize this query (the full worst-case query + captured EXPLAIN plan are below — hand these to Fable 5 as the optimization target).

EVIDENCE (dev session 2026-07-10, LogHub query tracer / auto-EXPLAIN): 23 "db slow-query plan" WARNs, ALL carrying the Space regex predicate (project ~ $), each 5,268–5,577 ms. Trigger: an all-time / very wide date range (now sticky via the new range persistence) → Parallel Seq Scan over all 442,377 rows applying the regex filter, ×~11 aggregations per dashboard. A 15-day window stays on the (sender,time_sent) index (~8ms); the cost grows with the range because col ~ pattern is not index-usable.

=========================================================================
WORST-CASE QUERY (punchcard aggregation, Teak space = protecht|teak regex), dur_ms=5577
=========================================================================
-- $1 sender, $2 start, $3 end, $4 limit (minutes); $5 hide set; $6 exact members; $7,$8 regex members
SELECT
    CAST(extract(dow FROM time_sent) AS int) AS dow,
    CAST(extract(hour FROM time_sent) AS int) AS hour,
    CAST(sum(CASE WHEN gap_seconds <= ($4 * 60) THEN gap_seconds ELSE 0 END) AS int8) AS seconds
FROM heartbeats
WHERE sender = $1
    AND time_sent >= $2
    AND time_sent <= $3
    AND (project = ANY($6) OR project ~ $7 OR project ~ $8)
    AND NOT (project = ANY($5))
GROUP BY extract(dow FROM time_sent), extract(hour FROM time_sent)
ORDER BY dow, hour;

=========================================================================
CAPTURED PLAN (EXPLAIN, all-time range: time_sent >= 2000-01-01)
=========================================================================
Sort  (cost=56466.77..56669.72 rows=81178 width=80)
  Sort Key: (((EXTRACT(dow FROM time_sent)))::integer), (((EXTRACT(hour FROM time_sent)))::integer)
  ->  Finalize GroupAggregate  (cost=34939.41..46238.70 rows=81178 width=80)
        Group Key: (EXTRACT(dow FROM time_sent)), (EXTRACT(hour FROM time_sent))
        ->  Gather Merge  (cost=34939.41..43700.57 rows=67824 width=80)
              Workers Planned: 2
              ->  Partial GroupAggregate  (cost=33939.39..34871.97 rows=33912 width=80)
                    Group Key: (EXTRACT(dow FROM time_sent)), (EXTRACT(hour FROM time_sent))
                    ->  Sort  (cost=33939.39..34024.17 rows=33912 width=76)
                          Sort Key: (EXTRACT(dow FROM time_sent)), (EXTRACT(hour FROM time_sent))
                          ->  Parallel Seq Scan on heartbeats  (cost=0.00..31387.59 rows=33912 width=76)
                                Filter: ((time_sent >= '2000-01-01 00:00:00') AND (time_sent <= '2026-07-11 04:55:30') AND (sender = 'panda') AND (project <> ALL ('{Wan2GP,Chasing-Your-Tail-NG,Hermes-Function-Calling}')) AND ((project = ANY ('{developer-tools}')) OR (project ~ 'protecht') OR (project ~ 'teak')))

Related: gaka-5mo (rollup-with-space fast path unused / HasMemberOutside dead — this bead blocks on it), gaka-e0l (add axes to rollup). Verify any fix with the same tracer: a Space dashboard load should drop well under the 250ms slow threshold.

title: Cover the ingest's Validate-failure branch and the standalone-note path
description:
Two small ingest paths ship untested, both in internal/books/ingest/annotations:

1. buildFromKindle's Validate-FAILURE branch. events.Validate is proven at the
   package level (TestValidateRejectsFabricatedTimestamp), but nothing drives an
   event that violates its declaration all the way through the ingest to confirm
   the error is SURFACED rather than swallowed. That branch returns an error on
   purpose — a violation is a bug in this package, not bad input from Amazon —
   and the claim "the declaration gates what reaches the database" is only true
   if that path works.

2. The standalone-NOTE path. The notebook parser has coverage for a note with no
   highlight, but every ingest test uses highlightAt(), so kind="note" never goes
   through extract -> Validate -> rowFromEvent. annotation.note.captured is a
   registered type with its own declaration and nothing exercises it.

Both are cheap: the fake notebook seam already exists.

title: Consolidate library syncs onto the reconcile kernel + event registry
description:
The library syncs (reading_items, both kindle and audible) still upsert directly —
they do not go through internal/books/reconcile or internal/books/events. The
annotation ingest does both, and is the reference implementation.

Deliberately deferred rather than done as part of boom-siwi.5: adopting the kernel
there is behaviour-preserving ONLY while the policy stays RetireNever, and flipping
it to RetireOnCompleteFetch would mean a transient empty library page could retire a
user's whole library. That deserves its own change with its own tests, not a side
effect of the annotations work.

Work:
1. Route kindle.SyncUser + audible.SyncUser through reconcile.BuildPlan with
   Policy: RetireNever. Behaviour-identical (nothing is retired today either), but
   it makes the policy EXPLICIT and gives both syncs uniform new/missing counts for
   logging and metrics — today a book vanishing from the Amazon library is invisible.
2. Register the library events: reading.item.discovered (Time=observed,
   Confidence=observed) and reading.finished (Time=source-reported). Note
   reading.finished already exists as reading_events rows with three origin consts —
   registering it means the origins become a declared enum instead of bare strings.
3. THEN evaluate whether RetireOnCompleteFetch is safe for the library. It needs a
   completeness assertion the Cloud Reader paginator can actually make (it follows
   paginationToken to exhaustion, so it probably can) plus a floor guard — retiring
   more than N% of a library in one sweep should refuse and alert rather than
   proceed.

See docs/design/change-detection-patterns.md §7 (the per-source table) and §5.1
(the deletion rules).

title: Annotations phase 2: Audible clips + bookmarks from the AUDI sidecar
description:
Phase 2 of the annotation corpus. Phase 1 (boom-siwi.5) ships the schema, the
book_annotations table + enriched view, the query domain, the API and the UI panel —
all source-agnostic. This bead adds the Audible half underneath them.

Work:
- internal/books/connect/amazon/annotations_sidecar.go — parseAudibleAnnotations +
  FetchAudibleAnnotations(ctx, cred, asin) (anns, ok, err), ok=false for the 404 clean
  miss, mirroring FetchLastPagePosition. MUST drop audible.last_heard (it is the
  playhead — persisting it mints a phantom bookmark at the current position on every
  book) and kindle.lpr.
- Wire shape is already live-verified (boom-siwi.1): audible.clip carries
  {annotationId, startPosition, endPosition, metadata, creationTime,
  lastModificationTime}; audible.bookmark carries startPosition only.
- position_unit = 'millis' — BELIEVED, not proven. The probe renders the span so the
  magnitude can be eyeballed; the proof is a live cut compared against the liberated
  M4B, which belongs to boom-siwi.3's acceptance criteria. Storing offsets verbatim
  means being wrong costs an UPDATE of position_unit, not a data rewrite.
- Migration: add reading_items.annotations_checked_at (deliberately left out of host
  00086 / books 00006 so the MVP shipped no unused column). Both trees. Add it to the
  reading_items column list in dumpTables.
- Sweep bounding: no "which audiobooks have clips" endpoint exists, so it is one
  sidecar call per candidate. Candidate filter source='audible' AND (status IN
  ('reading','read') OR finished), plus a rotating watermark copying
  ListUnmatchedReadingItemsForMatch / SetReadingItemMatchAttempted verbatim (ORDER BY
  annotations_checked_at NULLS FIRST LIMIT $N). lastModificationTime does NOT enable
  incremental sync — it lives inside the response body, so it cannot reduce request
  count, only writes.
- New kind books-audible-annotations + a second pipeline step, alongside the Kindle ones.

title: Readwise v2 ingest: /api/v2/books + /api/v2/highlights as a books source
description:
Ingest Readwise as a books source: /api/v2/books (one row per title Readwise knows) and
/api/v2/highlights (the annotation corpus, cursor-paginated, supports updated__gt for
incremental pulls).

Blocked on boom-siwi.1: if the direct-from-Amazon probe succeeds, this drops from "the
integration" to "a supplementary source" — still worth having, because Readwise carries
highlights from surfaces we do NOT own (web articles, Instapaper, other e-readers, manual
entry), but the priority and the shape of the match logic both change.

SHAPE — mirror the Hardcover connector, which is the closest existing analogue:
- internal/books/connect/readwise/ — client.go (token auth, Authorization: Token <key>),
  pull.go (incremental by updated__gt), match.go (Readwise book -> reading_item).
- Token is a user-scoped secret: store it encrypted, same treatment as the Wakatime key
  (AES-256-GCM under BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY). GET reports {"hasSavedKey": bool} only — never
  return or log the plaintext. Add it to the rotate-encryption-key command's column sweep.
- Job kind readwise-pull with a fleet concurrency cap, registered in
  internal/books/jobs/jobs.go alongside hardcover.PullJobKind.
- New pipeline stage in internal/books/pipeline/pipeline.go. Ordering: AFTER both ingests
  (so reading_items exist to attach to) and it can run before or after Hardcover match —
  matching on ASIN does not need the Hardcover linkage.
- Migration in BOTH trees: internal/shared/db/migrations (FK to users) AND
  internal/books/db/migrations (plain owner column). Drop every boomtime_test* DB after.

MATCHING
Readwise's Kindle-sourced books carry the ASIN, which is the strong key against our
reading_items. Non-Kindle sources have title/author only — fall back to the existing
Hardcover resolve/match fuzzy path rather than writing a second matcher.

FLAG
Feature-flagged off; flag-off must be byte-identical to today.

title: Audible clips -> audio slice -> transcript: turn audiobook clips into first-class text highlights
description:
The genuinely novel piece, and the reason owning the corpus beats renting it: Audible clips
are AUDIO, not text. Readwise cannot represent them. We can, because we already liberated
the audio.

An Audible clip is a timestamp range on a title we now hold as an M4B. We already parse
Audible chapter offsets in internal/books/liberate/chapters.go and already shell out to
ffmpeg (liberate/ffmpeg.go). So the chain is:

1. Clip timestamps come from boom-siwi.1's Audible annotation probe (Fiona sidecar
   type=AUDI, or the annotations namespace).
2. Slice [start,end] out of the liberated M4B with ffmpeg — no re-download, no re-decrypt;
   the file is already on the liberation sink (internal/books/liberate/sink.go).
3. Transcribe the slice to text (whisper). Attach the transcript AS the highlight text,
   keeping the audio offsets and a pointer to the slice so the UI can play it back.
4. The result is a first-class highlight row: same table, same fusion, same publish path as
   a Kindle highlight — searchable and pushable to whatever sink boom-siwi.4 picks.

DEPENDENCIES / GATES
- Blocked on boom-siwi.1 (we need the clip timestamps before any of this is reachable).
- Only works for titles that have actually been liberated. A clip on an unliberated title
  should degrade to a timestamped stub, not an error — do not trigger a liberation from
  the transcription path.
- Transcription cost/runtime is real: this belongs on the job queue, one job per clip, with
  a fleet cap. Decide local whisper.cpp vs a hosted API and record the reasoning; local
  keeps the "your data stays yours" property that the whole liberation effort exists for.

OPEN QUESTION recorded from the session that filed this: transcribed audio snippets could
be pushed INTO Readwise so audiobook highlights join the same review loop as Kindle ones.
That is a sink decision — see boom-siwi.4.
notes:
COMPUTE PLACEMENT (raised 2026-09-07): idea was a whisper DaemonSet on talos06/talos02 using the QSV decoders.

QSV is the wrong accelerator for the transcription half. Quick Sync is a fixed-function VIDEO
codec block; whisper is transformer inference and cannot touch it. The two stages of this
pipeline want different things:
  - ffmpeg cut of the clip range out of the liberated M4B: pure AAC audio decode, a few
    seconds of CPU. QSV does not apply to audio at all.
  - whisper inference: on Intel iGPU this is OpenVINO (whisper.cpp built -DWHISPER_OPENVINO=ON)
    or SYCL/oneAPI, NOT QSV. Otherwise plain CPU with a quantized ggml model.
So the node selector should target 'has an Intel iGPU + OpenVINO runtime', and QSV device
plugin access buys nothing here.

Also prefer NOT a DaemonSet and NOT a new microservice. A DaemonSet runs one pod per matching
node whether or not there is work; this is a queue consumer. boomtime ALREADY has the right
seam: reg.SetOffload(kind) marks a job kind as drained by the KEDA scale-to-zero fleet
(k8s/overlays/talos00-knowledgedump/keda-scaledjob-jobs.yaml + BOOM_JOBS_KINDS + the postgres
trigger query), which is exactly how liberation runs today — and those pods already mount the
book library, so the M4B is local to them. Adding a books-annotation-transcribe kind with
SetOffload reuses all of it: no new service, no new deploy, no second queue.
Open question for that ticket: model size vs latency, and whether the transcript write goes
through the existing job or a callback.
CLUSTER SURVEY (2026-09-07) — the capability already exists; build nothing new.

- talos02-gpu and talos06 (exactly the two nodes proposed) each expose gpu.intel.com/i915: 10.
  The intel-gpu-plugin DaemonSet is ALREADY running in ns intel-device-plugins across 3 nodes,
  with inteldeviceplugins-controller-manager. So iGPU access is a resource request
  (gpu.intel.com/i915: 1) + a nodeSelector — no device plugin to install, no DaemonSet to write.
  Caveat: i915:10 means sharedDevNum=10, so the iGPU is shared and contention is possible.
- ns gpu-inference already runs the scale-to-zero inference pattern: ollama-gateway
  (KEDA ScaledObject, external-push, min 0 / max 1, currently 0/0), gpu-broker, svc gpu-backend,
  plus gpu-cache-reaper + gpu-instance-reaper CronJobs. Worth reading before writing anything —
  it is the house pattern for 'GPU work that should not hold a pod open'.
- boomtime ALREADY has a KEDA ScaledJob: scaledjob.keda.sh/boomtime-jobs in ns boomtime,
  postgresql trigger, max 5, auth boomtime-jobs-pg-auth. This is the offload fleet
  reg.SetOffload() feeds, and its pods already mount the book library — so the liberated M4B
  is node-local to them.

RECOMMENDATION: a books-annotation-transcribe job kind + reg.SetOffload(kind), then add
gpu.intel.com/i915: 1 and a nodeSelector for the two iGPU nodes to the boomtime-jobs ScaledJob
pod template (k8s/overlays/talos00-knowledgedump/keda-scaledjob-jobs.yaml, plus BOOM_JOBS_KINDS
and the postgres trigger query). No new Deployment, no DaemonSet, no second queue, and it
inherits the existing scale-to-zero + reaper behaviour. whisper.cpp built with
-DWHISPER_OPENVINO=ON targets that i915; QSV is irrelevant to inference.

title: Decision: highlight publish sink — Readwise (review loop) vs Notion (knowledge base) vs native-only
description:
DECISION ticket. Once boomtime owns the highlight corpus (per boom-siwi.1/.2/.3), where
does it publish?

Candidates:

READWISE — the only candidate that is both a source and a sink. Its actual value is not
storage, it is the review loop: daily review, spaced repetition, the Mastery/Readwise Reader
surfaces. Pushing INTO it (POST /api/v2/highlights, which accepts source_type/source_url and
dedupes on text+book) means audiobook transcripts and anything else we synthesize join the
same review rotation as native Kindle highlights. Cost: another bidirectional sync with the
same echo-suppression traps that boom-m5kq is currently untangling for Hardcover.

NOTION — a sink only, never a source. Cheap and expressive: page-per-book with highlights as
blocks, or a highlights database with book/author/location/date properties. Good if the goal
is a browsable knowledge base you edit by hand. Bad as a system of record — no dedupe
semantics, no incremental cursor, and hand-edits in Notion have no clean path back.

NATIVE ONLY — keep highlights in boomtime, surface them in the Books explorer, push nothing.
Zero new sync surface. Loses the review loop entirely.

DECIDE ON:
- Is the goal REVIEW (Readwise wins), BROWSING/KNOWLEDGE-BASE (Notion wins), or FUSION-ONLY
  (native wins)? These are different products, not tiers of the same one.
- One-way push or bidirectional? Hardcover's LWW experience (boom-m5kq) is the cautionary
  tale: value-based echo suppression is permanent and reverses genuine remote edits. If we
  go bidirectional anywhere, take that lesson first.
- Whichever wins, it should be a SINK behind the same seam, not bespoke code — the Hardcover
  push path (internal/books/connect/hardcover/push.go, curation_push.go) is the template,
  including the BOOM_HARDCOVER_DRYRUN-style dry-run gate on every write.

Nothing is built from this ticket. Output is a written decision (docs/design/ or an ADR) and
whatever follow-up beads it implies.

title: AUDIT-MED: commits report attributes coding time to wrong commits (no ORDER BY + dropped empty windows, positional zip)
description: 2026-09-06 audit; found independently by two auditors, verifier DOWNGRADEd to medium (read-only display report, sole caller). queries/get_time_between.sql groups by (min_date,max_date) with no ORDER BY and INNER-joins heartbeats, so a commit gap with zero heartbeats emits no row and group order is plan-dependent; stats/commits.go:81-96 zips results positionally after a reverse. One empty gap shifts every later value onto the wrong commit. Fix: unnest WITH ORDINALITY + LEFT JOIN + COALESCE(sum,0) ORDER BY ordinality, drop the Go-side reverse-and-zip.

title: AUDIT-MED: local dev stack broken in two ways — Tiltfile ghost boomtime-cache resource; BOOM_ROLE=server strands offloaded job kinds
description: 2026-09-06 audit, both CONFIRMED. (1) Tiltfile:83 declares k8s_resource('boomtime-cache') and makes boomtime depend on it, but no Dragonfly/Redis workload exists in k8s/overlays/local — the manifest went with the RabbitMQ cleanup, the Tiltfile reference did not. (2) k8s/overlays/local/patch-deployment.yaml:25 pins BOOM_ROLE=server, but local has no worker Deployment and no KEDA, so DeriveKindFilter excludes avatar-render/label-image/books-liberate-book and nothing ever claims them locally — offloaded features silently queue forever in dev. Local should run role=all (single-node fallback is the designed behavior).

title: Two pre-existing test failures on main: shared/db TestDBSuite and server TestPSlug
description:
Both fail on clean main and are unrelated to the 2026-08-27 OpenAPI work — confirmed by running them in a worktree checked out at a pre-change commit. Filing so they are tracked rather than repeatedly re-diagnosed; they were mistaken for regressions twice during that day's work.

1. internal/shared/db TestDBSuite — labels spec fails with 'late-night-coder: condition has no kind discriminant: {}' (internal/shared/db/labels_test.go:58, via ListLabels at :22). A seeded label's condition JSONB is empty where the test expects a discriminated shape. Likely seed/migration drift rather than a code defect.

2. internal/shared/server TestPSlug_InjectsOGMetaForPublicProfile — the public /p/:slug handler is not injecting og:image / og:title / og:url / og:type / twitter:card, and an unknown slug no longer keeps the generic default og:title (og_inject_test.go:55, :69). CHECK THE LIVE SITE FIRST: if this reflects real behaviour, social-card previews for public profiles are silently degraded in production, which matters more than the test.

LOWER VALUE: internal/identity failed once during a full parallel 'go test ./...' and passed 4/4 in isolation and on re-run — almost certainly test-DB contention between packages sharing the isolated-DB harness. If it recurs, look at the harness's DB isolation under parallel load.
notes:
NARROWED 2026-09-07 (first CI run of the new quality gates surfaced this on Linux too).

TestPSlug is unchanged. The shared/db suite actually had TWO failures, and one is now fixed:

1. FIXED — ListSourceHealth. 'recent := time.Now().UTC()' keeps NANOSECOND precision, but
   Postgres timestamps are MICROSECOND, so LastSeen.Equal(recent) can never hold on a value
   that round-tripped the DB. It passed on macOS only because darwin's clock commonly yields
   a zero nanosecond tail; Linux CI failed on the first run (.030410 vs .030410793). Fixed by
   truncating the fixture to time.Microsecond, which keeps the assertion exact rather than
   loosening it to a tolerance.

2. STILL FAILING — labels/ListLabels: 'late-night-coder: condition has no kind discriminant: {}'.
   What is established:
   - It is DETERMINISTIC, not a race: fails on 3/3 local runs, on a clean-HEAD worktree, and in CI.
   - A freshly migrated DB is CLEAN (0 rows with condition '{}'); only the suite's boomtime_test
     has exactly 1 (146 labels, 1 blanked). So a spec in the suite does it and does not clean up.
   - The blanked row is TEST-CREATED, not blanked-in-place: its label column is
     'late-night-coder' (the id), whereas migration 00036 seeds label='LATE NIGHT CODER'. So the
     seeded row is DELETED and a helper re-inserts a stub under the same id.
   - condition is JSONB NOT NULL with NO DEFAULT, so the '{}' was written explicitly — it cannot
     come from an INSERT that merely omits the column.
   Ruled out: dumpTables is complete for labels (condition IS listed, and the column list matches
   information_schema exactly, so it is not the boom-qs80 missing-column class); labels_test's own
   upsert spec uses throwaway id 'test-upsert-label' with cleanup; branch_padding_test's
   ensureLabelRow uses throwaway 'aw-written-<sender>' ids; awards_test's ensureLabels writes a
   VALID condition under ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; the admin create path rejects an empty condition.
   Next step for whoever picks this up: find the writer of a literal '{}' condition, or the
   DELETE that removes the seeded row — grep is exhausted, so bisect the suite by running
   ginkgo with --focus per Describe and checking labels after each.
