title: Delete the stale hand-authored OpenAPI entries — several now CONTRADICT the generated schema
description:
Since the spec started generating schemas from Go types (2026-08-27), the remaining hand-written doc.AddOperation entries in internal/shared/openapi/spec.go are the LEAST trustworthy part of the spec — and the most dangerous, because a hand-authored entry OUTRANKS the generated one. Enrichment only fills empty prose; it never overwrites text someone wrote. So a description that has drifted from the code keeps publishing, sitting right next to a schema that says otherwise.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE SPEC (https://boomtime.knowledgedump.space/api/openapi.json), all three self-contradictory today:

1. GET /api/v1/users/current/stats/ai — description: 'Per-day AI-vs-manual attribution derived from user_agent parsing (Copilot, Cursor, etc.)'. FALSE. db.GetAIActivity (internal/shared/db/ai_activity.go:56) sums ai_input_tokens, ai_output_tokens, ai_line_changes, human_line_changes and counts DISTINCT ai_session — the columns the wakatime plugin populates. There is no user_agent parsing in that query at all.

2. GET /api/v1/users/current/workouts — 200 response description is literally '{workouts:[...]}' while the generated schema alongside it is {byLabel, events, hasData}. A reader sees both and cannot tell which is real.

3. GET /api/v1/users/current/stats/health — description promises a 'workouts breakdown'; the payload is {days, hasData, totals}.

THE FIX IS DELETION, NOT EDITING. All three routes already carry accurate .Doc() prose at their registration in internal/boomtime/stats/routes.go, written by an agent that read the handlers. It is currently latent, suppressed by the stale spec.go text. Deleting those AddOperation entries lets the accurate prose through and removes a source of truth that can go stale — that is the direction this whole refactor is heading.

TWO PRECEDENTS from 2026-08-27 (78c9cc4): two entries were already deleted for exactly this reason (the avatar-prompt endpoint became an SSE stream and widget-def PATCH became a 204, while both entries still published a JSON 200). And three more declared a response body on a 204 or 101, which is impossible — that class is now stripped centrally for every 1xx/204/3xx.

WORTH DOING SYSTEMATICALLY: audit all remaining AddOperation entries for the same drift, then delete every one whose route is on the typed seam and whose prose the registration already supplies. The endpoint is a spec.go that holds only what a generator genuinely cannot recover — query parameters, security overrides, curated status-code sets, and the deliberately hand-tuned public-profile subset (which must NOT be deleted; it omits the fields widget.Scrub strips, and a test guards it).

title: Typed CachedJSON variant to unblock the ~13 stats endpoints still stubbed in the spec
description:
After the seam migration (5d16f0b) ~85 of 192 operations still emit a placeholder schema. The largest single cluster is internal/boomtime/stats, where ~13 endpoints go through apihelpers.CachedJSON(cch, logger, c, key, compute func() (any, error)). The 'any' erases the payload type at the helper seam, so neither reflection nor the typed registrar can see it — these are the heavy dashboard aggregations (bigbets x6, stats, projects, loc, leaderboards, active_files) plus admin/sources.

SHAPE OF THE FIX: a generic sibling, e.g.

  func CachedJSONT[T any](cch *cache.TTL, logger *slog.Logger, c *echo.Context, key string, compute func() (T, error)) error

or better, one that returns (T, error) so it composes with apiroute's handler signature rather than writing to c itself. The caching behaviour (TTL hit -> JSONBlob of pre-marshalled bytes) must not change; only the type must survive.

Worth doing because it is ~13 of the most-used endpoints in the app AND it is the last structural blocker. Everything after it is either genuinely non-JSON (blob/redirect/204/WS) or genuinely branch-dependent (books push/match), which are correct to leave alone.

UNBLOCKS boom-vqi7 (Go -> TypeScript): the generated client is only as good as the schema coverage, and the stats endpoints are exactly the ones the dashboard consumes.
close_reason:
Done, and went past the original scope. The typed CachedJSON problem turned out not to need a typed CachedJSON.

THE FIX WAS THE OTHER DIRECTION. CachedJSON serves PRE-MARSHALLED bytes from the TTL cache, which is the entire point of it on the heaviest dashboard aggregations. Routing those through a (Resp, error) signature would have added an unmarshal on every cache hit plus a re-marshal on the way out — taxing the hot path to satisfy documentation. Added apiroute.WritesJSON[T] instead: the handler keeps its own write, the type is DECLARED rather than enforced. Strictly worse than the normal path, strictly better than the generic object those routes carried, and the doc comment says exactly that so nobody reaches for it to dodge naming a type. All 12 stats endpoints kept their caching byte-for-byte.

FINAL NUMBERS across 192 operations (placeholder schemas / weak prose / auto summaries / no documented success): 50/91/75/2 -> 0/0/0/0. Pinned by a ratchet (internal/shared/server/openapi_quality_test.go) that names offending routes on failure, so an undocumented route breaks the build instead of appearing covered — which is how the 50 accumulated in the first place.

ALSO SHIPPED, none of it in the original ticket: .Doc() at the registration call so prose cannot drift from the route; Raw/Redirect/WebSocket forms so non-JSON routes stop being documented as JSON objects; Group registrars (an agent found that everything mounted via RegisterAdminRoutes on an *echo.Group was structurally unable to leave the stub — ~14 routes; echo's Group.Add returns the resolved path, so no prefix duplication was needed); and PUTLimit/PATCHLimit/GPUTLimit/GPOSTLimit.

FIVE HAND-AUTHORED SPEC ENTRIES WERE WRONG, not merely thin — worth knowing because a stale hand entry OUTRANKS the generated one: three declared a response body on a 204 or 101 (impossible), and two had gone stale against the code (avatar prompt is now an SSE stream, widget-def PATCH now answers 204, both still publishing a JSON 200). The bodyless-status rule is now enforced centrally for every 1xx/204/3xx rather than per entry.

Two bugs were in MY OWN ratchet, found by running it rather than trusting it: it demanded a 2xx success (flagging 11 correctly-documented WebSocket/redirect routes) and treated any slash in a summary as auto-generated (flagging 'Pause / resume a goal').

UNBLOCKS boom-vqi7 (Go -> TypeScript): schema coverage is now complete enough for openapi-typescript to generate a client that is not any-shaped.

title: Books e2e specs cannot run locally — /app/books renders 'Nothing to show'
description:
FOUND 2026-08-26 while writing the liberation e2e (boom-w20s.18). ALL books e2e specs fail locally, including the pre-existing books-explore.spec.ts which is unrelated to any current work — so this is an environment gap, not a regression.

SYMPTOM: every spec times out on locator('table') because /app/books renders the empty state: 'Nothing to show — No tracked books match your current search and filters.'

WHAT I RULED OUT:
- Data missing. seedReadingDemo silently warn-and-continues on failure (helpers.ts:213-222), and it WAS failing inside global-setup. Running it by hand works: 'Seeded reading demo for e2e-playwright-user: 41 reading_items'. Confirmed 49 rows land in the .env database (BOOM_DB_NAME=test on localhost:5432).
- Wrong backend/DB. The :8080 listener is a LOCAL boomtime process (not the tilt pod as the older note suggests), and lsof confirms it holds connections to localhost:5432 — the same Postgres the seed wrote to.
- Missing auth state. web/e2e/.auth/state.json exists and is regenerated by global-setup.

So: data present, correct database, session present, page still empty. The remaining candidates are (a) the browser session resolves to a DIFFERENT owner than the seed targeted, or (b) the Books page's default filters exclude the seeded rows. I did not chase it further.

WORTH FIXING REGARDLESS: seedReadingDemo swallows its own failure with console.warn and returns. That is why this presented as a mysterious empty page rather than a clear setup error — global-setup should fail loudly when the seed it depends on did not run, or the specs that need it should skip with a reason rather than time out on a locator.

IMPACT: books-explore.spec.ts, books-liberation.spec.ts and any future books spec are effectively unrunnable locally. They may still be green in CI if CI stands the stack up differently — worth checking before assuming they cover anything.

title: Liberation runs single-node — spread catalyst-go-jobs across the cluster
description:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while asked to give liberation '5 workers'. It got 5, but they all run in ONE process on ONE node, which is probably not what was wanted.

CURRENT REALITY:
- Liberation runs on catalyst-go-jobs, the POSTGRES-backed queue, executed in-process by the boomtime SERVER pod.
- boomtime-worker (--role=worker) consumes AMQP, and the KEDA ScaledObject targeting it triggers on the RabbitMQ queue boomtime.image-jobs (min 0 / max 4). It therefore never scales in response to go-jobs work, liberation included.
- BOOM_BOOKS_LIBERATE_CONCURRENCY is per-PROCESS parallelism. 5 means 5 goroutines in the server pod on talos06.
- Every boomtime pod currently sits on talos06 or talos02-gpu.

NODE CAPACITY ACTUALLY AVAILABLE (kubectl, 2026-08-25):
  talos00       control-plane   NoSchedule            <- genuinely unavailable
  talos01       PreferNoSchedule (memory-constrained) 11.6 cpu / 21GB
  talos02-gpu   no taints                             13.6 cpu / 62GB
  talos03       PreferNoSchedule (memory-constrained) 15.6 cpu / 13GB
  talos06       no taints                             15.6 cpu / 62GB
Four of five nodes can take work. Two are freely schedulable, two are soft-discouraged (PreferNoSchedule, so usable under pressure).

ON THE DAEMONSET IDEA (DJ's suggestion: a worker daemon per node that KEDA schedules): a DaemonSet has NO /scale subresource, so a KEDA ScaledObject cannot target one. 'Always one per node' and 'replica count varies with demand' are alternative designs, not a combination. The buildable version of the intent is Deployment + KEDA + topologySpreadConstraints.

PROPOSED:
1. Make liberation (and other heavy go-jobs kinds) runnable on the worker role, so work can leave the server pod at all. Check whether --role=worker currently drains the Postgres queue or only AMQP — the deployment comment says it is inert unless broker != inprocess, which suggests AMQP-only and is the crux.
2. Add a KEDA ScaledObject with the POSTGRES scaler over the jobs table (keda-scaledjob-jobs.yaml already establishes that pattern for avatar-render), triggering on queued go-jobs rather than RabbitMQ depth.
3. topologySpreadConstraints on the worker podspec (topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname, maxSkew 1, ScheduleAnyway) so replicas spread rather than stacking on talos06.
4. The scratch emptyDir + ephemeral-storage limits must move onto the WORKER podspec too — a worker cannot liberate into a volume it has not mounted. Same for the NFS library mount.
5. Decide the per-pod concurrency separately from the replica count once work can actually spread; 5-in-one-pod and 5-pods-of-1 have very different disk and network profiles.

CAUTION: liberation fan-out multiplies concurrent requests to Amazon's CDN. 5 in one pod is 5 connections; 4 replicas x 5 is 20. Given the 403 WAF incident on 2026-08-25, raise the aggregate deliberately rather than as a side effect of adding replicas.
close_reason:
All four phases shipped and verified in production. Phase 1: reg.SetOffload(LiberateBookKind) in the books module + library/scratch volumes and topologySpreadConstraints on the KEDA ScaledJob — liberation now fans out across nodes. Phase 2: deleted internal/boomtime/queue/imagejobs (~2266 lines); the WebSocket migration I had planned as the risky part turned out already done (the FE polls REST). Phase 3: retired RabbitMQ entirely — code, amqp091-go dependency, RabbitmqCluster, mgmt ingressroute, podmonitor, the ScaledObject and boomtime-worker; Argo pruned them all. Phase 4: deleted BOOM_QUEUE_BROKER / BOOM_JOBS_PROVIDER / BOOM_JOBS_UNIFIED rather than renaming, and deliberately did NOT add BOOM_JOB_RUNNER (a flag with one legal value is the same mistake). Plus the Grafana board rebuilt on the real metrics.

RESULT: 1012 of ~1035 titles liberated, 546.5GB on disk, DB count and filesystem agree exactly. Remainder is 20 denied + 3 podcasts (now terminal) + 5 stale rows from mid-flight pod restarts.

THINGS CAUGHT ALONG THE WAY: an env override (BOOM_JOBS_EXCLUDE_KINDS) that made SetOffload dead code; deleting base/worker broke the local overlay; and deleting patch-server-rabbit.yaml silently dropped args --role=server with it, which reverted the server to role=all and quietly undid the fan-out — found by reading the startup log rather than trusting a green rollout.

title: ConfigMap flag flips don't take effect until a manual pod restart
description:
BIT TWICE IN ONE SESSION (2026-08-25, during the boom-w20s liberation rollout), both times costing real debugging time.

boomtime reads its BOOM_* config via envFrom.configMapRef. Environment variables are materialised at CONTAINER START, so editing boomtime-config and letting Argo sync it changes the ConfigMap object while the RUNNING pod keeps its old values indefinitely. Argo reports the app Synced and Healthy the whole time, because from its point of view it is.

Symptom 1: flipped BOOM_FEATURE_BOOKS_LIBERATION to false as a kill switch while ~1040 jobs were hammering Amazon. CM said false; the pod kept draining the queue at ~250 requests/minute for several more minutes until manually restarted.

Symptom 2: flipped it back to true. CM said true, image was current, Argo green — but the HTTP routes 404'd... actually 405'd, because the liberation routes register at boot behind cfg.LiberationEnabled() and were absent, so a POST fell through to the GET-only SPA catch-all. Looked like a routing bug in freshly written code; was a stale pod env.

The 405-not-404 detail is worth remembering: for a feature-gated POST route, an unregistered route does NOT give 404 on this server, because the SPA catch-all claims the path for GET.

FIX OPTIONS:
1. kustomize configMapGenerator with a name/hash suffix, so the Deployment's podspec references boomtime-config-<hash> and any data change is inherently a new podspec -> automatic rollout. Cleanest, but renames the ConfigMap and every reference to it.
2. A checksum annotation on the pod template derived from the ConfigMap content (the Helm pattern). Needs something to compute it — Argo does not do this natively for plain kustomize.
3. Accept it and document loudly: any BOOM_* change requires 'kubectl rollout restart deployment/boomtime deployment/boomtime-worker'. Cheapest, and at minimum this should be written down wherever app-config.yaml is edited.

RECOMMEND (1). The whole point of a feature flag is being able to flip it in a hurry; a kill switch that needs a second manual step, at the exact moment you are trying to stop something bad, is not a kill switch.

Also worth checking whether boomtime could watch its own ConfigMap and hot-reload the feature gates — but note that would not have helped symptom 2, since routes are registered once at boot by design.

title: Measure Amazon's official DRM-free EPUB/PDF download coverage (cheap, do before any Kindle DRM work)
description:
Since 2026-01-20 Amazon serves EPUB/PDF directly from Manage Your Content and Devices for verified purchasers of DRM-free titles. No DRM, no port, no legal grey area.

We ALREADY mint the cookies this needs (internal/books/connect/amazon/readamazon.go exchanges the refresh_token for website cookies at www.amazon.com/ap/exchangetoken/cookies and drives read.amazon.com with them).

TASK: one cookie-auth MYCD call to measure what fraction of the library is covered. Coverage is publisher-opt-in and pre-2025-12-09 titles need the publisher to have re-confirmed status, so it is probably thin — but 'probably thin' is a guess and this is an hour to turn into a number.

WHY IT MATTERS: every DRM-free title obtained this way is one that needs none of the KFX decrypt work, none of the kfxlib conversion hole, and none of the licence exposure. If coverage turns out material, the shape of the whole Kindle epic changes. Measure before building.

Discovered during the boom-w20s Kindle liberation research (2026-08-25).

title: OpenAPI drift guard has a blind spot: feature-gated routes escape it
description:
FOUND WHILE ADDING boom-w20s.15. internal/shared/server/openapi_drift_test.go walks the ROUTER and fails when a live route is absent from the OpenAPI spec. Good guard, but it only sees routes actually REGISTERED in the test's server configuration — and a growing number of routes register conditionally behind feature flags.

Concretely: the four liberation routes (POST/DELETE /api/v1/books/items/:externalId/liberate, POST /api/v1/books/liberate/sweep, GET /api/v1/books/liberation/status) register only when cfg.LiberationEnabled() is true. In the drift test's config it is false, so the routes do not exist, so the guard passes while the spec has no entry for any of them. Same for everything behind BOOM_FEATURE_BOOKS, BOOM_FEATURE_LABEL_IMAGES, BOOM_FEATURE_GITHUB_STATS, and the OIDC routes.

Result: the guard implies total route coverage it does not have, and the gap grows with every new feature flag. Exactly the sort of test that is worse than no test if believed.

PROPOSED FIX: build the router for the drift check with ALL feature flags forced ON so the guard sees the maximal route set — a change to the TEST config, not to production wiring. Check whether any flag has a hard dependency (missing table, external service) making it unsafe to enable in a unit test; if so the guard should at minimum ENUMERATE the flags it could not enable and fail if that list grows silently.

RELATED: boom-vqi7 (generate TS types from the spec) depends on this. Generating client types from a spec whose coverage is overstated would ship confidently-wrong types for every feature-gated endpoint.
notes:
MORE EVIDENCE (2026-08-26): the blind spot is wider than one route. internal/shared/openapi/spec.go has 125 AddOperation entries and ZERO of them are books routes — the entire books domain is undocumented, and the drift guard reports success because newRouterForDrift() never registers those routes (they are feature-gated behind BOOM_FEATURE_BOOKS_* / the domain module). So the guard's two-way check is sound but its INPUT is incomplete: a route that is gated off at test time can never drift, because the guard cannot see it.

Hit this again adding GET /api/v1/books/liberation/excluded — added a route, ran the suite, 53 specs green, no drift reported. Deliberately did NOT add a one-off spec entry for it: it would be the only documented books route and still unchecked.

FIX SHAPE: build the drift router with every feature flag ON (the guard is about documentation completeness, not runtime config), or fail the guard when a known domain registers zero routes.
close_reason:
Fixed 2026-08-27 in c638283, verified live in v1.2.0-270-g15eec02.

ROOT CAUSE was the fixture, not the guard. Both the drift test and the spec's route walk built their router with a zero-value &handler.Handler{}, so every 'if h.Cfg != nil && h.Cfg.X()' predicate was false. Gated routes never registered, so the walk never saw them, so they could never drift — a route invisible to the check is not a route the check protects.

FIX: config.DocumentationFixture (every ROUTE-GATING predicate satisfied, including the COMPOUND ones — LiberationEnabled also needs BooksLibraryPath, GithubConnectEnabled also needs three OAuth values) plus server.DocumentationRouter, an enumeration-only router that is never started. 142 routes -> 193. The drift guard now checks against the full surface.

TWO NON-OBVIOUS TRAPS, both found by measuring rather than reasoning:
1. Each domain's Register reads Cfg off ITS OWN bag, not the top-level handler. Setting handler.Cfg alone still left GitHub connect and notifications hidden because identity.Register checks h.Identity.Cfg.
2. The jobs and metrics routes gate on DEPENDENCY availability (h.DB != nil), not a feature flag, so no amount of flag-setting reaches them. A nil-pool *db.DB satisfies it — registration only closes over the handle to build RequireCap middleware.

Guarded by TestDocumentationRouterIsStrictSuperset (may never LOSE a route), a route-count floor, and one representative route per gated family. Mutation-verified: blanking BooksLibraryPath fails the liberation case by name.

title: Generate TypeScript API types from the OpenAPI spec (kill hand-written FE types)
description:
GOAL (DJ): Go types -> generated TypeScript for the FEs to consume, instead of the hand-maintained response shapes in web/shared/lib/api.ts (every endpoint currently re-declares its response inline as a generic arg to request<T>, so Go and TS drift silently and only fail at runtime).

GOOD NEWS — most of the work is already done. There IS an OpenAPI 3 spec: internal/shared/openapi/spec.go, hand-authored via kin-openapi, 128 AddOperation entries, with model schemas produced from internal/model/*.go by openapi3gen (UseAllExportedFields), served at /api/docs/. And internal/shared/server/openapi_drift_test.go already fails the build when a router route is missing from the spec. So route coverage is guarded.

THE ACTUAL GAP: the drift guard proves every ROUTE exists in the spec, NOT that every operation declares a typed RESPONSE BODY. 128 operations vs 79 schema references, so a meaningful number of operations likely return an untyped/empty schema. Generating TS off the spec today would emit  for those and give false confidence.

PROPOSED SHAPE:
1. Audit response-schema coverage: which of the 128 operations lack a typed 200 body. Extend the existing drift test to ALSO fail when an operation has no response schema — same mechanism, stricter assertion. That converts this from a one-off cleanup into a guarantee.
2. Backfill the missing response schemas in spec.go (openapi3gen off the real handler return types; several handlers return anonymous map[string]any envelopes today and will need named model types first — that is the bulk of the work).
3. Codegen step: openapi-typescript over the emitted spec -> web/shared/lib/api.gen.ts. There is already an export path (internal/shared/openapi/export_test.go) to dump the spec, so this can run in CI/Taskfile without booting the server.
4. Migrate api.ts endpoint-by-endpoint from inline generics to the generated types. Incremental — both can coexist.
5. CI check that the committed api.gen.ts matches a fresh generation, so a Go model change that is not regenerated fails the build rather than shipping a lie.

WHY NOT tygo/go2ts (direct Go-struct -> TS): the spec already exists, is drift-guarded, and is the thing Swagger UI serves — a second, parallel source of truth would be strictly worse. Generate from the spec.

NOTE the domain split: books FE (internal/books/web/src) and boomtime FE (web/) both consume web/shared/lib/api.ts, so the generated types need to live somewhere both reach — and the standalone catalyst-books image must not end up needing host-only operations. Worth deciding whether the spec is split per-domain at the same time (relates to boom-ocve and boom-zp2s).
notes:
UNBLOCKED 2026-08-27. The blocker described in this ticket ('several handlers return anonymous map[string]any envelopes and need named model types first — that is the bulk of the work') is done.

State now, verified against the DEPLOYED spec at https://boomtime.knowledgedump.space/api/openapi.json: 192 operations, 0 placeholder schemas, 0 auto-derived descriptions, 0 auto-generated summaries. ~90 map[string]any literals became named response types across two agent swarms; schemas generate from Go types via openapi3gen off a typed registration seam (internal/shared/apiroute).

So step 2 of this ticket's plan is complete and step 1 is superseded — internal/shared/server/openapi_quality_test.go is a stricter guard than the one proposed here: it fails the build if ANY operation lacks a real success schema or carries generic prose, and names the offenders.

REMAINING WORK IS JUST STEPS 3-4: run openapi-typescript into web/shared/lib/api.gen.ts and migrate web/shared/lib/api.ts off its inline generics.

TWO CAVEATS FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP:
- The spec is generated with every feature flag FORCED ON (config.DocumentationFixture), so it describes the full binary surface, not one deployment. Generated types will include routes a given server 404s. That is intended.
- A handful of routes use apiroute.WritesJSON, where the response type is DECLARED rather than enforced (the handler owns the write because apihelpers.CachedJSON serves pre-marshalled bytes). Those schemas are accurate today but are not compiler-guaranteed — worth a spot-check against the handler when the generated client looks surprising.

title: Unify books data access — reading_items et al. do not belong in internal/shared/db
description:
PROBLEM: books data access is now SPLIT across two incompatible patterns and the inconsistency is the actual defect.

(a) The long-standing pattern: every books table (reading_items, reading_activity, book_sync_state, reading_events, reading_monitor) has its accessors hung as methods on the SHARED *db.DB in internal/shared/db/. That is a god-object holding one domain's queries, and it is exactly what the domain-framework epic (boom-zp2s) set out to undo — a domain cannot be lifted into the standalone catalyst-books image, or out of boomtime entirely, while its persistence lives in the host's shared package.

(b) What boom-w20s.13 introduced: internal/books/liberate/store.go holds the shared *pgxpool.Pool and owns its own SQL, keeping all liberation code inside internal/books/. Isolated as intended, but now books has TWO ways to reach the database.

DECISION REQUIRED — the ticket is only actionable once this is picked:
  1. CONVERGE ON (b): migrate the books accessors out of internal/shared/db into a books-owned store (internal/books/db or per-package stores). Aligns with boom-zp2s and makes the standalone image genuinely self-contained. Large: ~12 files of accessors plus their tests, all currently exercised against the shared boomtime_test DB.
  2. CONVERGE ON (a): move liberate/store.go's queries back onto *db.DB. Small and immediately consistent, but re-grows the god-object and moves AWAY from the domain-framework direction.

Recommendation: (1), staged — new books tables get domain-owned stores from day one, existing accessors migrate table-by-table behind an interface so the host and standalone both keep working throughout. Do NOT do it as one big-bang move; reading_items alone has 7 test files against it.

Also worth settling in the same pass: books CONFIG (FeatureBooks, AudibleSyncInterval, HardcoverSyncInterval, and the BOOM_BOOKS_* liberation vars added in boom-w20s) all live in internal/shared/config/config.go for the same historical reason and has the same smell.

Context: raised by DJ during boom-w20s.13 after seeing the deviation called out.
design: See docs/design/catalyst-domains-spike.md (Module seam) and the boom-zp2s epic. internal/books/liberate/store.go is the current example of (b); internal/shared/db/reading_items.go is the current example of (a).

title: Prod storage for the liberation library (NFS PV/PVC + mount)
description: DONE 2026-08-24. k8s/overlays/talos00-knowledgedump/audiobook-library.yaml (static NFS PV nfs://192.168.1.36/volume1/media/audiobooks, synology-nfs class, RWX, Retain + bound PVC) and patch-server-audiobook-library.yaml (mount at /media/audiobooks/liberated with subPath: liberated). Follows arr-stack-private/base/storage/synology-private-storage.yaml. Static not dynamic because the export already exists and is shared with the media servers. subPath both scopes boomtime's output and gets the dir created by kubelet, satisfying NewFSSink's must-already-exist rule without an initContainer. app-config.yaml ships BOOM_FEATURE_BOOKS_LIBERATION=false so it is inert; enabling is a one-line ConfigMap change. Verified with kustomize build. NOTE: when liberation jobs move to the worker fleet, copy the volume/volumeMount pair into the worker patch.

Naming-template editor UI with live preview; per-book path override; re-organize an existing library when the template changes; legacy AAX support via activation_bytes (pre-AAXC titles, detected by content_format in v1 and marked unsupported_format); library export to CSV/JSON (Libation's export feature); replace/upgrade-quality flow. title: HTTP: liberate endpoints on internal/books/api
description: POST /api/v1/books/items/:id/liberate (enqueue one; 409 if already in flight), POST /api/v1/books/liberate/sweep (owner sweep), GET /api/v1/books/liberation/status (counts by liberation_status + in-flight), DELETE /api/v1/books/items/:id/liberate (forget local file: clear state, optionally unlink). All behind LiberationEnabled() - 404 when off, per the existing books route gating. Design doc section 8.1.
close_reason: internal/books/api/books_liberation.go: POST/DELETE /books/items/:externalId/liberate, POST /books/liberate/sweep, GET /books/liberation/status. All gated on LiberationEnabled() so they 404 when off (the existing e2e convention). Every mutation ENQUEUES — a liberation is minutes of download plus minutes of remux and would blow any proxy timeout inline. Ownership is verified BEFORE enqueue so a bad id is an immediate 404 rather than a job failing minutes later; 409 on an in-flight run so double-clicking does not start a second 600MB download; MaxAttempts(1) because an automatic retry re-downloads the whole book. DELETE keeps the file unless ?deleteFile=true. The handler shares the SAME liberate.Service instance as the job handlers (wired via Module.RegisterJobs -> SetLiberation), so manual and swept liberations run identical code. NOTE: these routes are feature-gated and therefore escape the OpenAPI drift guard — filed as boom-i18f.

title: FE: liberation column, Liberate button, sweep confirm with size estimate
description: booksExplorerConfig.tsx: add liberation_status column + facet - nearly free because state lives on reading_items. BookDetailSheet.tsx: Liberate button + status/progress + last error. Library-wide 'Liberate all' action whose confirm dialog STATES THE ESTIMATED SIZE - a first sweep is hundreds of GB and the user should see that number before clicking. Design doc section 8.2.
notes: PARTIAL (2026-08-25). DONE: internal/books/web/src/features/books/LiberationPanel.tsx — per-book Liberate/Re-liberate/Delete-file control for the detail sheet, plus LiberateAllButton for the Books toolbar with a confirm that states the book count AND a rough GB estimate before committing a NAS to it. Availability is probed via the status endpoint (404 when the feature is off) so no feature flag needed threading through the app. api.ts client methods added. FE typecheck green. NOT DONE, and the reason: surfacing per-row liberationStatus needs the migration-00082 columns threaded through the QUERY DSL (the Books page reads rows via the DSL, not via api.getBooksItems), plus the ReadingItemDTO in web/shared/types/meta.ts and its Go producer. Until then the panel shows the ACTION and its queue feedback but not live per-book state — progress arrives via toast and Admin > Jobs. The explorer liberation_status column + facet is blocked on the same DSL work.
close_reason: COMPLETE — the DSL threading that was blocking it is done. internal/shared/query/domains.go: the reading domain's leaf projection now carries liberationStatus/liberationError/liberatedAt/audioPath/audioBytes/contentFormat, and a new liberationStatus DIMENSION is whitelisted on all three measures so it is a group-by axis and filter. liberation_status is COALESCEd to 'none' server-side in BOTH the dimension and the row column — a NULL would silently vanish from a group-by, and 'how many have I not liberated' is the question the axis mostly gets asked; the two must not disagree about the spelling. ReadingItemDTO (web/shared/types/meta.ts) gained the matching fields, so BookDetailSheet's LiberationPanel now reads live per-book state straight off the row instead of the structural casts it had. Explorer: 'Liberation' group axis + a leaf column, defaultVisible FALSE (liberation is off unless enabled, so an always-on column would be permanently empty for everyone else), sorted for TRIAGE rather than alphabetically — done > in-flight > broken > untouched. Panel also now suppresses the badge for 'none' and disables the button for 'denied' (terminal; retrying is how an account gets flagged) and shows the stored file size. 5 new FE tests incl. an unknown-future-status case so a new server-side status cannot break the column before the FE knows it. 788 FE tests green (was 783); go + query/queryapi suites green.

title: CLI: boomtime books liberate + status (with smart completion)
description: boomtime books liberate <asin|--all> [--force] and boomtime books liberation status. Per the standing boomtime-cli-smart-completion convention BOTH need dynamic completion: ASIN/title completion via dbEntityCompleter off reading_items, and enum completion for any --status filter. Wire through cmd/boomtime/completion.go's existing generator layer. Design doc section 8.3.
close_reason: internal/books/liberate_cmd.go + cmd/boomtime/books.go. 'boomtime books liberate [ASIN] --user U [--all] [--limit N] [--force]' and 'boomtime books liberation-status --user U'. Commands live in internal/books (like dedup_reads.go) so the admin CLI-runner can introspect + invoke the same defs in-process, and both carry climeta class annotations (liberate=mutating — it only ever ADDS to the library; status=readonly). Per the standing smart-completion convention BOTH wire dynamic completion: --user via climeta.CompleteUsernames, and the positional ASIN via a DBEntityCompleter over ListUnliberatedASINs (deliberately NOT user-scoped — completion runs before --user is necessarily known, and a superset beats nothing; capped at 200). Runs INLINE unlike the web endpoints, which is documented as making it right for a one-off and wrong for a whole library over SSH. The disabled-feature error NAMES which of the three gate terms is missing rather than just saying 'disabled'. ffmpeg absence is a hard immediate error here (a person is watching a terminal) rather than the logged warning the job wiring uses. 4 tests: argument guards, completion+annotation wiring, humanBytes, orNone.

title: Chapters + tags + cover art from data we already hold
description: chapters.go: flatten nested content_metadata.chapter_info.chapters[] (chapter_titles_type Tree) depth-first -> ffmetadata file (TIMEBASE=1/1000, START/END/title). Honour is_accurate + brandIntroDurationMs/brandOutroDurationMs - Audible offsets can include branding segments. tags.go: title, subtitle, authors, narrators, series+sequence, release date, publisher, genre from category ladder, description - ALL already in reading_items.raw_meta from the library sweep, so NO extra Amazon call is needed for tagging (a real simplification over Libation, which re-fetches). notes: LIVE-VERIFIED CONSTRAINT (2026-08-24): chapter_titles_type=Tree does NOT guarantee nesting. A 37-chapter title came back entirely FLAT (0 nested children). The flatten must handle both shapes and must not assume depth. Brand offsets are real and non-zero (intro 3924ms, outro 4945ms) with is_accurate=true, confirming chapter offsets are measured from the start of the file INCLUDING the Audible intro — so the branding case in design doc 2.5 is live, not hypothetical.
close_reason: chapters.go + tags.go. CHAPTERS: flatten handles both shapes per the live finding that Tree does NOT guarantee nesting; leaves only (emitting parents too would overlap), part title prefixed onto children; boundaries REPAIRED from the next chapter's start because Audible's length_ms is not always trustworthy and ffmpeg rejects END<=START; ffmetadata escaping for =/;/#/backslash/newline since titles are Amazon-supplied. Audible offsets emitted UNMODIFIED — they already include the brand intro, so 'correcting' them would desync every mark. TAGS: MetadataFromRaw reads reading_items.raw_meta, so liberation needs ZERO extra Amazon calls (Libation re-fetches; we don't have to because ingest already persisted it). Genre = deepest category ladder rung; cover = numerically largest product_image; series index zero-padded so lexical dir order matches reading order; album=series when present else title. INTEGRATION TEST runs REAL ffmpeg+ffprobe: muxes our ffmetadata into a container and reads the chapters back, proving the document is genuinely valid rather than just self-consistent.

title: boomtime-worker Deployment claims scheduled jobs (reading-monitor) and orphans them on KEDA scale-down
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the reading-monitor orphan churn. The KEDA-scaled boomtime-worker Deployment (--role=worker, k8s/base/worker/deployment.yaml) has NO BOOM_JOBS_KINDS include-filter, so its jobs provider claims scheduled kinds like books-reading-monitor from the shared jobs table. When KEDA scales it 1->0 while idle, any such in-flight job is orphaned (status=running with a dead pod). The reaper (986b9cb/90ba995) now self-heals these in <=2min (reclaimed->queued->re-run on the always-on server), so it's bounded + non-urgent, but it causes needless churn + ~2min latency per orphan.

FIX (careful, live GitOps): give the boomtime-worker Deployment a strict BOOM_JOBS_KINDS include-filter of ONLY the kinds it should handle (the AMQP/image kinds it 'consumes' — confirm which: avatar-render/label-image), matching the intended design at main.go:909 ('the always-on server excludes heavy kinds; a ScaledJob includes them'). Then reading-monitor/hardcover/audible/etc are only ever claimed by the always-on server and never orphaned by scale-down. Verify against the existing keda-scaledjob-jobs.yaml (which correctly sets BOOM_JOBS_KINDS=avatar-render) — the boomtime-worker Deployment appears to be a separate workload missing the equivalent filter. Do NOT break image-job processing; confirm what the worker must handle before restricting.
close_reason: Fixed in c8fcdfc: worker/server kind-filter now DERIVED from the registry offload set (SetOffload/OffloadKinds + jobs.DeriveKindFilter). Worker claims only [avatar-render,label-image]; every other kind is server-resident by default so it can't be orphaned by a worker scale-down. Deployed + verified live (server log: role=server exclude=[avatar-render,label-image]). Env override retained as escape hatch; zero k8s manifest change.

title: cache/persist generated social cards, regen daily
description:
og.png currently renders live every request (buildSocialCardData DB queries + resvg) with only Cache-Control max-age=60 → crawlers re-render constantly. Cache the rendered PNG, refresh ~daily.

RECOMMENDED: Redis/Dragonfly blob cache. Key og:card:v1:<username> → PNG bytes, SETEX 24h ('regen daily' = TTL). Miss → render, store, serve. DEL on card edit (theme/tagline/enable) for instant refresh. Graceful fallback to live render when Redis absent (local inprocess). Bump Cache-Control to hours + add ETag. No migration, no backup bloat, shared across replicas, auto-expiring.
ALT: DB bytea blob — persistent but bloats every DB backup (gaka-awh.3 includes user cols) and would need a daily worker to refresh.
FOLLOW-UP (optional): daily worker warm-up that pre-renders all enabled public cards so the first crawler after expiry never eats a cold render.
close_reason: LIVE + verified in prod. App passthrough cache (844f639) + talos00 overlay env (3591fdb) + talos-homelab scoped-user/bucket (landed in f1f8cd1, flux-synced). Provisioned boomtime-cards bucket+user, reflected secret into ns boomtime, restarted server. og.png verified X-Card-Cache miss→hit, same ETag, no minio errors. Layering: Cloudflare 10min edge → app → S3 24h durable → render. Invalidate-on-edit wired. Daily regen = lazy 24h TTL (warm-up deferred).

title: OIDC web session too short (10-min id_token expiry) — extend or auto-refresh
description: oidc_sessions.id_token_expiry is set from the id_token exp = ~10 min (Authentik provider), so the OIDC web session expires every 10 minutes -> user re-auths constantly (and likely contributes to reload/429 churn). FIX options: raise the id_token/access_token validity on the Authentik boomtime provider (blueprint), and/or make /auth/refresh_token OIDC-aware to rotate+extend the oidc_session (re-check id_token via the stored hashed_refresh) instead of only minting a bearer.
design: QUICK BUMP DONE + LIVE (2026-08-05): raised the boomtime Authentik provider access_token_validity 10m->12h (talos-homelab c542cc1, Flux reconciled, worker restarted, blueprint re-applied, provider verified access_token_validity=hours=12). New OIDC web sessions now last 12h instead of 10m. REMAINING (the proper fix, keep this bead open): make boomtime's /auth/refresh_token OIDC-aware — use the stored oidc_sessions.hashed_refresh to silently mint a fresh id_token + rotate the session, so we can keep a SHORT id_token (better security) with a seamless long-lived session. Until then the 12h bump is the pragmatic relief.
close_reason: Proper fix shipped (d58d937): /auth/refresh_token is now OIDC-aware — provider refresh stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM), refresh-grant + re-verify rotates the session in place, best-effort fallback to the still-valid session. title: [MEDIUM] Stale link-intent + persistent oidc_state cookie → cross-account identity link on shared browser
description: oidc.go LinkOIDC/CallbackOIDC link-branch: putLinkIntent(state->initiatorUsername) captured at START, never re-verified at callback; oidc_state cookie (Path=/, MaxAge 600) NOT cleared on boomtime logout. On a shared/kiosk browser: A starts link → logs out → B logs in → callback completes state S → takeLinkIntent=A → HandleLink binds B's Authentik identity onto A's account. FIX: in CallbackOIDC link-mode, re-identify the current session cookie and require it == takeLinkIntent username before HandleLink; clear oidc_state on logout; shorten intent TTL.
close_reason: FIXED. Root correction: the session cookie is SameSite=Strict so it is NOT sent on the cross-site callback from Authentik (that's WHY linking uses the server-side intent map) — re-checking the session at callback would break legit linking. Correct fix: Logout now clears oidc_state + oidc_nonce cookies (clearOIDCFlowCookies) on BOTH branches, so an abandoned in-flight link on a shared/kiosk browser can't be completed by a different user after logout+relogin (no state cookie -> callback CSRF fails -> stale intent never consumed). Also putLinkIntent now reaps expired intents on every insert (bounds the map -> closes the authenticated memory-exhaustion DoS, which was also the linkIntents-janitor nit in .19). Suite 33/0.

title: [MEDIUM] ProvisionOIDCUser + /auth/register do zero username validation (control chars, cache-key '|' delimiter collision)
description: db/oidc.go:163-194 inserts claims.PreferredUsername verbatim as a boomtime username — no charset/length/NFC normalization anywhere (grep-confirmed). A self-service Authentik lets an attacker mint usernames with control chars, whitespace, 'admin' homoglyphs, or the cache-key delimiter '|'. apihelpers.CacheKey builds 'owner|name|...' — a username with '|' can collide another user's cache namespace → cross-user cached-payload leak. Pre-existing for local /auth/register too. FIX: validate/normalize usernames (allowlist charset [a-zA-Z0-9._-], max len, NFC) on BOTH provisioning and registration before insert.
close_reason: FIXED. New auth.ValidateUsername: 1..64 chars, ASCII allowlist [A-Za-z0-9._-] (rejects '|' cache-key delimiter, whitespace, control chars, non-ASCII/homoglyphs), no leading/trailing . or -. Wired into BOTH the local Register handler (before CreateUser) and OIDC resolveOrProvision (before ProvisionOIDCUser -> 400). Gates NEW username creation only; existing users never re-validated (behavior-preserving). Closes the cross-user CacheKey('owner|name|...') namespace-collision vector. Unit test TestValidateUsername (valid + 11 invalid cases + length bounds). Suite 33/0.

title: [MEDIUM] OIDC nonce generated but never verified (spec violation; replay defense absent)
description: oidc.go:76,110 mint a nonce + AuthCodeURL sends it (Authentik stamps id_token), but it's never stored (not in state cookie/server-side) and exchangeAndVerify (oidc_resolver.go:122) never compares idToken.Nonce. go-oidc does NOT auto-check nonce. state CSRF + TLS code-exchange mitigate most token-injection, but nonce is the OIDC-core-required belt-and-suspenders vs id_token substitution/replay. Applies to login AND link flows. FIX: persist nonce alongside state (2nd HttpOnly cookie or signed state / linkIntent), assert idToken.Nonce==expected in exchangeAndVerify.
close_reason: FIXED. LoginOIDC/LinkOIDC set an oidc_nonce cookie (Lax, alongside oidc_state); CallbackOIDC reads+clears it and threads it to HandleCallback/HandleLink -> exchangeAndVerify asserts idToken.Nonce != '' AND == expectedNonce (fail-closed on empty/mismatch/missing cookie). go-oidc doesn't check nonce itself; this closes the OIDC-core-required id_token substitution/replay defense. Mock fixture bakes the nonce; new spec 'rejects an id_token whose nonce does not match' (401 on wrong nonce AND on empty expected). Suite 33/0.

title: OIDC-aware /auth/refresh_token (don't re-mint a local session over an OIDC cookie)
description: Under BOOM_AUTH_PROVIDER=oidc, the SPA silent-refresh calls POST /auth/refresh_token, which resolves the OIDC session cookie -> owner, then mkTokenData + CreateAccessTokens + setRefreshCookie — MINTING a local refresh_tokens session and OVERWRITING the OIDC session cookie. Next OIDCResolver.ResolveCookie looks in oidc_sessions for the (now local) token -> miss -> 401; also leaves stray auth_tokens rows for OIDC-provisioned users (hit this during akadmin cleanup: users delete blocked by auth_tokens_owner_fkey). Fix: RefreshToken handler must be OIDC-aware — either refresh/extend the oidc_session (re-issue an opaque id bound to the same user, or no-op and let the cookie stand until id_token expiry) instead of minting a local session, OR have the FE skip the refresh loop under provider=oidc. Detect via auth.CurrentResolver().ProviderName()=='oidc'.
close_reason: Superseded by gaka-93f.14, which elevates this from a UX bug to a HIGH security finding (session-type confusion: OIDC refresh mints an unrevocable standalone local token that survives id_token expiry + IdP deprovision). Track + fix there.

title: Investigate dual-DB accessor: read-replica without heavy indices for free-tier users
description:
Free-tier users don't need the full-power query plan the paid tier gets. Right now we're serving everyone through the same trigram-indexed / rollup-materialized-view stack, which is over-optimized for the free-tier ceiling.

## Motivation
- Free tier is a loss leader. Serving them the same p50 latency as paid users burns disk + IOPS on the trigram indexes and rollup refreshes. Payment gating should let us route them to a cheaper query path.
- OIDC + payment work (gaka-0oe epic) is the natural time to plumb this — user tier is known at auth time, so an adapter layer can route the connection pool at that boundary.

## Sketch (needs design)
- Postgres primary keeps all the indexes (trigram, GIN, materialized rollups). Paid-tier reads route here.
- Read-replica (logical replication) drops the trigram indexes + heavy rollup refresh schedule. Free-tier reads route here.
- A DB adapter interface — call it db.Reader — implemented by two structs (indexedReader / lightReader). Handler resolves user → tier → picks reader.
- Writes still go to primary regardless of tier (Wakatime ingest + settings).
- Time-window queries on lightReader use raw heartbeats + on-the-fly aggregation instead of hb_rollup_daily. Slower (2–20x) but bounded to small windows (last 7 days).

## Open questions to answer before implementation
- Where does the tier decision live? auth middleware? handler resolveUser? both?
- What's the free-tier query ceiling (max window, max heartbeat count) before we degrade to 429 / paywall?
- How do we handle a user upgrading mid-session — connection pool churn? cached query results?
- Do the write path stats (rollup refresh trigger) need to be tier-aware?
- Physical replication vs logical — replication lag budget for a chart that reads 'today so far'?
- Do we bill by query-cost (Postgres pg_stat_statements) or by user-tier flat rate?

## Depends on
- gaka-0oe: user tier + OIDC integration (must land first — no tier concept without it)
- gaka-0oe.14: OIDC provider survey

## Deliverable for this bead
Design doc + POC harness (single test showing db.Reader interface routing to two connection pools with a tier flag). Not a full implementation. Then split into 3–5 sub-beads for schema, adapter, handler wiring, tier-aware caching, and the ops story (replication setup, monitoring, alert on lag).

title: Fix: rollup COALESCE fallback 'Other' collides with capWithOther bucket name
description:
Symptom: user-visible pie chart + widget cards show 'Other' consuming 55%+ of language / editor / platform charts. Looks like capWithOther is broken. It's not.

Root cause: internal/db/ingest.go:263 rolls heartbeats into hb_rollup_daily via:

  coalesce(project, 'Other'), coalesce(language, 'Other'), coalesce(editor, 'Other'),
  coalesce(platform, 'Other'), coalesce(machine, 'Other'),
  coalesce(category, 'Other'), coalesce(plugin, 'Other'), coalesce(branch, 'Other')

Heartbeats with NULL axis fields (AI console with no file open, editor sessions without recognized extension, plugin-less clients) show up as REAL rollup rows with axis-value='Other'. When stats.ToStatsPayload groups by language, this synthetic-string 'Other' bucket accumulates ALL null-language time — which for AI-heavy sessions can be 50%+ of total heartbeats.

capWithOther (internal/stats/segment.go:267) creates a DIFFERENT bucket named 'Other (N more)' with OtherCount > 0. The topEntries filter in widget/render.go:134 skips those correctly. But it CANNOT distinguish the ingest-COALESCE 'Other' from a real language named 'Other' — the OtherCount marker is what tells them apart.

## Fix options

1. Rename ingest COALESCE fallback per-axis:
   - language → 'Unknown' or '(untagged)'
   - editor → 'Unknown' or '(none)'
   - etc.
   - Requires migration: UPDATE hb_rollup_daily SET language='Unknown' WHERE language='Other' — but that would also nuke rows for a real user-project literally named 'Other'. Need pre-check via COUNT (LANGUAGE == 'Other' AND ... is rare enough to migrate safely with a warning banner).

2. Add a nullable-marker column (`is_missing_axis_X BOOLEAN`) so aggregation can distinguish "user literally coded in something called Other" from "no data".
   - Schema churn, per-axis columns bloat rollup table.

3. Store NULL in rollup (no COALESCE) and handle nulls in stats.ToStatsPayload / capWithOther. Group by (COALESCE NULL to '' for grouping key) then rename '' → '(untagged)' at serialization.
   - Cleanest semantically. Requires rewriting the rollup query + stats aggregation.

## Recommended: option 1 with '(untagged)' — reads clearly in tooltips, unambiguously distinguishes from any user-typed name (parens hint it's a synthetic marker).

## Interaction with capWithOther
Once the collision is resolved, capWithOther's 25% ceiling still applies to its synthetic 'Other (N more)' bucket. So the pie will show ACTUAL breakdown of real languages plus an '(untagged)' slice sized to whatever fraction of the user's heartbeats came in without a language.

## Second-order: high (untagged) fraction is a signal to fix language detection
If a user's chart shows 40% '(untagged)', that's a diagnostic that the language field isn't being set on their Wakatime client — worth surfacing in the UI ("40% of your time isn't tagged with a language — check your editor plugin config").

## Files touched
- internal/db/ingest.go — rename COALESCE fallback per axis
- internal/db/migrations/000XX_axis_untagged_rename.sql — one-time UPDATE
- FE: no change (labels flow through as strings)
close_reason: Same root cause as gaka-J1n; superseded by gaka-6ci.

## Functionality Surface

- SaveWorkouts — atomically inserts heartbeats(ty='workout')+workout_details (HR series + route JSONB), refreshes rollup + gaps
- GetHealthActivity(t0,t1) — merges workouts (from heartbeats) + rollup stats per day, aggregates for range
- GetWorkouts(t0,t1) — lists workouts + per-label aggregate (count/totalMin/kcal/avgHR)
- summariseDays — averages HR across days where AvgHR > 0 only (no /0)

## Domain Invariants
- OWNERSHIP ISOLATION: all 4 public fns bind by owner; no cross-owner leak
- Idempotency: replayed syncs of same samples don't double-insert
- Rollup determinism: refresh 2x with same input → bit-identical rows (no float drift)
- Workout-sample FK resolution: bogus UUID → NULL workout_id, no error
- Half-open time window: [t0, t1) semantics on GetHealthActivity + GetWorkouts
- summariseDays: 0-HR days excluded from average (no /0)

## Testing Pyramid

### Unit (pure logic, no DB)
- sortStringsAsc: unsorted → sorted, empty → empty, single → unchanged
- summariseDays: 0 days → zeros; 1 day HR=0 → hrCount=0; 3 days [70,80,90] → AvgHR=80 exact; mixed nulls → only non-zero counted

### Integration (real DB)
- SaveHealthSamples:
  - Roundtrip 10 samples → 10 rows
  - Idempotency: re-insert same set 3x → still 10 rows
  - Cross-owner: A+B samples → List(A) only A's
  - Rollup: 1 day sleep+HR → 2 rows in health_rollup_daily with correct kind/aggregates
  - Workout FK: valid UUID → workout_id matches heartbeat.id; bogus UUID → NULL
  - Boundary: ts_start=1000, since=1001 → excluded

- SaveWorkouts:
  - Atomic: 3 workouts → 3 heartbeats + 3 workout_details, all-or-nothing
  - IDs assigned: 5 workouts → 5 non-null unique IDs in input order
  - HR series: workouts with hr → hr_series is valid JSONB array; without → NULL (not "[]")
  - Rollup refresh: workouts on 2 days → hb_rollup_daily updated for both

- GetHealthActivity:
  - Day merge: 2 workouts day1 + 5 samples day1+day2 → 2 HealthActivityDay entries merged by "2006-01-02"
  - Workout aggregate: 3 workouts same day → Workouts=3, WorkoutMinutes=SUM/60, ActiveKcal=SUM
  - Sample aggregate: HR [70,75,80] → day.AvgHR=75; multi-day [75, 85] → range.AvgHR=80
  - Boundary: t0-t1 exclusive on t1 (half-open)
  - Empty range: HasData=false, zeros

- GetWorkouts:
  - List sort: newest first (time_sent DESC)
  - ByLabel grouping: A(60s+90s)+B(120s) → A(count=2,totalMin=2.5), B(count=1,totalMin=2), sorted totalMin DESC
  - Cross-owner: 0 rows
  - HR averaging: 2 workouts with HR → mean of non-zero; 1 workout no HR → 0 (no /0)

### E2E
- POST /health_samples → 202 accepted=1, sample in DB
- POST /health_samples.bulk 50 → 202 accepted=50, rollup computed
- POST /workouts → 201 with ID
- POST /workouts.bulk 10 → 202 with 10 unique IDs

## Acceptance Criteria
- Coverage 90%+
- Named invariants: ownership_isolation, idempotency, rollup_determinism, fk_safety, half_open_window
- Edge cases: empty payload, cross-owner, boundary timestamps, NULL fields

## Anti-tautology notes
BAD: insert qty=[10,20,30]; Aggregate.total==60 (re-runs the SUM)
GOOD: insert qty=[10,20,30]; assert count==3 AND max∈[29.9,30.1] AND min∈[9.9,10.1] AND total∈[59.5,60.5] — bounded invariants catch silent drops/dupes without re-implementing sum
BAD: Insert workout; ID>0
GOOD: Insert 5 workouts; IDs=[a,b,c,d,e] all unique in input order, all retrievable by ID

Est effort: 6 hours
close_reason: 89.0% coverage on health.go (up from 0%). 40+ tests pinning: idempotent-dedup, cross-owner isolation, tz-aware rollup, FK safety, half-open time-window semantics. **Caught production bug**: ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT idx_health_samples_dedupe was invalid (UNIQUE INDEX not CONSTRAINT); every Apple Watch sample save was silently 500ing. Fix + tests committed a677586.

title: Test coverage: internal/db/dashboard_layouts + widgets + widget_defs (16 fns, 0%)
description:

- widgets.go: 7 fns (Create/Get/List/Roll/RecordHit/ProjectExists/MemberSet)

- ListWidgetLinks(user)

### widget_defs (handler/widget_defs.go)

- GetWidgetDef(id) → owner, WidgetDef, ok — public renderer
- GetWidgetDefByName(user, name)
- ListWidgetDefs(user)

- Widget scope referential integrity: CreateWidgetLink validates project+space existence in handler layer
- No cascade between widget_defs and widget_links (orthogonal)
- SetDashboardLayout is byte-preserving JSONB roundtrip (gaka-25r pattern)
- UpdateWidgetDef is REPLACE-ALL of spec (no partial)
- Delete is idempotent (2x delete = 2x no-error)
- RecordWidgetLinkHit caps origins at 20 by LastSeen DESC

## Testing Pyramid

### Unit
- None (pure IO)

### Integration (real DB — 90% of coverage source)
- Cross-owner isolation across ALL three files:
  - A creates widget_def "MyDef" → B GetWidgetDef(uuid) returns ok=false OR owner!=B
  - A creates widget_link → ListWidgetLinks(B) doesn't include it
  - A SetDashboardLayout("public_profile") → B Get returns (nil,false)
- Referential check on link creation: nonexistent project/space → error
- Orphan tolerance: create link on project X, delete X → link still lists (no cascade)
- Byte-preserving JSONB roundtrip: SetLayout(`{"cols":12,"widgets":[{"i":"card","x":0}]}`) → Get returns byte-identical
- Upsert idempotence: Create widget_link twice → same UUID (deterministic on user+scope)
- Last-write-wins: SetLayout L1; SetLayout L2 → Get returns L2
- Empty layout → error
- Unique constraint: CreateWidgetDef(A,"Card") twice → 2nd fails
- Update semantics: Create+Update+GetByName returns new spec

- RecordWidgetLinkHit caps: 21 origins in → 20 stored (drop oldest by LastSeen)
- RecordWidgetLinkHit on bogus link_id: no-op no-error
- Delete idempotence: DeleteDashboardLayout twice → no error both
- Scope type CHECK constraint: CreateWidgetLink with "invalid_scope" → schema rejects

- Full HTTP CRUD for dashboard_layouts (413 on >4KiB, 400 on unknown scope, 204 idempotent delete)

- Coverage 90%+ across all 3 files
- Every named invariant pinned
- Edge cases: empty IDs, malformed JSON, concurrent RecordWidgetLinkHit racing origin-cap

BAD: Create+Get+Equal
GOOD: Create widget W for user A → assert user B's List does NOT contain W (pins isolation)
BAD: Update+Get returns new value

title: Test coverage: internal/db/award_ledger (LogAwards/List/Streaks, 0%)
description:
Coverage 0%. Untested: LogAwards (line 120), ListAwardLedger (182), GetLabelStreaks (244), and pure helpers KindDefaultPeriod, ResolvePeriod, PeriodBounds, periodStepBackward.

## Functionality Surface
- LogAwards(ctx, username, items, tz, at) → INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING per (username, label_id, period_start); called by handler/awards.go:90, awards_eval.go:71, awards_backfill.go
- ListAwardLedger(ctx, username, labelID, limit) → JOIN labels for name+kind, ORDER BY period_start DESC, label_id ASC; handler/awards.go:138
- GetLabelStreaks(ctx, username, tz, at) → per-label streak length; skip if no current-period entry (line 289-291); handler/awards.go:175
- Helpers (pure): PeriodBounds (tz-aware daily/weekly/monthly), periodStepBackward (one period earlier)

## Domain Invariants
- Idempotent upsert on PK (username, label_id, period_start) — repeated same-period calls are no-op
- Lifetime labels silently dropped in LogAwards; server-side eval filters them (awards_eval.go:65)
- ListAwardLedger scoped by username; joined labels allows NULL for deleted labels (COALESCE)
- Streak requires current-period entry — Monday-fired label returns 0 if queried Wednesday
- Timezone-aware period computation: UTC day-flip must not break Pacific streaks
- FK CASCADE deletes ledger rows on user or label removal
- Deterministic ordering: period_start DESC, label_id ASC (line 205)

## Testing Pyramid

### Unit (pure logic)
- PeriodBounds: exact-midnight in user tz, ISO Monday (not UTC Sunday), leap year, DST transition
- periodStepBackward: daily=-1d, weekly=-7d, monthly=-1 month (not ±30 days)
- KindDefaultPeriod: tier/tribe=lifetime, archetype/meme=weekly, patch=daily, unknown=weekly
- ResolvePeriod: perLabel override wins over kind default

### Integration (real DB, OpenIsolatedDB)
- Insert round-trip: LogAwards+ListAwardLedger contains item
- Idempotent upsert: LogAwards(u,[x])+LogAwards(u,[x]) → 1 row, second written=0
- Duplicate in same call: LogAwards(u,[x,x]) → 1 row (dedup semantics)
- Lifetime silently dropped: LogAwards(u,[{PeriodType=lifetime}]) → empty ledger, written=0
- Per-user scoping: alice+bob → ListAwardLedger("alice") returns ONLY alice's
- Streak empty: no rows → []
- Streak active: row for today, at=today+1h → count=1
- Streak inactive on gap: day1+day2, at=day4 → count=0 (not 2)
- Streak consecutive: N periods → count=N, walk hits all N
- Timezone-aware: 11pm UTC = 3pm Pacific same day → period_start = midnight Pacific, not UTC next day
- List order: 3 rows different period_start → newest first, tied label_id ASC
- Label filter: ListAwardLedger(labelID=y) returns only y
- Default limit: 501 items → 500 returned max
- FK cascade: DeleteUser("alice") → alice's ledger rows gone

### E2E
- POST /awards/log → persists AND response echoes ledger row joined with label
- GET /awards/streaks → flat map {L1: N} format
- GET /awards/ledger?label=L1&limit=10 → filtered + limited

## Acceptance Criteria
- Coverage 90%+
- Each invariant has a named test
- Edge cases: empty ledger, deleted user cascade, concurrent inserts, UTC/DST boundaries

## Anti-tautology notes
BAD: LogAwards(x); Get()==x
GOOD: LogAwards(a); LogAwards(b); List() has EXACTLY 2 (no drop AND no dupe)
BAD: streak count += 1 in loop, trust
GOOD: N consecutive → count=N AND next gap breaks walk (proves gap detection)
BAD: PeriodBounds only on UTC
GOOD: PeriodBounds on UTC AND Pacific across DST (proves tz param matters)

Est effort: 5 hours
close_reason: 92.3% coverage on award_ledger.go (up from 0%). 25 tests pinning: kind→period default mapping, override precedence, tz-aware period bounds (UTC + Pacific + DST edge), monthly=calendar-not-30-days, streak-active-requires-current-period, streak-breaks-on-gap. Committed 85555fb+4944055.

title: [DRY audit] Consolidate ginkgo test helpers after migration lands
description:
Runs AFTER gaka-0vp-17 (kill switch) closes with only ginkgo suites
on main. Systematic DRY sweep across all 22 migrated packages.

## Target patterns to extract

Based on the recurring shapes we hit during the parallel-migration
sweep, the following should get shared helpers instead of copy-pasted
per-package boilerplate:

### 1. Suite entry file (22 near-identical files)
Every package has:
  func Test<Pkg>Suite(t *testing.T) {
      RegisterFailHandler(Fail)
      RunSpecs(t, "<pkg> suite")
  }
Options:
- Leave as-is (idiomatic; ginkgo docs recommend one per package)
- Codegen via go:generate + a tiny script that stamps the file per package (probably NOT worth it — 22 files, 5 lines each = 110 lines)

Recommend: LEAVE. Each suite is 5 lines; centralizing would fight ginkgo's model.

### 2. Env save/restore helper (config, auth, several handler tests)
The setenv/DeferCleanup pattern is duplicated. Extract:
  package testutil
  func WithEnv(k, v string) // uses ginkgo.DeferCleanup internally
  func ClearEnv(keys ...string) // save all, register restore

Ship as: internal/testutil/env.go (ginkgo-aware).

### 3. HTTP harness setup (handler tests — very repetitive)
Every handler test does:
  hz := testutil.NewHarness(GinkgoT())
  e := hz.Router()
  user, token := hz.MintUser("prefix")

Extract a BeforeEach-friendly builder:
  hz, e, user, token := testutil.MintedHarness("prefix")
Or a "context" helper:
  ctx := testutil.NewHTTPContext(GinkgoT(), "prefix")
  ctx.MintUser(); ctx.Router(); ...

### 4. JSON response assertion helper
Most handler tests do:
  var out T; require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &out))
  assert.Equal(t, want, out.SomeField)

Extract:
  func Decode[T any](rec *httptest.ResponseRecorder) T
  func ExpectJSONStatus(rec, want int) // Fail with body dump on mismatch

### 5. Common gomega custom matchers (worth building)
- ContainAwardID(id string) — for the labels tests
- HaveHeader(name, value string) — for response-header asserts
- BeAJSONResponseOf(shape any) — decode + shape check in one

## Success criteria

- ≥20% LOC reduction across the test tree (currently ~25k LOC of tests → target ≤20k)
- Every new helper has a godoc + a usage example test (in internal/testutil/*_test.go)
- No test loses coverage — grep before/after for TestXxx / It / Entry count parity
- Existing suite entries all still work

## Sequencing

1. Wait for gaka-0vp-17 kill switch (only ginkgo on main)
2. Land helpers first (in internal/testutil)
3. Migrate one package to use each helper — verify green
4. Sweep the remaining 21 packages

Total effort: 4-6 hours if done in one focused session.

title: [KILL SWITCH] Delete stdlib _test.go, rename *_ginkgo_test.go → *_test.go
description:
Final child of gaka-0vp. Prereq: EVERY package migration child closed with 1:1 verification.

Steps:
1. Confirm go test ./... -count=1 passes with BOTH stdlib + ginkgo running (green in CI).
2. For each package with a _ginkgo_test.go sibling: delete the stdlib file. The _suite_test.go stays.
3. Rename *_ginkgo_test.go → *_test.go (removes the interim naming — the FINAL state is one _test.go file per test file, ginkgo-flavored).
4. Update docs/testing/ginkgo.md — remove the 'parallel' section, promote it to the canonical testing style.
5. Update CLAUDE.md (project) with the new testing convention.
6. Confirm go test ./... -count=1 is still green.

Deletion order suggestion (small first, so a bug is caught early):
- internal/apierr, model, wakatime, cache, config, openapi (bootstrap set)
- internal/labelcatalog, comfyui, logging, queue/*
- internal/worker/labelimages, auth, backfill/git, importer
- internal/widget, stats, testutil, server
- internal/handler, db (biggest — most risk)

Report per-package deletion + net LOC delta in the close note.
notes:
First bulk-delete attempt (2026-07-29) REVERTED. Learnings for the next attempt:

## What went wrong

Bulk-delete of stdlib _test.go files broke ~10 packages with undefined-symbol errors. The parallel migration produced ginkgo mirrors that referenced helpers still living in the stdlib file — deleting the stdlib file removed the helpers too.

## Missing-helper inventory (confirmed broken on first delete)

- internal/backfill/git: testCommit type, mkTestRepo helper
- internal/importer: mockWakatime helper
- internal/stats: day, mkPayload helpers
- internal/wakatime: strptr helper
- internal/worker/labelimages: testDatabaseURL const
- internal/server: silentLogger helper
- internal/widget: mustJSON helper
- internal/queue/imagejobs: internal (unexported) byLabelSnapshot method access (stdlib test was in-package; ginkgo mirror likely _test package — would need to move)

There are almost certainly more not surfaced by the first vet pass.

## Correct approach — per-package kill switch

For each package with a stdlib+ginkgo pair:

1. `git show HEAD:<file>_test.go` — enumerate every non-Test top-level def (funcs, types, vars, consts)
2. Extract those into a `<pkg>_helpers_test.go` file (or fold into the ginkgo file if it's the only consumer)
3. Verify `go build ./<pkg>/...` still clean
4. Delete the stdlib `_test.go` file
5. Rename `_ginkgo_test.go` → `_test.go`
6. Run `go test ./<pkg>/... -count=1` — must pass

Do ONE package per commit so a bad extraction is a targeted revert.

## Also uncovered by this attempt

- internal/handler/awards_coverage_ginkgo_test.go — redundant with the 146 discrete TestAchievement_* tests (I deleted it in the failed attempt; can safely re-delete)
- internal/handler/testhelpers_ginkgo_test.go — G-suffixed helpers; can drop the G suffix now that stdlib helpers are gone, but requires call-site updates
- internal/testutil/helpers_ginkgo_test.go — same as above

## Recommend

Convert this bead into an epic; file one child per package (22 children). Each child is 15-30 min of careful work. Total budget: 6-10 hours. Do NOT try bulk delete again.

title: [epic] Migrate all tests from stdlib testing to ginkgo/gomega (1:1, parallel, kill switch)
description:
Convert every _test.go file in internal/ from the Go stdlib testing
package to ginkgo v2 + gomega. Full 1:1 conversion (no test dropped),
parallel migration (both suites run under go test until the final
kill-switch), then delete the stdlib variants.

## Why

- Better readability: Expect(x).To(Equal(y)) beats
  if x != y { t.Errorf("x = %v, want %v", x, y) }
- Table-driven tests via DescribeTable + Entry — named cases in the
  output instead of cases[3] pointer chases
- Nested Describe/Context/It expresses invariants the way we already
  narrate them in godocs
- BeforeEach / AfterEach idioms clean up the ad-hoc t.Cleanup pattern
- Focus/skip via -ginkgo.focus regex is nicer than -run

## Ground rules (see docs/testing/ginkgo.md)

1. Parallel migration. For each foo_test.go, add sibling
   foo_ginkgo_test.go that ports 1:1. Both run under go test.
2. 1:1 coverage. No case dropped, no case fabricated. Ginkgo file
   header lists which case was TestXxx.
3. One suite entry per package: <pkg>_suite_test.go with
   TestPkgSuite(t) { RegisterFailHandler(Fail); RunSpecs(t, "...") }
4. Only after every stdlib case has a verified ginkgo equivalent do
   we delete the stdlib file (final ticket = kill switch).

## Deliverables (across children)

- 22 packages migrated (one child per package)
- docs/testing/ginkgo.md — migration guide (SHIPPED alongside this
  epic; child tickets reference it as canon)
- gaka-tst-ginkgo.KILL — final child deletes stdlib _test.go files
  and renames _ginkgo_test.go → _test.go

## Bootstrap (SHIPPED alongside this epic)

- go.mod: github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2 + gomega added
- internal/labels/labels_suite_test.go — first suite entry
- internal/labels/dbrow_ginkgo_test.go — first 1:1 conversion
  (4 stdlib TestXxx → 6 DescribeTable entries + 3 It blocks; all pass)

## Package inventory (~99 test files, ~25k LOC)

Big packages (>1k LOC): internal/db (33 files), internal/handler
(25 files), internal/stats (9 files), internal/importer (5 files),
internal/testutil (3 files).

Small independent packages (do first — proves the pattern for the
big ones): internal/apierr, internal/model, internal/config,
internal/cache, internal/wakatime, internal/labelcatalog.

## Non-goals

- No functional test changes. Same seeds, same assertions, same
  invariants. Just style.
- No new tests added during migration (file follow-up beads if a

title: Parametrized label-coverage test (pure Go, isolated per-label)
description:
The test the whole epic unblocks. Pure Go now that gaka-hc6.1 exists.

## Shape

internal/labels/coverage_test.go:

  func TestLabelCoverage(t *testing.T) {
    ctx := context.Background()
    catalog := loadCatalogFromMigratedDB(t)  // reads labels table from
                                              // freshly migrated test DB
    for _, label := range catalog {
      t.Run(label.ID, func(t *testing.T) {
        // FULL PER-TEST ISOLATION:
        // fresh username, cleanup after, own heartbeat batch
        username := "covtest_" + slugify(label.ID)
        t.Cleanup(func() { db.PurgeUser(ctx, username) })
        db.CreateUser(ctx, username)

        hbs := synthesizeHeartbeats(label.Condition, username, testClock)
        require.NoError(t, db.SaveHeartbeats(ctx, hbs))

        payload := buildPublicDashboardPayload(ctx, username)
        awards := labels.EvaluateAll(payload, []LabelSpec{label})
        awardIDs := lo.Map(awards, func(a LabelAward, _ int) string { return a.ID })
        require.Contains(t, awardIDs, label.ID,
          "label %q should fire against its own minimum-viable heartbeats", label.ID)
      })
    }
  }

## Per-condition heartbeat synthesizer

internal/labels/synthesize.go: one function per Condition primitive kind,
producing the minimum []db.Heartbeat to satisfy it. See gaka-hc6 parent's
brief for the primitive breakdown (13 kinds + 3 composers).

## Isolation guarantees
- Fresh username per label (heartbeats scoped by sender=username)
- t.Cleanup deletes the user's rows after each subtest
- No shared TestMain seeding many labels at once
- Adding a new label = new labels-catalog seed row + zero test code

## Not in this ticket
- Under-threshold negative fixtures (nice-to-have, file a follow-up bead
  if time allows during implementation)
- Full coverage of `not`-composed conditions (leave as skipped subtests
  with a t.Skip + a filed follow-up bead)

## Deliverables
- internal/labels/coverage_test.go
- internal/labels/synthesize.go + synthesize_test.go
- Runs in ≤ 30s locally (target 15s)
- go test -run 'TestLabelCoverage/python-master' -v works standalone

## Depends on
- gaka-hc6.1 (evaluator port; needed to call EvaluateAll from Go)
Nice-to-have dependency on gaka-hc6.3 (proves the whole request flow, not
just the evaluator+aggregation).
notes:
Implementation notes ready — post-gaka-hc6.1 (evaluator Go port). Everything upstream is landed.

## Environment
- Use internal/testutil.NewHarness (see internal/handler/auth_test.go for pattern). Harness gives fresh DB + Handler + auto-cleanup.
- Existing test-DB pattern: TestMain provisions a random-named Postgres db per package.

## Heartbeat synthesis (the hard bit)
- model.HeartbeatPayload — populate Sender, TimeSent (unix seconds float), Entity, Project, Language, Editor, Platform, Category as needed.
- DB.SaveHeartbeats attributes gap_seconds capped at time_limit (default 900s = 15min per heartbeat). So each heartbeat contributes ≤15min to whichever axes it declares.
- To fire "100 hours in Python": ~400 heartbeats spaced 15 min apart, each with language=python. Or lower threshold via a per-label fixture map (see below).

## Recommended scope for v1
Rather than trying to synthesize the exact production threshold (400+ heartbeats per label = 40k+ inserts for full catalog), use TWO tiers:

**Tier A — Representative primitives (v1, ships now):**
Pick ONE label per primitive kind:
- axis-time: python-novice (5h threshold — only ~20 heartbeats)
- axis-time-sum: terminal-veteran (vim+neovim+emacs ≥ 5h combined)
- distinct-count: a low-threshold polyglot variant (or dry-run the polyglot with 3 langs × 2h each)
- punchcard-hour-pct: night-watch (~10 heartbeats in [22,23,0,1,...5] hours)
- punchcard-dow-pct: weekend-warrior
- streak: consecutive-days
- daily-avg: daily-avg-1h (skip if no such label exists)
- trend: skip in v1 (needs 14 days of data)
- all/any/not composed: pick one label per composer

**Tier B — Full 114-label sweep (follow-up bead):**
File as gaka-hc6.6.1 — needs either (a) a threshold-scaling harness that runs each label at 1/10th threshold for tests, or (b) tolerance for a longer test (~2 min).

## Per-primitive synthesizer sketch (Go)
```go
func synthesizeForAxisTime(username string, cond labels.AxisTimeCond, at time.Time) []model.HeartbeatPayload {
    // 5h = 5*60*60 = 18000s. At 15min gap cap = 900s per heartbeat: 20 heartbeats.
    n := int(math.Ceil(cond.Hours * 3600 / 900)) + 1
    hbs := make([]model.HeartbeatPayload, 0, n)
    axisField := axisSetter(cond.Axis, cond.Value) // sets Language/Editor/etc
    for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
        t := at.Add(-time.Duration(n-i) * 14 * time.Minute)
        hbs = append(hbs, buildHB(username, t, axisField))
    }
    return hbs
}
```

## Full pipeline
```go
for _, row := range dbRows {
    t.Run(row.ID, func(t *testing.T) {
        username := "covtest_" + slug(row.ID)
        hz.Cleanup(username)
        spec := labels.SpecFromDBRow(dbRowAdapter(row))
        hbs := synthesizeFor(username, spec.Condition, referenceTime)
        if hbs == nil { t.Skip("primitive not synthesizable in v1"); return }
        require.NoError(t, hz.DB.SaveHeartbeats(ctx, hbs))
        payload, err := hz.H.buildAwardsPayload(ctx, username) // may need exposing via helper
        require.NoError(t, err)
        awards := labels.EvaluateAll(payload, []labels.LabelSpec{spec})
        ids := lo.Map(awards, func(a labels.LabelAward, _ int) string { return a.ID })
        require.Contains(t, ids, spec.ID, "label should fire against its own minimum heartbeats")
    })
}
```

## Blockers to check on
- `buildAwardsPayload` is a private handler method; may need to extract to a package-visible function OR use the HTTP endpoint via hz.Router().
- Cleanup queries in testutil.Cleanup already include heartbeats + hb_rollup_daily — full per-user teardown works out of the box.
- Need to also delete award_ledger rows in cleanup (add DELETE FROM award_ledger WHERE username=$1 to testutil.Cleanup).
- The buildAwardsPayload catalog fetch does ListLabels — for the test, we want to evaluate against just ONE label at a time. Bypass DB fetch: call labels.EvaluateAll directly with the single spec instead of routing through the handler.

Estimated implementation: 300-500 LOC of Go + heartbeat fixture builder + subtest runner. 3-6 hours for a careful implementation with per-primitive synthesizers.

## Alternative — payload-level test (simpler, ships same value for correctness)
If DB seeding is too heavy, build the Payload struct directly in Go and skip heartbeat insertion. Loses "does the aggregator produce the right payload from raw heartbeats" coverage but gains "does the evaluator fire for the payload each label expects." That's a substantial subset of what the user asked for and is 100 LOC instead of 500.

Reasonable v1: payload-level. Follow-up: heartbeat-level.

title: Server endpoints: GET /awards (own + public); server-write ledger
description:
Wire the Go evaluator (gaka-hc6.1) behind two handlers, and move the ledger
write from client-POST to server-eval.

## Endpoints
- GET /api/v1/users/current/awards
    - Loads the caller's PublicDashboardPayload from the same source the
      dashboard handler uses (internal/stats aggregation)
    - Loads the labels catalog
    - Runs evaluator
    - Writes ledger rows (same idempotent upsert as today's
      /awards/log — dedupe via (username, label_id, period_start))
    - Returns []LabelAward JSON
    - Cache-Control: private, max-age=30
- GET /api/public/profile/:slug/awards
    - Resolves username via slug (existing helper)
    - Respects public_profile_enabled
    - Same shape but public-scoped
    - Cache-Control: public, max-age=180 (longer — visitors don't need
      up-to-the-minute; hero can stay stable for 3 minutes)
    - Does NOT write to ledger from a public visit (only own visits do —
      keeps the ledger from being pollutable by "anyone who loads a slug")

## Ledger write ownership shift
- Today: FE POSTs /awards/log after evaluating client-side
- After this: server writes on its own /awards call; FE never POSTs from
  the JIT path
