title: Golden-fixture drift guard: Go evaluator ≡ TS evaluator
description:
Prevent silent divergence between the Go evaluator (gaka-hc6.1) and the
still-alive TS evaluator during the transition. Once TS is deleted
(gaka-hc6.5) this test drops out, but until then it's the tripwire.

## Design

- Shared fixture format: web/src/test-fixtures/evaluator-golden/*.json
  Each file: { payload: PublicDashboardPayload, catalog: LabelSpec[],
              expectedAwards: string[] } (labelIds, sorted)
- TS test asserts: evaluate(payload, {catalog}).map(a=>a.id).sort() === expectedAwards
- Go test asserts: EvaluateAll(payload, catalog).IDsSorted() === expectedAwards
- If both pass, the two evaluators agree on every fixture.
- Fixtures are HAND-AUTHORED to exercise every primitive at threshold ±
  epsilon plus one composition case each (all/any/not).

Minimum 12 files, one per primitive kind + 3 for composition. Each fixture
should be small (one axis, one label) so the intent reads at a glance.

drift guard between TS catalog + Go worker catalog). CI-enforced parity
during the deprecation window.

description:

and delete the client-side TypeScript evaluator once every consumer is on the

title: Backfill fidelity: complexity-weighted session length + tail spread
description:
User feedback (2026-07-28):
  "the issue was with our git backfills it didnt really properly extend the days,
   i commited so infrequently and probably in large chunks its having trouble
   articulating some of the fidelity in the synthetic backfill"

## Current algorithm (internal/backfill/git/cluster.go)
- ClusterGap: 30 min — commits closer than this merge into one session
- PreCommitLead: 15 min — session starts 15m BEFORE first commit
- PostCommitTail: 5 min — session ends 5m AFTER last commit
- HeartbeatRate: 2 min — heartbeats within session

## What this yields for a lumpy-commit user
- One weekly commit = one 20-minute session (15m lead + 5m tail)
- ~10 synthetic heartbeats per commit REGARDLESS of what the commit contains
- A 500-line-changed commit gets the same 20 minutes as a 5-line-changed commit
- Between commits: 0% activity — even though real work happened

## Proposed fixes (pick one or ship both)

### Option A — Complexity-weighted PreCommitLead (small, targeted)
Scale PreCommitLead with lines_changed:
  lead(c) = clamp(BASE_LEAD + c.LinesAdded + c.LinesDeleted × TIME_PER_LINE,
                  MIN_LEAD, MAX_LEAD)
E.g. BASE_LEAD=15m, TIME_PER_LINE=6s, MIN=15m, MAX=8h.
- 5-line commit  →  15m + 30s → clamped to 15m (unchanged)
- 500-line commit → 15m + 50m ≈ 65m of prior "typing"
- 3000-line commit → 15m + 5h → clamped to 8h
Simple, matches user's mental model, doesn't invent time between commits.

Requires: adding EstimatorConfig knobs (BaseLead, TimePerLine, MinLead, MaxLead)
+ admin UI exposure + new tests. Bounded blast radius.

### Option B — Rest-day-aware inter-commit spread (bigger, richer)
Between two commits within some soft-threshold gap (e.g. ≤ 3 days), spread
synthetic activity across a chunk of the intervening period. Rules:
- Gap > SOFT_GAP (default 3 days) → do nothing (treat commits as isolated
  sessions per current algo). Prevents inventing 3-week vacations as active.
- Gap ≤ SOFT_GAP → treat as one "campaign"; distribute
  min(commit2.complexity * TIME_PER_LINE, gap - SESSION_END) of work into
  the gap
- Only distribute across the AUTHOR'S TYPICAL WORK WINDOW (e.g. 10:00-19:00
  in user tz — reuse gaka-dg7 tz resolver)
- Never place synthetic heartbeats on days already having REAL heartbeats
  (heartbeats.source IS NULL or != 'backfill:*') — real data wins

Requires: bigger algorithmic change, workday inference (or a knob), and
careful boundary handling. High impact for the lumpy-commit case.

### Option C — Just widen defaults + educate
Raise PreCommitLead default from 15m → 45m, PostCommitTail from 5m → 15m.
Doesn't fix the "one commit = one session" root problem but gets 60m per
commit instead of 20m. 3x cheaper improvement, no algorithmic risk.

## Recommendation
Ship A + C together in one PR. Ship B only after A+C are in production and
we can compare the calendar shapes.

## Related
- The complexity-factor design was deferred earlier this session ("except 3").
  This bead is the promoted follow-up.
- gaka-b5n GitHub OIDC epic (unrelated but landing near this in time).
- Any tuning should ship with regression tests over a fixture repo — a
  100-commit fake repo with known commit shapes → assert the output session
  lengths are within expected bounds.

## Acceptance
- User can rotate their range picker across a multi-year backfilled history
  and see credibly-shaped daily activity (not all-empty-then-spike)
- Configurable via admin backfill config (existing UI) — no code redeploy
  needed to tune

title: GitHub stats endpoints: fetch + cache + public variant
description:
Two endpoints, one background cache-warm strategy.

## Endpoints
- GET /api/v1/users/current/github/stats
    - Cache hit (< 1h old) → return cached JSON
    - Miss → fetch fresh, upsert cache, return
    - Requires the caller to have a linked GH identity; 404 otherwise
- GET /api/public/profile/:slug/github/stats
    - Same shape as own variant, but scoped by slug
    - Respects users.public_profile_enabled AND a new users.public_github_enabled
      column (default true; user can opt out separately)
    - Returns 404 if profile private OR user has no linked GH
    - Never returns access_token_encrypted or any per-token metadata

## Fields returned
{
  ghLogin: string,
  avatarUrl: string,
  followers: int,
  following: int,
  publicRepos: int,
  totalStarsReceived: int,
  contributionsLastYear: int,
  contributionGrid: [{date, count}] * 371,        // 53 weeks * 7 days
  topRepos: [{name, description, stars, language, url}] * 6,
  fetchedAt: string
}

## GitHub API strategy
- REST v3 for user + repos (google/go-github)
- GraphQL v4 for contributions grid (REST doesn't expose the grid data —
  ContributionsCollection query)
- Use the encrypted access_token from external_identities for auth (5000 req/hr
  vs 60 unauth'd)
- Rate limit handling: if we hit primary limit, return the cached row even if
  stale, add X-Boom-Stats-Stale: true header
- Secondary rate limit (abuse detection): backoff + never retry more than 2x

## Caching
- Table: github_stats_cache (from child 2)
- TTL: 1h for own view, 6h for public view (public gets more aggressive cache
  since visitor count on a profile can be high and stats don't change fast)
- Cache-Control: private, max-age=300 (own); public, max-age=1800 (public)

## Deliverables
- internal/github/client.go — wraps go-github + a small GraphQL helper
- internal/handler/github_stats.go — both handlers + cache logic
- internal/db/github_stats_cache.go — Get/Upsert
- Route registration
- Unit tests: cache-hit path returns without an HTTP call (assert with a mock)
- Integration test: happy-path fetch → cache write → subsequent hit returns cached
- Docs: link to GitHub's rate limit docs + note about needing a linked identity

title: Account linking API: link/unlink + last-auth-method guard
description:
Explicit link/unlink endpoints for signed-in users. Distinct from the login
callback in child 3 because the UX is different — user is already
authenticated, and they're initiating the link from Settings, not from /login.

## Endpoints
- POST /api/v1/users/current/link/github/start
    - Same as /auth/oidc/github/start but sets an extra bit in the state
      cookie so the callback knows this is a LINK, not a SIGN-IN
    - Returns the redirect URL to the browser (FE performs the redirect
      itself so it can preserve any client-side draft state)
- DELETE /api/v1/users/current/link/github
    - Refuses if IsSoleAuthMethod(username) returns true — 409 Conflict
      with body {code: "sole_auth_method", message: "set a password first"}
    - Otherwise sets revoked_at, clears github_stats_cache row, returns 204
- GET /api/v1/users/current/identities
    - Returns []{provider, handle, avatarUrl, linkedAt, lastUsedAt} for the caller
    - Used by the Settings page identity table

## Guard: last auth method
- Sole auth method = users.hashed_password IS NULL AND no other non-revoked
  external_identities row
- The guard must be enforced in a single transaction (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE +
  DELETE) so it's race-safe against parallel unlink requests from two tabs

## Admin visibility
- GET /api/v1/admin/users/:username/identities (already-existing admin allowlist
  gate applies) — for the admin/support use case where an operator needs to
  see which users have GH linked

## Deliverables
- internal/handler/link_github.go with the three handlers
- internal/db/external_identities.go: add IsSoleAuthMethod + tx-safe RevokeIdentity
- Route registration
- Unit tests: guard fires when it should + doesn't when it shouldn't
- Integration test: link then unlink round-trip

title: OAuth flow (backend): /auth/oidc/github/start + /callback
description:
Implement the two entry-point HTTP handlers plus the state/signing helpers.

## Endpoints
- GET /auth/oidc/github/start?return_to=/app
    - Generates random nonce, signs {nonce, return_to, exp=+10min} with server secret
    - Sets HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure, path=/auth cookie 'gh_state'
    - 302 to github.com/login/oauth/authorize with state=<nonce>, client_id,
      redirect_uri, scope=read:user user:email
- GET /auth/oidc/github/callback?code=&state=
    - Reads gh_state cookie, verifies HMAC + expiry + state param matches nonce
    - Rejects if BOOM_ENABLE_GITHUB_OIDC is false (404 — pretend endpoint doesn't exist)
    - Exchanges code with GH (client_id + secret + code + redirect_uri)
    - Fetches userinfo: GET https://api.github.com/user + /user/emails
    - Case A (authenticated session present): calls LinkIdentity on the current
      user, redirect to return_to (default /app/settings/account)
    - Case B (no session): LookupUsernameByExternal(github, sub)
        - Hit → set refresh cookie for that user, redirect to return_to (/app)
        - Miss → CreateUserFromGitHub (see child 2's LinkIdentity + a new
          username-collision-safe user create), then set refresh cookie
    - Cache token encrypted (BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY) so we can call GH later on
      user's behalf

## Config
- BOOM_ENABLE_GITHUB_OIDC (bool, default false)
- BOOM_GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
- BOOM_GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
- BOOM_GITHUB_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URL (must match the value in the registered GH OAuth app)
- BOOM_OAUTH_STATE_SIGNING_KEY (32-byte HMAC key; separate from encryption key)

## Failure modes to cover
- code missing / state missing → 400 with a UI-friendly redirect
- state cookie missing / expired → 400
- state param ≠ cookie nonce → 400 (CSRF attempt logged)
- GH token exchange 4xx/5xx → 502 with a Try Again UI
- userinfo missing email (private only, no verified) → 400 "please verify a GH email first"
- collision (existing user with same GH login but not linked) → NEVER auto-claim;
  redirect to /login with a message explaining "sign in with your existing password, then link"

## Deliverables
- internal/handler/oauth_github.go (start + callback handlers)
- internal/oauth/state.go (HMAC sign/verify helpers, small & focused)
- internal/oauth/github.go (client for token exchange + userinfo)
- Config wiring in internal/config
- Unit tests: state sign/verify positive + tamper cases
- Integration test: happy-path callback with a mock GH server (httptest.Server)

title: Data model: external_identities + github_stats_cache migrations
description:
Two new tables + a bump to users. All in ONE migration so rollback stays clean.

## external_identities
Represents a foreign identity linked to a boomtime user. 1:N per user
(one row per provider linked). Unique on (provider, sub) so a GH account
can only back one boomtime user.

CREATE TABLE external_identities (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  username TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(username) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  provider TEXT NOT NULL,              -- 'github' (add more later)
  sub TEXT NOT NULL,                    -- provider's stable user id
  handle TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- gh_login at link time (denormed)
  email TEXT,                           -- primary verified email at link time
  avatar_url TEXT,                      -- for the linked-identities table UI
  access_token_encrypted BYTEA,         -- AES-256-GCM under BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY
  scopes TEXT,                          -- space-separated, exact string GH returned
  linked_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  last_used_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ,               -- soft-delete; unlink sets this
  UNIQUE (provider, sub) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL,
  UNIQUE (username, provider) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL
);
CREATE INDEX ON external_identities(username);

## github_stats_cache
Per-username snapshot of GH stats. Hourly cache TTL — the FE is fine with
"data from up to 1h ago" for public profile decoration.

CREATE TABLE github_stats_cache (
  username TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES users(username) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  gh_login TEXT NOT NULL,
  followers INT,
  following INT,
  public_repos INT,
  total_stars_received BIGINT,
  contributions_last_year INT,
  contribution_grid_json JSONB,         -- 53*7 cells for the contributions grid
  top_repos_json JSONB,                 -- top-N by stars, capped payload
  fetched_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

## users bump
No column addition needed on users itself — external_identities backfills the
association. If gaka-0oe hasn't landed by the time this ships, ensure the
migration guards ordering so it can go either way.

## Deliverables
- internal/db/migrations/00045_external_identities.sql
- internal/db/external_identities.go with:
    - LinkIdentity(username, provider, sub, handle, email, avatarURL, encToken, scopes)
    - LookupUsernameByExternal(provider, sub) → (username, bool)
    - ListIdentities(username) → []ExternalIdentity
    - RevokeIdentity(username, provider) → error
    - IsSoleAuthMethod(username) → bool (no password AND no other identity)
- internal/db/github_stats_cache.go with Get/Upsert helpers
- Unit tests for the accessors against a real Postgres (per feedback_test_layering)

title: Design doc: GitHub OIDC arch + provider abstraction seam
description:
Write docs/design/github-oidc.md capturing the architectural decisions BEFORE
any code lands. Covers:

- Library choice: golang.org/x/oauth2 (raw), coreos/go-oidc (id_token verify),
  google/go-github v65 (typed REST). GH doesn't ship a public OIDC discovery
  document — it's OAuth2 with a userinfo call — so go-oidc is optional. Pick
  one path and justify.
- Provider abstraction: define an OidcProvider interface with (Start, Callback,
  FetchUserinfo, FetchStats) methods so provider #2 later is drop-in. Do NOT
  build the abstraction speculatively — just show where the seams go.
- Session model: refresh cookie stays the source of truth for the web session
  (matches gaka-0oe substrate). OAuth access_token is stored separately in
  external_identities.access_token_encrypted (encrypted at rest under
  BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY — same threat model as encrypted_wakatime_key).
- Scopes: minimum viable = read:user + user:email. public_repo optional if we
  want private repo counts (probably skip for MVP).
- CSRF: state cookie MUST be signed+HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, path=/auth. Bind
  it to the return_to path.
- Redirect URI: BOOM_GITHUB_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URL env var (must match what the GH
  OAuth app is registered with — one URL per environment)
- Rollout: BOOM_ENABLE_GITHUB_OIDC feature flag, default off in prod
- Account collision policy: what to do when a GH login matches an existing
  boomtime username but is NOT linked yet — force link flow, DON'T silently
  claim
- Deliverable: design doc committed to docs/design/, review comments folded
  in, follow-up children in this epic all reference sections of it

title: [epic] GitHub OIDC login + linked-account GitHub stats
description:
Ship GitHub as boomtime's FIRST first-class OIDC / OAuth provider — both as a
sign-in path (new users can join via GH; existing users can link + sign in
via GH) and as a data source (contributions, repos, followers, stars on the
public profile + widgets).

This epic is intentionally scoped as "GitHub, then generalize." We start with
one provider done end-to-end (auth, link, unlink, data pull, cache, UI, widget,
docs, tests) and design the abstraction just wide enough that adding a second
provider later (Google, GitLab, an Authentik-federated custom OIDC) is
additive, not a rewrite.

## Why now / why this shape

- boomtime is Wakatime-compatible for editor plugins (still Basic auth), so
  the OIDC path is for the WEB session only. Editor plugins keep using the
  API-token bearer they already use.
- GitHub is the highest-signal identity for our audience — devs. Onboarding
  with "sign in with GitHub" is the shortest path to a new user seeing their
  own profile.
- The public profile already has label chips + tier badges. Adding GitHub
  contribution stats + top repos on the same card gives the profile a
  "personal identity" surface a Wakatime-only view can't provide.

## Depends on gaka-0oe (OIDC-readiness substrate)

The `gaka-0oe` epic covers the identity refactor (h.identify() resolver, RBAC
tiers, external_identities table concept). This epic assumes that landing
first — trying to ship provider-specific auth flows before the resolver
supports multiple identity backends is a mess we've already scoped away from.

## User flow (target end-state)

### First-time visitor
1. Lands on /login, sees username/password + "Continue with GitHub" button
2. Clicks GH button → redirected to github.com/login/oauth/authorize
3. Grants scopes: read:user, user:email (optionally public_repo)
4. Redirected back to /auth/oidc/github/callback with code + state
5. Server verifies state cookie, exchanges code for access_token, fetches
   userinfo (login, id, avatar, email, name)
6. Server sees no external_identity row for (github, sub) → creates a new
   boomtime user with:
     - username = github_login (with collision-suffix if taken)
     - email = primary verified GH email
     - avatar hint = GH avatar url (pre-populates chibi seed)
     - external_identities row linking (github, sub) → username
7. Refresh cookie set → redirect to /app → dashboard renders

### Returning visitor (GitHub-only)
1. Clicks "Continue with GitHub" → same OAuth dance
2. Server finds existing external_identities row → resolves username →
   sets refresh cookie → /app

### Existing password user linking GH
1. Signed in via password already
2. Settings > Account > Linked identities → "Link GitHub" button
3. Same OAuth dance but callback sees an authenticated session AND resolves
   an existing user — creates link row scoped to current username instead of
   creating a new user
4. On success returns to Settings with the GH row now showing (avatar +
   login + Unlink)

### Unlinking
1. Settings > Account > Linked identities > Unlink → confirm modal
2. Server refuses if this is the ONLY authentication method (no password
   set, no other linked identities) — must set a password first
3. Otherwise deletes the row; GH stats card + widget disappear from
   public profile on next fetch

### Data flow (GitHub stats)
1. After link (or on any dashboard load if linked), FE calls
   GET /api/v1/users/current/github/stats
2. Server: cache hit (< 1h old) → return cached; miss → fetch from GH
   REST + GraphQL (contributions graph is GraphQL-only), write cache
3. Public variant: GET /api/public/profile/:slug/github/stats — respects
   public_profile_enabled + only exposes fields the user has opted to show
4. FE renders a "GitHub" card on the public profile (contributions grid,
   top-N repos, follower count) + provides a widget type for the embeddable
   widget system

## Non-goals for THIS epic
- OIDC providers beyond GitHub (Google, Apple, GitLab, custom Authentik) —
  those come after the abstraction proves itself with one provider done end
  to end
- Pulling GitHub commit heartbeats INTO wakatime data (that's a separate
  ingestion concern — this epic is auth + profile stats only)
- Removing password auth (we keep it; GH is additive)
- Federated logout / RP-initiated logout (GH OAuth doesn't support it
  cleanly anyway)

## Success criteria
- New user can go from /login to a working /app session in ≤ 3 clicks
  using only GitHub
- Existing password user can link GH and see the "Unlink" CTA + no data loss
- Public profile at /p/<slug> renders a GitHub card (contributions grid +
  top repos) when the owner has linked and opted in
- BOOM_ENABLE_GITHUB_OIDC feature flag off => login button hidden, endpoints
  404 (safe default for orgs that don't want it)
- Test pyramid: unit for state signing + callback contract; integration
  hitting a mock GH OAuth; at least one Playwright e2e for the golden path
notes: SUPERSEDED (partial) by Authentik federation decision (gaka-93f): GitHub becomes a federated OAuth *source inside Authentik* (a blueprint), NOT a boomtime-direct OIDC flow. Children b5n.3/.4 (GH-direct OAuth+callback) are dropped. GitHub *stats* children (b5n.5/.8) survive as an independent data-source feature, deprioritized post-billing.

title: Survey homelab OIDC providers with gitops-viability lens (Authentik, Dex, Zitadel, Keycloak, Okta, …)
description:
User uses Authentik today but has expressed frustration with the manual setup surface (outposts, providers, apps, all clicked through in the UI). Wants GITOPS-first: declare providers/clients/users/groups in yaml, apply, done. Zero click-ops.

Investigate whether there's a better fit for a k8s-on-Talos homelab where gitops (argocd) is the primary deploy vehicle. Key concerns:
1. Can the entire provider config live in git? (CRDs, operator, terraform, or just YAML-imported bootstrap)
2. What's the outpost/proxy story? Does the app need per-tenant sidecars or does the OIDC provider stand alone?
3. Client + user + group provisioning: manual or declarative?
4. Boomtime-specific: how easy to register boomtime as a new client, add users, assign groups — all in a PR?

Providers to compare (add more if worth):
- Authentik (current) — check for authentik-operator or terraform provider, blueprints
- Dex (k8s-native, has CRDs) — evaluate whether its feature surface matches Authentik's
- Zitadel (rust-based, self-hostable) — declarative-first design
- Keycloak — mature, has keycloak-operator, big JVM footprint
- Ory Hydra / Kratos — headless, gitops-friendly but more assembly required
- Vault + OIDC — auth as identity provider
- Cloud (Okta, Auth0, Google Workspace) — for comparison; likely rejected due to homelab spirit

Deliverable: comparison matrix + top-2 recommendation with gitops-viability score + migration cost estimate from current Authentik setup.
acceptance_criteria: docs/design/oidc-provider-survey.md written (uncommitted). Comparison matrix has columns: Provider, GitOps story, CRD/Operator, Outpost required, Config-in-git rating, Client provisioning, Group/user provisioning, Learning curve from Authentik. Top-2 recommendation with rationale. Migration cost estimate. No code changes.
notes: Fed into gaka-0oe design doc as an appendix. User wants as much in gitops as possible, as little manual as possible.

title: User demarcation system (RBAC + tiers) + OIDC-readiness groundwork
description:
Lay groundwork for two related concerns:

1. USER DEMARCATION — some users should be on a lighter user model where boomtime does NOT generate certain per-user indices/rollups (hb_rollup_daily, health rollup, projects extras, etc.). Motivation: cost + storage for users who don't need dashboards (e.g. read-only visitors, public-profile-only, evaluator/demo accounts, service accounts, quota-limited free tier). Shape open: could be RBAC (roles: 'full', 'read-only', 'service', ...) or feature flags per user ({rollups_enabled, backups_enabled, public_only, ...}) — plan agent to recommend based on codebase fit.

2. OIDC READINESS — today boomtime does username/password + refresh_token cookie auth. Groundwork to make a future OIDC/OAuth swap low-lift. Not implementing OIDC yet — just abstracting the identity resolution + user provisioning so a provider swap doesn't touch every call site. Also worth considering: boomtime AS an OIDC provider (issuing tokens other apps trust) — same abstraction shape, opposite direction.

BOTH share the same substrate: a clean identity + capability layer that today's hardcoded '(user, has-token, is-authenticated)' model doesn't cleanly express. This bead is the epic for scoping that layer + breaking into sub-beads with clear execution boundaries.

Deliverable of the scoping: a plan doc under docs/design/user-model-and-oidc.md + a set of sub-beads (schema, capability check middleware, index-skip flag propagation, OIDC-shaped identity resolver interface, etc.) each with acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc committed at docs/design/user-model-and-oidc.md. Sub-beads filed under gaka-<epic>. Recommended shape (RBAC vs feature-flags) argued with reference to existing patterns. Concrete first-slice bead sized for one session's work.
notes: Idea captured mid-goals-agent work. Not blocking — parallel scoping. See gaka-wpb for the concurrent goals feature that shares some patterns (JSONB spec, owner-scoped tables) worth cross-referencing when the scoping agent lands.

title: GetTotalTimeBetween SQL broken — unnest(unknown) is not unique
description:
Discovered during the gaka-oew audit. `get_time_between.sql` uses `unnest($1,$2,$3,$4)` which fails on every call under the current Postgres version:

  ERROR: function pg_catalog.unnest(unknown) is not unique (SQLSTATE 42725)

**Impact:** /api/v1/commits/:project/report endpoint (only caller) 500s whenever any commit data would trigger the aggregation. No handler test exists (blocked by GitHub-credential requirement in commits.go), which is why this hadn't been caught.

**Fix:** cast the array params in get_time_between.sql to explicit types, e.g.
    `unnest($1::text[], $2::text[], $3::timestamp[], $4::timestamp[])`

**Re-enable regression test:** `TestTotalTimeBetweenAscendingOrder_KnownBroken` in `internal/db/aggregation_invariants_test.go` — it currently just t.Skip()s. Restore the seeded-data version once fix lands.
close_reason: Cast fix in a23e152; regression covered by TestTotalTimeBetweenReturnsAscendingSums in internal/db/aggregation_invariants_test.go (also asserts two-user tenant isolation)

title: Purge hidden rows destructively from curation rules
description:
Add a destructive purge tool for hide rules — trashcan icon on remapping rows visible only when rule.action=='hide'. Tests to add (mirror apply suite): purge happy-path, idempotent, owner-scoped, transaction rollback, preview===run regression, rename-rule rejection, exact/regex/template matching. Apply variant retains its existing UX (no typing gate). Trash icon appears only on hide rules; zap icon appears only on rename rules; pen and X always. Backend runs DELETE heartbeats + DELETE curation_rules atomically. Preview endpoint dispatches on rule.action.

title: UI shows case-differing duplicates for language/project/editor axes
description:
User reports seeing rows like 'Python' and 'python' (or 'VSCode' and 'vscode') side-by-side in remappings + stats UI. The query-time rename remap uses lower(col) = ANY(pre-lowered arr), so the apply path IS case-insensitive — but somewhere upstream the LIST/GROUP query is case-sensitive, producing duplicate rows before the remap runs.

Repro: pick an axis (language/project/editor). Ingest heartbeats with mixed casing for the same underlying value. Open the axis's list view or the remappings suggestion list. Should collapse to one row per lowercased value; currently shows N rows.

Suspects to investigate: the GROUP BY in internal/db/stats.go (does it group by col or lower(col)?), the projects list handler, the remappings-suggestion query in internal/db/curation.go (what does 'suggest a rename' use as its distinct set?), the frontend heartbeat-axis dedup if any.

Fix strategy: pick ONE canonical case — probably keep raw casing in heartbeats table (existing rows shouldn't rewrite unless the apply-mapping feature runs) but change every LIST/GROUP path to group case-insensitively (lower(col) in GROUP BY + SELECT MIN(col) or MAX(col) or an aggregated-cardinality-highest label to pick a display representative). Consistent with query-time remap semantics.
notes:
Investigation

Root cause (multi-day case-variant duplicates): the case-fold wrap pattern in
internal/db/{bigbets.go,remap.go,project_extras.go} used `MODE() WITHIN GROUP
(ORDER BY expr)` PER (day, lower(col)) group. When day1 has 3× "Writing Docs"
+ 1× "writing docs" and day2 has 3× "writing docs" + 1× "Writing Docs", each
day's MODE picks a different display casing. The DB rows return with
different `Category` strings; downstream stats/segmentAligned groups by raw
name → two ResourceStats rows → dashboard shows two rows (the user-reported
"Writing Docs 1h5m" / "writing docs 22m").

Affected paths (before the fix):
  1. internal/db/bigbets.go:35 GetCategoryDaily — category axis → Category
     breakdown widget (the exact user report), CategoryStreamgraph.
  2. internal/db/bigbets.go:134 GetMomentum — project axis (per week) → the
     Momentum panel; different weeks could pick different project casings.
  3. internal/db/remap.go:257 regroupStatRows — project/language/editor/branch
     /platform/machine/entity for GetUserActivity + GetUserActivityRollup →
     Overview projects/languages/editors/platforms/machines segments (Big
     Bets, top-N charts, everywhere segment()/segmentStat() consumes).
  4. internal/db/remap.go:297 regroupProjectStatRows — language/entity for
     GetProjectStats → project page language/file breakdowns.
  5. internal/db/project_extras.go:85 branch case-fold in GetProjectExtras →
     project page branch breakdown.

Not touched (no per-day/per-week grouping so MODE tie-break stays global):
  - internal/db/leaderboards.go:79 (group is (project,language,sender), MODE
    is global per sender; no cross-day inconsistency)
  - internal/db/active_files.go:54 (group is lower(entity); global)
  - internal/db/entities.go:57 ListEntitiesByType (group is lower(entity); global)

Fix (SQL-side, Option A from the brief): replaced the per-group MODE picker
with a two-CTE pattern (helper `canonicalPickCTE` in remap.go). Step 1 groups
by (day, <raw_val>, lower(<expr>)) preserving the raw variant. Step 2 per
lower-key picks the display representative from the sum of totals across all
days (highest-total wins; alphabetical ASC tie-break). Step 3 joins on
lc = lower(<expr>) and regroups (day, canonical) → one canonical casing per
lower-key across the entire time range.

Rename remap runs BEFORE the pick (unchanged pattern) so `rs.remapExpr` still
resolves to the display value first, and case-folding kicks in on the
post-remap value.

Regression coverage: added TestCaseFoldMultiDayCanonicalPick in
internal/db/case_fold_test.go with two sub-tests (category + project) that
seed each variant on two days with flipped majorities and assert:
  - EXACTLY one display casing across both days;
  - summed total = sum(attributed seconds across the seed);
  - the picked variant is one of the raw input casings.

Verification:
  - full internal/db suite: PASS (all pre-existing TestCaseFold* cases pass +
    the new regression);
  - internal/handler, internal/stats, internal/widget, internal/importer: PASS;
  - `yarn typecheck && yarn test && yarn build`: green (no FE changes; FE
    now receives already-canonical data — no dedupe needed on that side).
close_reason: Fixed via 5ac02a0 (fix(stats): dedupe categories/languages/projects case-insensitively)

title: Apply mapping destructively from remappings page
description:
On the Remappings page, add an 'apply' icon next to the existing pen (edit) icon on each remap row. Clicking it destructively applies that mapping to the underlying data — rewriting the target column values on the affected rows — and then removes the mapping row itself (obviating it).

Currently a rename mapping (e.g., 'old-project-name' → 'new-project-name') persists forever as a translation layer. This is fine for a while, but eventually the user wants to collapse the history — permanently rewrite the historical rows so the mapping is no longer needed. This lets the mapping table stay lean and the raw data stay canonical.

Backend:
- POST /api/v1/users/current/remappings/:id/apply — runs UPDATE + DELETE in single transaction. Response: {rowsAffected, sqlRun}.
- GET /api/v1/users/current/remappings/:id/preview — returns affected-rows diff without touching data. Response: {sqlPlanned, affectedRows: [{id, before, after}], totalAffected}.
- Owner-scoped. Never let one user apply another user's mapping.
- Idempotent: if 0 rows match, still succeeds with rowsAffected: 0 and removes the mapping row.

Frontend:
- New icon (Zap/Check from lucide-react, terminal-hacker aesthetic).
- Click → preview → destructive-styled confirm modal.
- Modal shows exact SQL (monospace, code block) + affected-rows diff table (capped at 100 with 'and N more' footer).
- Confirm invalidates remappings + affected column query.
- Toast on success.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm modal must show: (1) exact SQL that will be executed in a code block (UPDATE + DELETE, monospace), (2) before/after diff table (heartbeat_id | col before → after), capped at 100 rows with overflow footer, (3) destructive-styled confirm button + cancel. SQL displayed in preview must be identical to SQL run by apply. Backend runs UPDATE + DELETE atomically in single transaction.
notes: UX rationale: keeps the mapping table lean and the raw data canonical. Rename mappings should not persist forever as a translation layer — user wants to collapse history. Destructive/irreversible action, so the confirm modal is the safety valve. SQL transparency is core to the terminal-hacker aesthetic.

title: (BUG) Alpha MEDIUM: DB backup silently drops encrypted_wakatime_key column on restore (data loss, not confidentiality)
description:

Impact:
  - POSITIVE for confidentiality: an exfiltrated backup ZIP does not carry any user-scoped Wakatime ciphertext (still-secure), and NEVER carries the BOOM_ENCRYPTION_KEY env var.
  - NEGATIVE for durability: an admin-initiated restore silently wipes every user's saved Wakatime key + status, because RestoreAll TRUNCATEs users first and then COPYs back only those three columns. The FE will report hasSavedKey=false after restore, with no warning.
  - No downgrade path leaves plaintext elsewhere; goose down for 00023 drops the column (fine).

Suggested fix:
  Either (a) explicitly add encrypted_wakatime_key + wakatime_key_status + wakatime_key_checked_at to dumpTables[users] so restore preserves them (blob is still safe since the caller controls the key material); OR (b) add a preflight warning to the restore UI "any saved Wakatime keys will be cleared" and document the intentional strip.

description:

title: No body-size limit on /api/v1/users/current/password (argon2 DoS amplifier)
description:
Charlie red-team run (2026-07-23).

Repro: `POST /api/v1/users/current/password` with `{"currentPassword":"A"*10_000_000,...}` (10 MB) returned 401 in ~58ms — server accepted, JSON-decoded, and ran argon2 verify against the attacker-controlled 10 MB input.

Impact: argon2id is m=64 MiB, p=4 per verify. Combined with (a) no body-size cap on this route and (b) no rate limit (see the sibling ticket), an attacker with a valid access token can pin ~256 MiB + arbitrary body allocation per request, easily saturating memory or CPU. Backup route uses `http.MaxBytesReader(c.Response(), c.Request().Body, restoreMaxBytes())`; the change-password handler should adopt the same pattern with a small (e.g., 4 KiB) cap.

Suggested fix: reject bodies > ~4 KiB before Bind. Cheap. Standalone. Compatible with the frontend.

Files:
- /Users/panda/catalyst-devspace/workspace/boomtime/internal/handler/password.go
close_reason: Closed

title: No rate limiting on /api/v1/users/current/password or /auth/login (argon2 brute force feasible)
description:
Charlie red-team run (2026-07-23).

Observed: 20 rapid POSTs of wrong `currentPassword` all returned 401 in ~22ms each, no throttling, no lockout. Same for 15 rapid `/auth/login` wrong-password attempts (all 403, no backoff). Argon2id params (t=1, m=64 MiB, p=4) hash in ~20ms on this box, so an attacker with a valid access token can brute-force `currentPassword` at ~50 attempts/s per connection.

Chain: if an attacker phishes/xss's an access token but not the password, they can (a) change the account password to lock the user out, and (b) even without an access token, spray `/auth/login` against known usernames unlimited.

Impact: HIGH — brute-force enables account takeover with just a captured session cookie/token; the change-password revocation guarantee becomes moot if the attacker just wins the password swap first.

Suggested fix: token-bucket per (owner, IP) on `/auth/login` and `/api/v1/users/current/password` (e.g., 5 wrong attempts / 15 min → 429). Log the events for audit.

title: Public dashboard cache leaks disabled-profile data for 5 min
description: The public endpoint GET /api/public/profile/:slug sets 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=300'. title: Detect + warn on wakatime.com API schema drift during import
description: We depend on the wakatime.com API shape for /import (heartbeats, user_agents, machine_names). If Wakatime changes their domain model/response schema, imports could silently drop or mangle fields. Add drift detection: during an import run, validate fetched payloads against the expected schema (e.g. strict-decode with unknown-field detection, required-field checks) and surface a WARNING banner on the Import page when drift is detected (unknown fields, missing expected fields, type changes), with details of what drifted. Import should still proceed where safe (warn, don't hard-fail, unless required fields are gone). Optionally persist drift findings on the import_jobs record so past runs show it.
design:
# Plan: Detect + warn on wakatime.com API schema drift during import (gaka-unq.1)

## Context (as-built)

- Fetch/decode: `internal/importer/importer.go` — `getJSON()` (json.Decoder straight into typed structs), called from `fetchLookups()` (user_agents, machine_names), `importDay()` (heartbeats), and `FetchAllTimeRange()`. Response structs: `importHeartbeat`/`heartbeatList`, `userAgent(List)`, `machineName(List)`, `allTimeResponse`.
- Job model: `internal/db/importjobs.go` (`db.Job`, `jobColumns`, `scanJob`); table from migrations `00005`/`00006` (`import_jobs`, `import_job_logs`). Job JSON is the shared FE contract and flows through REST (`internal/handler/import.go`: ImportJobs/ImportJob) AND the WS stream (Hub `Event{Type, Job, Log}` in `internal/importer/hub.go`, snapshot + progress/state events in `ImportJobWS`).
- FE: `web/src/pages/Import.tsx` + `web/src/components/import/{CurrentRunPanel,RunDetail,HistoryList,LogTerminal,ImportStateBadge}.tsx`, socket in `web/src/hooks/useImportJobSocket.ts`, types in `web/src/types/api.ts` (`ImportJob`).

## Approach: decode-into-map diff with per-endpoint schema specs (NOT DisallowUnknownFields)

Rationale:
- `json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields` aborts on the FIRST unknown field and turns decode into a hard error — the opposite of "warn, don't fail". It also gives no structured findings and cannot express a benign-field allowlist.
- Raw-message byte comparison against a golden payload is too brittle (ordering, values change every response).
- Chosen: for each response, unmarshal the envelope as `struct{ Data []json.RawMessage }` (plus keep the existing typed decode), then diff a SAMPLE of items against a `schemaSpec` per endpoint:
  - `known` field set: json tags of the typed struct (built once via reflection or hand-listed).
  - `baseline` allowlist: fields wakatime returns today that we deliberately don't map (heartbeats: `id`, `created_at`, `machine_name_id` is mapped, but e.g. `project_root_count`, etc. — capture a live response to seed this; see Open Questions). CRITICAL: without this, unknown-field detection fires on 100% of imports.
  - `required` set: heartbeats `entity`, `type`, `time`, `user_agent_id`; user_agents/machine_names `id`, `value`; envelope requires `data`.
  - Type check: for each present known field, `json.Unmarshal(fragment, new(FieldType))`; failure => `type_changed`.
- Sampling: check the first N=5 items of each day's heartbeat payload (schema is uniform per response); lookups are small — check all. Findings are deduped by `(endpoint, kind, field)` with a running count, so repeated drift across 1000 days produces one finding with count.

## Backend changes

1. New file `internal/importer/drift.go`
   - `type DriftFinding struct { Endpoint, Kind, Field, Detail, Severity string; FirstSeenDay string; Count int }` with JSON tags (camelCase to match FE contract). Kinds: `unknown_field`, `missing_required`, `type_changed`, `envelope_changed`. Severity: `warning` | `error` (error == required field gone / envelope broken).
   - `type driftCollector` (per-job, single goroutine — no locking): `check(endpoint, day string, raw []byte, spec schemaSpec)`, `findings() []DriftFinding`, `hasNew() bool` (to emit a log line only on first occurrence).
   - `schemaSpec` values for `heartbeats`, `user_agents`, `machine_names` (+ optionally `all_time_since_today`).
2. `internal/importer/importer.go`
   - Refactor `getJSON` into `getRawJSON(ctx, endpoint, auth, query) ([]byte, error)` (read body once); callers do `json.Unmarshal(body, &typed)` then `collector.check(...)`. Imports are network-bound; the second parse of a sampled prefix is negligible.
   - `run()`: create a `driftCollector`; thread it into `fetchLookups`/`importDay`. On each NEW finding, `log("warn", "schema drift: <endpoint>.<field> <kind> (<detail>)")` so it appears live in LogTerminal via the existing log event path.
   - Hard-fail semantics: `missing_required` on heartbeats => skip that day's insert (record error-severity finding + error log line, continue — matches existing per-day resilience). `missing_required` on user_agents/machine_names (`id`/`value`) or missing `data` envelope => fail the job (already the behavior when fetchLookups errors). Everything else warns and proceeds.
   - Before `FinishImportJob` (all terminal paths incl. cancelled), persist findings: `w.DB.SetJobDrift(ctx, jobID, findingsJSON)`. Also persist after fetchLookups drift so early-failing jobs carry findings.
   - Testability: make the base URL injectable (`Worker.BaseURL` defaulting to the `wakatimeAPI` const) so tests can point at httptest.
3. `internal/db` — persistence + exposure
   - Migration `internal/db/migrations/00014_import_jobs_drift.sql`: `ALTER TABLE import_jobs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS drift JSONB;` (nullable; Down drops it).
   - `internal/db/importjobs.go`: add `Drift json.RawMessage \`json:"drift"\`` to `db.Job` (RawMessage avoids db->importer import cycle; FE just sees the array). Add `drift` to `jobColumns` + `scanJob`. New method `SetJobDrift(ctx, id int, drift []byte) error`.
   - No handler changes needed for exposure: `db.Job` is already serialized in `/import/jobs`, `/import/jobs/:id`, and every WS snapshot/progress/state event — the `drift` field rides along automatically, including for historical runs.

## Frontend changes

1. `web/src/types/api.ts`: add `DriftFinding` interface (`endpoint`, `kind`, `field`, `detail`, `severity`, `firstSeenDay`, `count`) and `drift: DriftFinding[] | null` on `ImportJob`.
2. New `web/src/components/import/DriftBanner.tsx`: amber warning banner (red-tinted when any finding has `severity === "error"`), headline like "wakatime.com API drift detected — 3 finding(s); some fields may not have been imported", with a collapsible details table: endpoint / field / kind / detail / count / first seen. Follow the Card + lucide-icon style used by `CurrentRunPanel` (e.g. `TriangleAlert` icon).
3. Wire-up:
   - `web/src/components/import/CurrentRunPanel.tsx`: render `<DriftBanner findings={job.drift}/>` when non-empty — updates live because progress/state events carry the fresh Job.
   - `web/src/components/import/RunDetail.tsx`: same banner for historical runs.
   - `web/src/components/import/HistoryList.tsx` (optional polish): small warning icon on rows whose job has drift.
   - No changes needed in `useImportJobSocket.ts` (it stores whole Job objects).

## Drift vs hard-fail summary

- WARN (import proceeds): unknown field not in struct tags nor baseline allowlist; type change on an optional field (that field imports as nil for affected rows); new envelope keys.
- ERROR, skip day, job continues: required heartbeat field (`entity`/`type`/`time`/`user_agent_id`) missing or type-changed — inserting would mangle data.
- ERROR, fail job: `data` envelope missing/non-array, or user_agents/machine_names lacking `id`/`value` (every heartbeat's UA resolution would silently break).

## Testing strategy

- Pure unit tests in `internal/importer/drift_test.go` against fixture JSON strings: (a) golden current-schema payload incl. baseline unmapped fields => zero findings; (b) injected unknown field => one `unknown_field` warning; (c) removed `entity` => `missing_required` error; (d) `time` as string => `type_changed`; (e) dedupe/count across repeated items; (f) envelope without `data`.
- Integration test with `httptest.Server` + injectable BaseURL and the existing test DB harness (see `internal/db/importjobs_test.go`, `internal/testutil`): run a 1-day job against drifted fixtures, assert `import_jobs.drift` persisted, warn log line emitted, and job still `completed`; second test asserting required-lookup drift fails the job.
- FE: type-check only unless component tests exist; manual verification of banner via a seeded job row.

## Risks & gotchas

- False-positive noise is the #1 risk: wakatime ships benign additive fields regularly. Mitigations: baseline allowlist seeded from a real capture, dedupe-with-count, warning (not error) severity, and treating envelope extras leniently.
- Optional-field ABSENCE is not drift (JSON omits null fields routinely) — only required fields trigger `missing_required`.
- `dependencies` heartbeats field is `[]string`; a per-element type change won't fail whole-array decode cleanly — the type check should treat "known field fails typed decode" uniformly.
- WS payload growth: drift array is capped naturally by dedupe (bounded by field count); still cap findings at e.g. 50.
- Cancelled/failed paths must also persist drift (use the background-context pattern already in `finishCancelled`).

1. Baseline allowlist: can you capture one real response each for heartbeats/user_agents/machine_names from your wakatime account to seed the known-unmapped field lists? (Plan assumes at least `id`, `created_at` on heartbeats.)
2. Should a completed-with-drift job get a distinct visual state in HistoryList (badge variant) or is the banner in RunDetail enough?
3. Cover `all_time_since_today` (range discovery) too, or only the three import endpoints? Plan says optional/cheap to include.
4. Sample size per day (default 5 items) and findings cap (default 50) — any preference?
5. Any desire to suppress previously-acknowledged drift across future jobs (persistent "known drift" table), or is per-job reporting fine for v1? Plan assumes per-job.

design:
# Plan: Save/Load entire DB to/from a file (Heartbeats page)

## Approach

Add two authenticated endpoints — a streaming full-logical-dump download and an upload+replace restore — plus "Save DB" / "Load DB" controls on the Heartbeats page next to the derived-data panel.

**Export format decision: ZIP archive of per-table Postgres COPY text files + a JSON manifest, produced Go-natively via pgx.**

- File: `boomtime-backup-<ts>.zip` containing:
  - `manifest.json` — `{ app: "boomtime", formatVersion: 1, createdAt, gooseVersion, tables: [{name, columns, rows}] }`. `gooseVersion` = `SELECT max(version_id) FROM goose_db_version`; per-table `columns` recorded to enable future forward-compat.
  - `tables/<name>.copy` — output of `COPY <table> (col, ...) TO STDOUT` (Postgres text format: exact round-trip of NULLs, arrays, bytea, timestamps).
- Why Go-native COPY instead of pg_dump: no pg_dump binary in the alpine app image (ticket constraint), and pgx v5 (already at v5.10.0 in go.mod) exposes `conn.PgConn().CopyTo(ctx, w, sql)` / `CopyFrom(ctx, r, sql)` — raw COPY protocol streaming with no row-by-row marshalling.
- Why ZIP not tar.gz: `archive/tar` requires entry sizes up-front (would force spooling each table to temp files); `archive/zip`'s writer streams entries without knowing sizes (data descriptors), so the dump can stream straight to the HTTP response. On restore we spool the upload to a temp file anyway (needed for `zip.NewReader`'s ReaderAt, and it lets us fully validate the archive+manifest *before* truncating anything). Deflate gives good compression on COPY text.
- Snapshot consistency: run the whole dump on one acquired conn inside `BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` so all tables come from a single MVCC snapshot.

**Table inventory** (from migrations 00001–00013; `tags`/`project_tags` were dropped in 00013 and are excluded). FK-safe load order — this exact order is the dump order too:

1. `users` (PK username)
2. `projects` (FK → users)
3. `auth_tokens` (FK → users)
4. `refresh_tokens` (FK → users)
5. `heartbeats` (FK → users, → projects(owner,name))
6. `badges` (FK → users, → projects)
7. `hb_rollup_daily` (no FK)
8. `curation_rules` (no FK)
9. `spaces` (no FK enforced; owner column)
10. `space_rules` (FK → spaces, ON DELETE CASCADE)
11. `import_jobs` (no FK)
12. `import_job_logs` (FK → import_jobs)

`goose_db_version` is NOT restored (schema is owned by the running binary's migrations); its max version is recorded in the manifest and checked on restore.

## Backend changes

**New file `internal/db/dump.go`** (package db, alongside `derived.go`):
- `var dumpTables = []dumpTable{ {name, columns []string}, ... }` in the FK-safe order above. Explicit column lists on both COPY directions guard against column-order drift.
- `func (d *DB) DumpAll(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer) error` — acquire conn from `d.Pool`, open repeatable-read read-only tx, write `manifest.json` then each `tables/<n>.copy` into a `zip.Writer` via `PgConn().CopyTo(ctx, zw, "COPY <t> (cols) TO STDOUT")`. Row counts for the manifest come from `CopyTo`'s CommandTag (`RowsAffected()`); since zip entries stream, write the manifest LAST (or as the final entry `manifest.json`) so counts are known — reader locates it by name, order in archive is irrelevant.
- `func (d *DB) RestoreAll(ctx context.Context, zr *zip.Reader) (RestoreSummary, error)` — single tx on one acquired conn:
  1. Validate manifest (app id, formatVersion == 1, gooseVersion == current DB's max version_id — mismatch is a 409-style error, nothing touched).
  2. `TRUNCATE users, projects, auth_tokens, refresh_tokens, heartbeats, badges, hb_rollup_daily, curation_rules, spaces, space_rules, import_jobs, import_job_logs RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE` (one statement).
  3. For each table in FK order: `PgConn().CopyFrom(ctx, entryReader, "COPY <t> (cols) FROM STDIN")`.
  4. Reset sequences for every serial PK (`heartbeats.id`, `curation_rules.id`, `spaces.id`, `space_rules.id`, `import_jobs.id`, `import_job_logs.id`): `SELECT setval(pg_get_serial_sequence('<t>','id'), coalesce(max(id),1), max(id) IS NOT NULL) FROM <t>`.
  5. Normalize interrupted job states (`UPDATE import_jobs SET state='failed' WHERE state IN ('queued','running')`) — mirrors `importer.Worker.RecoverInterrupted`.
  6. COMMIT.
- `RestoreSummary` struct: per-table row counts + gooseVersion, JSON-tagged like `DerivedStatus`.

**Derived resync after restore** (in handler, after commit): the dump already contains `gap_seconds` + `hb_rollup_daily`, but per ticket run a safety-net rebuild: `SELECT DISTINCT sender FROM heartbeats` → for each, existing `d.ResyncDerived(ctx, sender)` (`internal/db/derived.go:51`, which calls `RecomputeGaps` + `RefreshRollup` from epoch). Then `h.Cache.InvalidatePrefix("")` to drop ALL cached aggregates (every key starts with `owner|`, so empty prefix clears everything).

**New file `internal/handler/backup.go`** (mirrors `derived.go` style):
- `GET /api/v1/users/current/db/export` → `h.DBExport`: `resolveUser` auth; set `Content-Type: application/zip` + `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=boomtime-backup-<ts>.zip`; stream `h.DB.DumpAll(ctx, c.Response())`.
- `POST /api/v1/users/current/db/import?confirm=replace-all-data` → `h.DBImport`: `resolveUser` auth; require the literal `confirm` param server-side (400 without it — prevents accidental curl); reject 409 if an import job is running (check via Worker/import_jobs state); spool `c.Request().Body` to a temp file with `io.Copy` + `http.MaxBytesReader` size cap (env-tunable, e.g. `BOOM_RESTORE_MAX_BYTES`, default ~4GB); `zip.NewReader` + manifest validation; `h.DB.RestoreAll`; resync derived; invalidate cache; return `RestoreSummary` JSON. Guard with a package-level `sync.Mutex` (or atomic flag) on Handler so only one export/restore runs at a time.
- Content type: raw `application/zip` body (not multipart) — simplest streaming, one file, matches fetch upload.

**Route registration** in `internal/server/server.go` next to the derived routes (lines ~84–85):
```
e.GET("/api/v1/users/current/db/export", h.DBExport)
e.POST("/api/v1/users/current/db/import", h.DBImport)
```

## Frontend changes

- **`web/src/lib/api.ts`**: `exportDb(): Promise<Blob>` and `importDb(file: File): Promise<RestoreSummary>`. The shared `request()` JSON-parses, so both use direct `fetch` with `authStore.authHeader()` + `credentials: "include"`; export reads `res.blob()`, import POSTs the File as the raw body with `?confirm=replace-all-data`.
- **`web/src/types/api.ts`**: add `RestoreSummary` next to `DerivedStatus` (line 45).
- **New `web/src/components/heartbeats/BackupPanel.tsx`** rendered in `web/src/pages/Heartbeats.tsx` directly below `<DerivedStatusPanel />` (the derived-data panel, per ticket). Contents:
  - "Save DB" button: `useMutation(api.exportDb)` → `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` + programmatic `<a download>` click + revoke. Spinner while pending; sonner toast on error (matches `DerivedStatusPanel` patterns).
  - "Load DB" button (`variant="destructive"` outline): hidden `<input type="file" accept=".zip,application/zip">`; selecting a file opens the confirm dialog.
- **New `web/src/components/heartbeats/RestoreConfirmDialog.tsx`** using `@/components/ui/dialog` (pattern: `RenameGroupDialog.tsx`): shows file name + size, red warning copy ("This ERASES every table — heartbeats, projects, users, tokens, settings — and replaces them with the backup. You will likely be logged out."), a text input requiring the user to type `REPLACE` before the destructive submit enables, and a pending state during upload/restore.
  - On success: toast with restored row counts, `queryClient.clear()` (all data changed), then call `api.getCurrentUser()`; on 401/403 (the restored `auth_tokens`/`refresh_tokens` don't contain the current session) clear auth state and redirect to `/login` via `useAuth`.

## Security / guarding

- Both endpoints behind `resolveUser` token auth like every other handler; single-user self-host, but note the export is inherently whole-DB (contains ALL users' data + password hashes + auth/refresh tokens) — call this out in the modal and keep the filename obviously sensitive.
- Restore triple-guarded: (1) server-side `confirm=replace-all-data` param, (2) client typed-`REPLACE` modal, (3) single-flight mutex + running-import-job rejection.
- Full validation (zip integrity via central directory, manifest app/format/goose version) happens on the spooled temp file BEFORE the TRUNCATE — a corrupt/foreign file can never wipe data. Restore itself is one transaction: any COPY error rolls back to the pre-restore state.
- Upload size cap via `http.MaxBytesReader`; temp file created in `os.TempDir()` and removed via defer.

## Testing strategy

- **`internal/db/dump_test.go`** (uses `harness_test.go` fixtures + isolated test DB): seed users/projects/heartbeats/curation/spaces/tokens/import jobs → `DumpAll` to buffer → mutate+add rows → `RestoreAll` → assert exact row equality per table, sequence positions (insert a new heartbeat post-restore, no PK collision), `gap_seconds`/rollup intact, running jobs normalized to failed. Plus: manifest gooseVersion mismatch rejected with nothing truncated; corrupt zip rejected.
- **`internal/handler/backup_test.go`** (pattern: `curation_test.go` via testutil/dbtest): 400 without confirm param, 401/403 without token, happy-path round trip through HTTP, cache invalidated.
- **Frontend (vitest, patterns in `api.test.ts` / `SourceHealthPanel.test.tsx`)**: confirm button disabled until `REPLACE` typed; api functions hit right URLs with auth header; post-success logout path on 401.
- **Manual e2e** via docker-compose: dump ~440k-heartbeat DB, restore into a freshly-migrated empty DB, verify Overview/Heartbeats dashboards and login with backed-up credentials.

## Risks & gotchas

- **Session self-invalidation**: restore replaces `auth_tokens`/`refresh_tokens`; when loading another instance's backup the caller's token vanishes mid-session. Handled by post-restore auth re-check + redirect to login (see frontend). Don't try to re-insert the caller's token — its user may not exist in the backup.
- **Schema drift**: a dump from an older/newer binary has different columns. v1 requires exact gooseVersion match; manifest records columns so a later version can do tolerant column-intersection restores.
- **Memory**: dump streams end-to-end (COPY → zip → response). Browser-side `res.blob()` holds the file in RAM — fine at expected sizes (~440k heartbeats ≈ tens of MB deflated); if backups grow huge, switch Save DB to a native `<a href>` download using the existing `?token=` query-auth pattern (`resolveUserFromQueryToken`, handler.go:114).
- **TRUNCATE locks**: restore takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on all tables; concurrent dashboard queries will briefly block — acceptable for single-user, and the mutex prevents concurrent restores.
- **`heartbeats_sender_project_fkey`**: projects MUST load before heartbeats (order above); a dump is internally consistent so no orphan risk.
- **Serial sequences**: forgetting `setval` after COPY of explicit ids ⇒ duplicate-PK failures on the next ingest. Covered by step 4 + test.
- **fetch has no upload progress**; acceptable v1 (spinner). XHR-based progress is a possible follow-up.

## Open questions for DJ

1. Strict gooseVersion equality on restore, or accept older dumps (restore column-intersection then rely on migrations having already run)? Plan assumes strict-equal for v1.
2. Is forced re-login after restore acceptable UX? (Alternative is messy.)
3. ZIP chosen over tar.gz for Go streaming ergonomics — any preference for tar.gz for tooling reasons (e.g. inspecting with standard unix tools)?
4. Want a matching CLI subcommand (`boomtime dump` / `boomtime restore` in cmd/boomtime/main.go) reusing `DumpAll`/`RestoreAll` for cron/scripted backups? Cheap once the db layer exists.
5. Cap for upload size — is a 4GB default sensible for your data volumes?
6. Should `badges` (has data? feature looks dormant) and `import_job_logs` be included? Plan includes both for true full-fidelity.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /Users/hdaniels/catalyst-devspace/repos/gakatime/internal/db/dump.go (new; model on internal/db/derived.go + sessions.go RecomputeGaps/RefreshRollup)
- /Users/hdaniels/catalyst-devspace/repos/gakatime/internal/handler/backup.go (new; model on internal/handler/derived.go)
- /Users/hdaniels/catalyst-devspace/repos/gakatime/internal/server/server.go (route registration, ~line 84)
- /Users/hdaniels/catalyst-devspace/repos/gakatime/web/src/components/heartbeats/BackupPanel.tsx (new; model on DerivedStatusPanel.tsx; mount in web/src/pages/Heartbeats.tsx)
- /Users/hdaniels/catalyst-devspace/repos/gakatime/web/src/lib/api.ts (exportDb/importDb + types in web/src/types/api.ts)
close_reason: Implemented: Go-native COPY-based zip dump (GET /db/export) + validated transactional restore (POST /db/import?confirm=replace-all-data) with FK-ordered truncate+load, sequence repositioning, job normalization, per-sender derived resync, full cache invalidation; Heartbeats-page BackupPanel + typed-REPLACE RestoreConfirmDialog with post-restore session check. Plan defaults taken on open questions: strict gooseVersion equality, forced re-login on foreign backups, ZIP format, 4GiB default cap (BOOM_RESTORE_MAX_BYTES), badges+import_job_logs included, no CLI subcommand (cheap follow-up). Destructive tests run on dedicated <testdb>_dump/_backup databases to survive parallel test packages.

design:
# gaka-7m4 — "Other" bucket breakdown tooltips: implementation plan

Scope: ONLY the mechanism for showing what's inside an "Other (N more)" bucket on hover. Shared tooltip styling/richness is owned by sibling gaka-9pt; this plan adds the minimal data plumbing + a small breakdown-HTML helper that gaka-9pt can later restyle.

## 1. Audit — where "Other" comes from and which charts show it

Collapsing happens ONLY in the backend, in `capWithOther()` at `/Users/hdaniels/catalyst-devspace/repos/gakatime/internal/stats/stats.go` (~line 395, `resourceTopN = 12`). It keeps top-12 `model.ResourceStats` and synthesizes one `Other (N more)` entry with summed `TotalSeconds/TotalPct/TotalDaily/PctDaily` — the tail members are DROPPED, so the FE cannot recover them today. Call sites:
- Stats payload (`/api/v1/users/current/stats`): projects, editors, languages, platforms, machines, categories (stats.go ~329-334)
- Project statistics: languages (~555, reused for `LanguagesDaily` via `languagesDaily()` ~595), files (~574), branches (~639)
- Momentum endpoint (`internal/stats/bigbets.go`) does NOT create an Other bucket (top-N only) — despite the ticket text, MomentumGrid is NOT affected.

Charts that RENDER an Other segment (affected — need the breakdown tooltip):
1. `web/src/components/charts/PieChart.tsx` — renders every item incl. Other. Used by Overview "Project breakdown" (`stats.projects`) and Projects "Language breakdown" (`stats.languages`).
2. `web/src/components/charts/ColumnChart.tsx` (stacked mode) — Overview "Total activity" stacked by category (incl. Other, built in `OverviewDashboard.tsx` `categoryColumnSeries`), and Projects "Total activity" stacked by language (built from `languagesDaily` in `web/src/pages/Projects.tsx` `languageColumnSeries`, which includes the "Other (N more)" series).
3. `web/src/components/charts/HeatmapChart.tsx` — Overview "Activity per project" + "Activity per language"; explicitly keeps the Other row (isOther logic at ~line 31).
4. `web/src/viz/council/CategoryStreamgraph.tsx` — keeps the Other layer last (~line 38).

Charts that deliberately EXCLUDE Other (no change; document as audited):
- `web/src/viz/council/CategoryBreakdown.tsx` (filters it out entirely — see open question)
- `web/src/components/TopProjectsBar.tsx`, `web/src/viz/council/BranchActivity.tsx`, `web/src/components/charts/FileBarChart.tsx`, `web/src/lib/mostActive.ts` (StatCards)
- `web/src/viz/council/MomentumGrid.tsx` (payload has no Other)
- editors/platforms/machines lists are not consumed by any FE chart today.

## 2. Approach (recommended mechanism)

**Backend carries the collapsed members on the Other entry itself** (Option A). Rejected alternatives: a drill query (per-hover latency, new endpoint, cache keys — overkill for a tooltip) and FE retention (impossible — the FE never sees the tail).

- Extend `model.ResourceStats` (`/Users/hdaniels/catalyst-devspace/repos/gakatime/internal/model/model.go` ~line 81) with:
  `OtherMembers []OtherMember \`json:"otherMembers,omitempty"\`` and a new
  `OtherMember { Name string \`json:"name"\`; TotalSeconds int64 \`json:"totalSeconds"\`; TotalPct float64 \`json:"totalPct"\` }`.
  Only the synthesized Other entry populates it; `omitempty` keeps every existing payload byte-identical otherwise.
- In `capWithOther()`: the tail is already sorted desc (list is sorted before slicing); carry the top `otherMembersCap = 20` tail members (name/totalSeconds/totalPct only — NO per-day arrays, that's exactly what capping exists to avoid). The FE derives "…and K more" as `tailCount - members.length`, where tailCount parses from the existing `Other (N more)` name (or add an explicit `otherCount int` field — cleaner; see open questions).
- Range-total breakdown only: day-scoped tooltips (stacked columns, heatmap cells) show the member breakdown *over the whole range*, labeled as such. Carrying per-day tail matrices would reinflate the payload capping exists to bound.

## 3. Shared changes

Backend:
- `internal/model/model.go`: `OtherMember` type + `ResourceStats.OtherMembers` (+ optional `OtherCount`).
- `internal/stats/stats.go`: populate members in `capWithOther`. `languagesDaily()` stays as-is (`LanguageDaily` keeps only name+daily; the FE joins back to the capped `Languages` list by name for members).

Frontend shared:
- `web/src/types/api.ts`: mirror `otherMembers?: { name: string; totalSeconds: number; totalPct: number }[]` (+ `otherCount?`) on `ResourceStats` (~line 80s).
- New `web/src/viz/otherBreakdown.ts`:
  - `isOtherBucket(name)` — consolidate the 6+ duplicated `startsWith("Other (")` checks (HeatmapChart, CategoryStreamgraph, CategoryBreakdown, OverviewDashboard, TopProjectsBar, mostActive) OR reuse/re-export the existing one in `web/src/lib/mostActive.ts`.
  - `otherBreakdownHtml(r: { otherMembers?, totalSeconds, name })` → HTML string: one row per member (truncated name via `truncate` from `@/lib/utils`, `secondsToHms`, pct-of-Other), display-capped at ~8 rows + a final `+K more (Xh Ym)` line. Returns "" when no members. Keep markup/inline styles consistent with existing `web/src/viz/d3/tooltip.ts` tooltips so gaka-9pt can restyle in one place.
- `web/src/components/charts/types.ts`: `ColumnSeries` gains optional `otherMembers` (or simpler: `stats?: ResourceStats` back-reference).

## 4. Per-chart checklist

- **PieChart** (`web/src/components/charts/PieChart.tsx`): in the `mousemove` handler (~line 61) append `otherBreakdownHtml(d.data)` when present. Data already flows (items are ResourceStats).
- **ColumnChart stacked** (`web/src/components/charts/ColumnChart.tsx` ~line 147): append breakdown from `ser.otherMembers`; label it e.g. "Top in Other (range)". Callers must thread members:
  - `web/src/components/OverviewDashboard.tsx` `categoryColumnSeries` (~line 154): pass `otherMembers: c.otherMembers` through (note `bucketItems` spread already preserves extra fields).
  - `web/src/pages/Projects.tsx` `languageColumnSeries` (~line 122): join `languagesDaily` name → `stats.languages` entry to attach `otherMembers` to the Other series.
- **HeatmapChart** (`web/src/components/charts/HeatmapChart.tsx` mousemove ~line 137): rows are ResourceStats, so `otherBreakdownHtml(d.row)` when hovering the Other row.
- **CategoryStreamgraph** (`web/src/viz/council/CategoryStreamgraph.tsx` mousemove ~line 107): it already does `series.find(s => s.name === layer.key)`; append breakdown from that entry.
- **Audited, no change**: CategoryBreakdown, TopProjectsBar, BranchActivity, FileBarChart, MomentumGrid, Punchcard/Calendar/Sessions (no Other buckets).

## 5. Testing

- Go: extend `internal/stats/capwithother_test.go` — members populated only on the Other entry, sorted desc, capped at `otherMembersCap`, empty when list ≤ topN; `internal/stats/project_extras_test.go` branch/files cases assert members too. `go test ./internal/stats/...`.
- FE unit (vitest, patterns in `web/src/viz/bucket.test.ts` / `web/src/lib/mostActive.test.ts`): `otherBreakdown.test.ts` — html rows, display cap + "+K more" math, empty-string when absent; `isOtherBucket` cases incl. plain "Other" category vs "Other (N more)".
- Manual: seed >12 projects/languages/categories; hover Other in the 4 affected charts (Overview + Projects pages, light/dark); confirm non-Other tooltips unchanged; confirm payload size stays sane on all-time range with many files.

## 6. Risks & gotchas

- **"Other" the real category vs "Other (N more)" the aggregate**: a genuine "Other" category value exists (see `mostActive.ts`). Gate the breakdown on `otherMembers` presence, never on name matching.
- **HeatmapChart FE re-slices to topN=7** (~line 36): rows 8–12 are silently dropped and NOT folded into the Other row, so the Other row's breakdown will list only the backend tail (items 13+), not the dropped 8–12. Pre-existing inconsistency — call out in tooltip copy or fix separately (open question).
- **Day-scoped tooltips show range totals**: label clearly ("in range") so a per-day stacked segment tooltip doesn't imply per-day member values.
- **Payload growth**: files tails can be huge — the 20-member cap bounds it (~1–2 KB per capped list). `omitempty` keeps Wakatime-compatible consumers unaffected.
- **Tooltip `white-space: nowrap`** in `web/src/viz/d3/tooltip.ts` — multi-row breakdown needs block rows + truncated long names (file paths!) or the tip overflows; coordinate with gaka-9pt before changing shared tooltip CSS.
- OverviewDashboard's `bucketItems` uses object spread, so `otherMembers` survives bucketing automatically — but verify no other reshaping strips it (e.g. `categoryColumnSeries` maps to a new object; must copy explicitly).

## 7. Open questions for DJ

1. Explicit `otherCount` field vs parsing "Other (N more)" from the name (name parsing breaks if the label is ever localized/renamed)? Recommend the field.
2. Member caps: 20 carried / 8 displayed OK? Files tails especially can be hundreds.
3. Should `CategoryBreakdown` (currently hides Other entirely) start rendering an Other row with the breakdown, or stay as-is?
4. Fix the HeatmapChart topN=7 re-slice so dropped rows fold into Other (accurate breakdown), or accept "backend tail only"?
5. Percentages in the tooltip: % of Other, % of chart total, or both?
